# D2R VR Authentic Settings - English, the text built into the program (made by tools/lang_sync.py - do not edit by hand).
#
# TRANSLATING: copy this file to <code>.txt in this folder (de.txt, pl.txt, pt-BR.txt...: your language's code), change
# language.name below to your language's own name, and translate the text after each "=" - by hand, or give the file to an AI or a
# translator and ask it to keep every line's key. Keep as they are: the keys before the "=", every {name} in braces (the program puts
# a number or a name there; it may move anywhere in the sentence), ini names like [hud] bar_place or d2r_vr.ini, file names, units
# (cm, m/s, Hz, %), and \n (a new line). A line you leave out, or leave empty, stays English. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Save as UTF-8 (Notepad's default). Your language appears in Settings > Home > Language; the program opens again in it.
# The same English under several keys is listed once: its translation is used for all of them.

language.name = English

# ===== Tab: Home =====
tab.home = Home

# --- Start ---
group.start = Start
group.start.help = The big START button: it starts Diablo II under D2RLoader, the way the mod runs. With BodyWalk and FlatVR it also starts BodyWalk, and FlatVR when Game Link is up.
@run.d2r_launch.label = START
@run.d2r_launch.tip = Starts Diablo II under D2RLoader, the way the mod runs. In VR with native OpenXR and "Controls without BodyWalk" nothing else is started; with BodyWalk and FlatVR it also starts BodyWalk, and FlatVR when Game Link is up.

# --- How you play ---
group.how_you_play = How you play
group.how_you_play.help = Pick how you play: flat on the monitor with mouse and keyboard, or in VR in the headset. The Status column says what is still missing for the way you picked.
mode.platform.tip = Native OpenXR (the default 3D choice below) needs no BodyWalk with "Controls without BodyWalk"; the FlatVR choices need BodyWalk with Game Link and FlatVR - the Status column says what is missing.
mode.platform.choice0 = Flat: on the monitor, mouse and keyboard
mode.platform.choice1 = VR: in the headset

# --- In the headset ---
group.in_the_headset = In the headset
group.in_the_headset.help = How the game gets into your headset: the 3D choice (Native OpenXR is the default), the headset's refresh rate, the VR render size and your height. Frame generation is here too. Start with "3D in the headset".
@stereo3d.source.label = 3D in the headset
@stereo3d.source.tip = Native OpenXR (the default): the game is an OpenXR app and shows its own stereo pair in the headset, one pass two pictures - each eye's real view and the head's place in the room, paced by the headset, no FlatVR - from the game's first frame. First (F4) and third person (F2) in stereo, F1 and F3 in 3D too (Stereo tab, "F1 and F3 in real 3D"); menus and open panels as a flat picture where you look. FlatVR is stopped while the game holds the headset, so BodyWalk's own panels are not in it; buttons and gestures need BodyWalk's OpenXR layer and the profile's gesture source set to OpenXR (or "Controls without BodyWalk"). Switches while the game runs. FlatVR stereo: the game draws each frame once and the right eye is drawn again from the same work with its own camera - true 3D at nearly the mono frame rate; it needs a game restart to switch on the first time. FlatVR 3D depth: one picture, FlatVR makes the second eye from ReShade's depth (works with DLSS). The FlatVR choices set the Stereo tab's Real stereo and, while BodyWalk runs, FlatVR's 3D source (BodyWalk 1.76 or later). Native OpenXR - eyes by turns: the game draws one eye a frame, left and right in turn - about half the graphics card's work of the default; the other eye is made on the graphics card from pictures already drawn (the eye drawn this frame moved across with its depth, its own last picture under it), so both eyes show this frame's head, and monsters where they are now. Each eye's own pixels are new at half the rate. The idea is bearstonem/d2r-pcvr's.
@stereo3d.source.choice0 = Native OpenXR (default)
@stereo3d.source.choice1 = FlatVR stereo
@stereo3d.source.choice2 = FlatVR 3D depth
@stereo3d.source.choice3 = Native OpenXR - eyes by turns
stereo.headset_rate.label = Headset refresh rate
stereo.headset_rate.tip = Sets the game's frame cap (in its own options, Settings.json) - the line under it says what is written and why: the rate itself for one picture a frame (mono, the 3D from the depth) and for both eyes from one game frame (one pass, two pictures: FlatVR stereo); twice the rate for eyes by turns (one eye a game frame, each eye at the rate); none for native OpenXR (the headset paces the game itself). More pictures than the headset shows make the frame shake. The game reads it when it starts: set it with the game closed (it writes its own options on exit), or restart the game after. VR only: in flat mode (How you play) the game runs at the frame cap you set in its own options - yours is kept before the rate writes its own, and comes back when you switch to Flat or start the game in flat mode.
@render.vr_px.label = Resolution (VR render size)
@render.vr_headset.label = Use the headset's recommended size
openxr.frame_generation.label = Frame generation (experimental; restart the game)
openxr.frame_generation.tip = Native OpenXR with both eyes from one game frame: OFXR Bridge (by tig3rmast3r, an OpenXR layer) makes every other headset frame from the two the game drew, by optical flow - the game draws half the frames, so it needs about half the graphics card's and the processor's work a second. Experimental: moving edges, the hands and the dark can smear or shimmer; it may fail to start (the game then runs without it, the log says why). It works only with "3D in the headset: Native OpenXR" - with the eyes by turns it stands aside (each eye would get a quarter of its frames real). FidelityFX works on any graphics card; NVIDIA's needs an RTX or a GTX 1660 (not a GTX 10 or 1650). It is loaded for this game only - nothing for other games, no tray program, no registry. Needs a game restart: switched on, it starts with the next game start; switched off it stands aside until the next game start. The backend and NVIDIA's options change while the game runs. Under Virtual Desktop set its SSW to Disabled: with both, the game draws only a quarter of the frames. While it runs, "Each eye exactly as the headset gives it" (Stereo) is set aside: the two together went black in the headset. Needs the bridge installed (the button below) and the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime (x64). The idea of using it here is bearstonem/d2r-pcvr's.
openxr.frame_generation.choice0 = Off
openxr.frame_generation.choice1 = FidelityFX (any graphics card)
openxr.frame_generation.choice2 = NVIDIA optical flow (RTX, GTX 1660 family)
openxr.frame_generation_preset.label = Frame generation: NVIDIA quality
openxr.frame_generation_preset.tip = NVIDIA's optical flow: how carefully it follows the motion. Slow is best and costs most; Medium is the bridge's suggested start. Live.
openxr.frame_generation_preset.choice0 = Slow (best)
openxr.frame_generation_preset.choice1 = Medium
openxr.frame_generation_preset.choice2 = Fast
openxr.frame_generation_scale.label = Frame generation: NVIDIA flow resolution
openxr.frame_generation_scale.tip = NVIDIA's optical flow on a smaller picture: 50% is the bridge's suggested start; 100% is rarely worth its cost. Live.
@run.framegen_get.label = Download and install OFXR Bridge 0.2.1 (frame generation)
@run.framegen_get.tip = Downloads OFXR Bridge 0.2.1 (V116) from its GitHub releases (github.com/tig3rmast3r/OFXR-Bridge, LGPL-3.0-or-later), checks its SHA-256 and puts the layer with its licences into d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs\ofxr of the mod - only for this game; nothing is registered for other games. About 0.6 MB.
openxr.block_listed_layers.label = Turn off OpenXR layers known to break the picture
openxr.block_listed_layers.tip = Native OpenXR: some programs put an OpenXR layer into every VR app on the PC (overlays like XSOverlay or fpsVR, OpenKneeboard, OpenXR Toolkit, Quad-Views-Foveated...). They are left as they are - except the few known to distort this game's picture (cross-eyed, stretched) while it draws each eye its own way: Quad-Views-Foveated for now, the list [openxr] blocked_layers in d2r_vr.ini (names comma-separated, yours to edit). On (the default): a listed layer is switched off for this game only, through the switch the layer names for it - nothing is written to the registry, other games keep it. With "Each eye exactly as the headset gives it" (Stereo) the game draws as other games do and nothing is switched off. Off: every layer loads. The line under it names the layers found. Taken when the headset session starts.
render.vr_resolution_ui.label = Menus and the mouse follow the VR render size
render.vr_resolution_ui.tip = With a VR render size apart from the window, the game still sized its interface and limited its mouse to the WINDOW: on a window wider than the picture the menus lost their right edge, and on a window lower than the picture the mouse - the laser - could not reach the bottom (the main menu's Play and Create Character buttons). On: the game's interface is laid out over the whole picture (its toolbar at the picture's bottom, as with a window of the picture's shape) and the mouse reaches all of it. Live. Off: the window's size, as before. (Found by bearstonem/d2r-pcvr.)
render.menu_wide.label = Main menu at 16:9
render.menu_wide.tip = Native OpenXR without ReShade ("No ReShade"; with ReShade it does nothing): the game lays its menus out for the shape of its picture, and a square picture (the square window, a square or the headset's render size) squeezed the main menu - its side panels over the hero, its bottom buttons cut off. On: while the game shows its own menus (the main menu, the character list, Create New) its picture is 16:9, as wide as the render size, and the panel in the headset has that shape. 3 s after the menu comes up the game takes the new size (a short rebuild of the picture); in a game the picture is the size picked again once the hero has stood in the world 3 s, as the render size always was. The monitor shows the menu stretched to the window. Live. Off: the menus in the picture's own shape, as before. (The 16:9 menus are bearstonem/d2r-pcvr's idea.)
@bodywalk.userHeight.label = My height, m
@bodywalk.userHeight.tip = Your height: the world is scaled to it (Stereo > Scale and depth > Life-size world). The same number as BodyWalk's Mapping > Avatar > Body Height, changed in both places; with BodyWalk not running it is kept here. Measure it with the T-pose on the Body tab if you want it exact.
@status.native_xr.label = Native OpenXR (the first 3D choice above) needs a BodyWalk that takes the game's headset (1.78 or later) or "Controls without BodyWalk"

# --- View (F1 - F3 in the game) ---
group.view_f1_f3_in_the_game = View (F1 - F3 in the game)
group.view_f1_f3_in_the_game.help = The view of flat mode: F1 the game's own camera, F2 third person, F3 first person with mouse look and W A S D. Switch in the game with F1, F2, F3 (F12 goes round); the game no longer gets these keys.
mode.flat_view.tip = Switch in the game with F1, F2, F3 (F12 goes round). The game does not get these keys: put its skills on others.
mode.flat_view.choice0 = F1  The game's own camera
mode.flat_view.choice1 = F2  Third person
mode.flat_view.choice2 = F3  First person: mouse look, W A S D

# --- View (F1 - F4 in the game) ---
group.view_f1_f4_in_the_game = View (F1 - F4 in the game)
group.view_f1_f4_in_the_game.help = The view in VR: F1 from above, F3 the game on your floor, F4 first person with the body following your controllers. Switch in the game with F1 - F4 (F12 goes round); the game no longer gets these keys.
mode.vr_mode.tip = Switch in the game with F1 - F4 (F12 goes round). F3: the game lies on the floor of your room. F4: arms on the controllers, the trunk held. The game does not get F1 - F4.
mode.vr_mode.choice0 = F1  From above
mode.vr_mode.choice2 = F3  The game on your floor: look down at it and walk round it (mixed reality)
mode.vr_mode.choice3 = F4  First person: the body follows yours (controllers)

# --- Draw distance ---
group.draw_distance = Draw distance
group.draw_distance.help = How far round you the world is drawn, in one slider: the room rings, the models' radius, the game's sky dome at its edge and the fog together, so the fog is full just before the drawn world ends. Nearer runs faster on a weak processor or graphics card. Each single value is on the Draw distance tab (and where it was: Performance, World, Sky); changing one of them shows Custom here.
@distance.stop.label = Draw distance (near - far)
@distance.stop.tip = Sets five things at once, near (1) to far (8): how many rings of rooms round you the game draws, how far out it draws monsters and objects (the models' radius: the edge of the drawn world), the game's sky dome at that edge, and where the fog starts and is full - outdoors full just before the dome (at 0.9 of the radius), in caves at the radius - so nothing pops out of the void. 3: 2 rings, models out to 200. Farther costs processor time (more rooms and models each frame); nearer is lighter. The line under it says what is set now. Custom: one of the single values was changed by hand - moving the slider sets them all again. Live.

# --- The game and ReShade ---
group.the_game_and_reshade = The game and ReShade
group.the_game_and_reshade.help = Checks and installs what the mod needs: D2RLoader (the mod runs only under it) and ReShade (the fog, the sky, the ceiling and FlatVR's depth need it). Buttons to share your own ReShade with the mod or put it aside, and to make the Arcane Sanctuary sky.
@status.d2rloader.label = D2RLoader
@run.d2rloader_get.label = Download and install D2RLoader 1.3.1
@run.d2rloader_get.tip = Downloads D2RLoader 1.3.1 from d2rloader.net, checks it against the SHA-256 the site publishes and unpacks it into the game's folder, beside D2R.exe. The mod runs only under D2RLoader.
@status.reshade.label = ReShade and the mod's effect
@run.reshade_get.label = Install ReShade
@run.reshade_get.tip = Downloads the current ReShade with add-on support from reshade.me, installs it for DirectX 10/11/12 and puts it in the mod as mods\D2R-VR\reshade\ReShade64.dll (renamed from dxgi.dll: the plain D2R.exe refuses a dxgi.dll), which the mod loads itself. Shown only while there is no ReShade (no dxgi.dll next to D2R.exe either). The fog, the sky, the ceiling and the depth for FlatVR need it.
@run.reshade_paths.label = Add D2R VR's folders to my ReShade (its search paths)
@run.reshade_paths.tip = The ReShade you have as dxgi.dll next to D2R.exe looks for effects and pictures in the game's folder, not in mods\D2R-VR\reshade where D2R VR's effect (D2R_DepthFog.fx) and pictures are. This adds D2R VR's two folders to EffectSearchPaths and TextureSearchPaths in your ReShade.ini - two list items at the end, nothing else of the file changes (a copy is kept as ReShade.ini.before_d2rvr; D2R VR's uninstaller takes them out again). D2R VR Setup does this by itself; press it if you installed ReShade after D2R VR. The game must be closed. Takes effect at the next start of the game.
@run.reshade_aside.label = Put my dxgi.dll aside (dxgi.dll.off) - D2R VR gets its own ReShade
@run.reshade_aside.tip = Your ReShade stays as it is while it is dxgi.dll; D2R VR uses it. Only press this if you want D2R VR to have a ReShade of its own (mods\D2R-VR\reshade) instead: dxgi.dll is renamed to dxgi.dll.off (nothing is deleted, nothing replaced), then Install ReShade is offered. The game started without D2RLoader has no ReShade then. "Bring my dxgi.dll back" undoes it. Takes effect at the next start of the game.
@run.reshade_back.label = Bring my dxgi.dll back (dxgi.dll.off / .bak)
@run.reshade_back.tip = Renames dxgi.dll.off (or a dxgi.dll.bak you made yourself) back to dxgi.dll - the ReShade you put aside. D2R VR then uses that one as it is. Leave it as it is if you want D2R VR's own ReShade (Install ReShade). Takes effect at the next start of the game.
@status.reshade_note.label = IMPORTANT
@status.arcane_sky.label = Arcane Sanctuary sky: not made yet
@status.knock_props.label = Knockable props: off ([weight] knock_props, Weapon Weight)
@status.kurast_boat.label = Kurast Docks canoe: not looked at yet
@run.arcane_make.label = Make the Arcane Sanctuary sky now
@run.arcane_make.tip = Reads the star layers and clouds out of your game's own files (read only) and makes the pictures the mod draws the Arcane Sanctuary's sky with (D2R_Arcane, in ReShade's reshade-shaders\Textures: mods\D2R-VR\reshade for the mod), and takes the game's flat star cards out of the level's files in mods\D2R-VR\D2R-VR.mpq (the game's own files stay as they are). This program does it by itself when it opens; press this after the game was updated or a picture was deleted. Nothing already right is written again. The game may be running: it finds the pictures within 2 seconds.

# --- Other mods ---
group.other_mods = Other mods
group.other_mods.help = Load the mods you build with D2RMM (or put in the game's mods folder) together with D2R VR. Ticked, their files are merged into D2R VR's mod at each START; D2R VR's own VR changes stay on top of yours.
mods.merge_data_mods.label = Load my other mods with D2R VR (D2RMM)
mods.merge_data_mods.tip = The game loads only one mod, and D2R VR is that mod, so the mods you build with D2RMM (mods\D2RMM) or put in the game's mods folder yourself were not loaded with it. On: at START (and the launcher's Play) their data files are copied into D2R VR's mod (mods\D2R-VR\D2R-VR.mpq) and loaded with it; when you build your mods again in D2RMM the next START takes the new files. Not merged: another VR mod (D2R-PCVR), a mod with D2RLoader plugins of its own, a packed .mpq. Two mods with the same file: D2RMM's is taken. D2R VR's own files keep their VR changes on top of yours. Your characters stay in D2R VR's save folder. Everything that was done is in d2r_vr_data_mods.txt (mods\D2R-VR\d2rloader\logs). Off: the other mods' files are taken out again at the next START, D2R VR alone as before.
@status.data_mods.label = Other mods: not looked at yet

group.d2r_vr.help = This program and the mod: the language of this program, the version, the update check, and Collect logs - one zip with what support needs to find a problem.
hud.headset_language.label = In the headset too
hud.headset_language.tip = The words the mod draws in the headset - the skill panel, the settings in the headset, the first-start guide, the calibration prompt, the map's buttons - in the language picked above. A text not translated yet stays English. Off: English, as before. The game's own texts are the game's language (its own settings).

@update.download.tip = Opens the download page in your browser. This program never downloads or runs anything itself.
@run.collect_logs.label = Collect logs for support

While the game runs it first records 10 s of how the frames are drawn - keep playing and turn your head. Nothing is sent anywhere: post the zip in our Discord (#diablo-2-vr).
@status.collect.label = Collect logs: a zip on your desktop to post in our Discord

@run.flatvr_stop.label = Stop FlatVR
@run.flatvr_stop.tip = Stops FlatVR in BodyWalk. The same as STOP FLATVR on BodyWalk's FlatVR tab.

# --- Monitor (screen recording) ---
group.monitor_screen_recording = Monitor (screen recording)
group.monitor_screen_recording.help = What the game's window on your monitor shows while you play in VR - for recording or streaming it with OBS: both eyes in turn, or one eye only, at its own proportions. The headset's picture does not change.
render.monitor_eye.label = Monitor shows (to record the screen)
render.monitor_eye.tip = What the game's window on the monitor shows while the headset has the stereo pair - for OBS or any screen capture of the game. The headset gets each eye as before; only the window changes. Both eyes in turn (as before): the window shows each picture as it is drawn - left, right, left - and a recording flickers between the eyes (doubled edges); with "Native OpenXR" (one pass, two pictures) it already showed the right eye alone. The left eye / The right eye: that eye only, steady, at every frame - after the headset took the other eye's picture, the window gets this one's instead (one extra copy on the graphics card a frame, a small fraction of a millisecond). With "Native OpenXR - eyes by turns" the frames that draw the other eye show this eye as the headset has it then: made on the graphics card for that frame (smooth), or, with the box below, its last picture the game drew. Menus and loading show the flat picture as before. Live. The idea is bearstonem/d2r-pcvr's.
render.monitor_eye.choice0 = Both eyes in turn (as before)
render.monitor_eye.choice1 = The left eye
render.monitor_eye.choice2 = The right eye
render.monitor_eye_fit.label = Monitor: the eye at its own proportions (cropped to the window)
render.monitor_eye_fit.tip = With a VR render size apart from the window (Resolution, In the headset: a square picture in a wide window) Windows stretches the picture over the window - the monitor showed it squashed. On: the middle of the eye's picture in the window's shape is drawn over the whole picture first, so the window shows it at its real proportions (the top and bottom, or the sides, cut off). Nothing changes when the window has the picture's shape. Live. Off: stretched as before.
render.monitor_eye_drawn_only.label = Monitor: eyes by turns - only pictures the game drew
render.monitor_eye_drawn_only.tip = "Native OpenXR - eyes by turns" only: the frames that draw the other eye show this eye's last picture the game drew - each picture twice, at half the rate, but never one made on the graphics card (made pictures can smear at the edges of moving things). Off (the default): the picture made for this eye that frame - every frame new, as the headset shows it. Live.

# ===== Tab: Performance =====
tab.performance = Performance

# --- Processor ---
group.processor = Processor
group.processor.help = For Ryzen processors with 3D V-Cache (X3D): the game runs on the cores with the big cache and its drawing thread gets a higher priority. On other processors nothing changes.
render.vcache.label = Game on the cores with the big cache (Ryzen X3D)
render.vcache.tip = On a Ryzen with 3D V-Cache on one of its two core groups (7900X3D, 7950X3D, 9900X3D, 9950X3D) the game's threads are asked to run on the cores with the big L3 cache, and its drawing thread gets a higher priority - D2R's frame is bound by that one thread. Other processors: nothing changes. The log says which cores were taken. Live.

# --- Quality ---
group.quality = Quality
group.quality.help = How much the game draws and how good it looks against how fast it runs. A preset (Potato to High) sets everything here at once: room rings, model radius, fog, sky, cave ceiling and its torch light. Room rings, models and the frame cap need a game restart.
@preset.preset.label = Quality preset
@preset.preset.tip = Sets the settings below at once. Light (a weak PC): no ReShade at all - the game in the headset with Native OpenXR, the eyes by turns (one eye drawn a frame, the other made from it with the depth, the cheaper way: no rims, no strip filling, no sharper read, its own picture not kept - Stereo tab), as Potato otherwise; the sky and the fog drawn by D2R VR itself ("Sky and fog without ReShade"), the menus as a flat picture. It ticks "No ReShade" below and sets the 3D in the headset to "Native OpenXR - eyes by turns"; restart the game. Potato: as Low, but no ceiling, the 3D made from ReShade's depth instead of real stereo (one frame a picture, not two) and the headset at 72 Hz, the game capped at it; the others 90 Hz. Low: 1 room ring, models out to 150, near fog (30 to 100; in caves 60 to 100), ceiling on with coarse relief (8 steps). Medium: 2 rings, 200, fog 30 to 200 (in caves 100 to 200), ceiling on. High: 3 rings, 400, fog 30 to 250, finer ceiling relief and torches lighting the ceiling (heavy on the CPU). Every preset also sets the 3D in the headset: FlatVR stereo (Low, Medium, High) or FlatVR 3D depth (Potato) - it switches Native OpenXR off (set it again on the Home page). With Native OpenXR on this shows Custom. Changing any of them by hand shows Custom.
@preset.preset.choice0 = Light: no ReShade (native, eyes by turns)
@preset.preset.choice1 = Potato
@preset.preset.choice2 = Low
@preset.preset.choice4 = High
@preset.preset.choice5 = Custom
render.no_reshade.label = No ReShade (Native OpenXR - eyes by turns only; restart the game)
render.no_reshade.tip = For a weak PC: the game runs without ReShade - D2R VR does not load ReShade64.dll at all and hooks the game's graphics itself. Only for "3D in the headset: Native OpenXR - eyes by turns" (Home): one eye drawn a frame, the other made on the graphics card with the game's depth. The sky, the fog and the cave ceiling come back drawn by D2R VR itself (the box below). Off with it: the overlays kept apart from the picture the second eye is made from (labels laid back, the wrist orbs - drawn into the picture), the lights' fix for the square window, and the menus as a panel (they show as the flat picture). On a GTX 1050 Ti the game went from about 44 to 53-60 frames a second without any effect. Read when the game starts: restart it after a change. With your own ReShade as dxgi.dll beside the game it does nothing (the game loads that one itself). Off (the default): ReShade as before.
render.native_effects.label = Sky and fog without ReShade (drawn by D2R VR itself; restart the game)
render.native_effects.tip = With "No ReShade": D2R VR draws its own effect itself - the sky outdoors, the distance fog, the cave ceiling and the rest of what ReShade drew in the picture (the switches on this tab and on Sky / Ceiling still decide which). Its shaders are built in the background when the game starts and at each new picture size - the first time a while (several seconds; the picture has no sky till then), then from a cache beside d2r_vr.ini at once. What it costs the graphics card is in the log every 10 s. Off: no effect at all - the lightest. Read when the game starts.
render.rings.label = Room rings around the hero
render.rings.tip = Extra room rings around the hero. With fog, 4-6 is enough.
render.model_radius.label = Model visibility radius
render.model_radius.tip = The game's own is 150.
@skyfog.way.label = Sky and fog drawn by
@skyfog.way.tip = Who draws the sky and the distance fog, both at once. The game (new): its own fog pass with our numbers and a sky dome of ours the game draws itself - no frame time of ours (VR F4; without ReShade for its fog's options below). Our effect (old): the fog shader's sky and fog (ReShade's, or D2R VR's own without ReShade). Writes [sky] game_sky and [fog] game_fog together. Live.
@skyfog.way.choice0 = The game draws them (new)
@skyfog.way.choice1 = Our effect (old)
fog.enabled.label = Distance fog
fog.enabled.tip = A distance fog. Who draws it: the selector above (our effect, or the game itself). With the sky on, it fades into the sky.
fog.light.label = Light fog (weak graphics cards)
fog.light.tip = Our effect's fog the short way: the depth read once a pixel, the fog by it, the sky still drawn in the void - no depth blur, no fog over glows and sparks against the sky, no cave ceiling. A fraction of the full fog's cost on the graphics card (the log's 10 s line says it). Off: the full fog, as before.
fog.start.label = Fog start
fog.start.tip = Where the fog begins. World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall).
fog.end.label = Full fog
fog.end.tip = Where the fog is complete. World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall). Near fog hides what a short render distance leaves out.
fog.caves_start.label = Fog start in caves
fog.caves_start.tip = Where the fog begins in caves, dungeons and crypts. World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall).
fog.caves_end.label = Full fog in caves
fog.caves_end.tip = Where the fog is complete in caves, dungeons and crypts. World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall).
sky.enabled.label = Sky outdoors
sky.enabled.tip = A painted sky over the black void outdoors. Who draws it: the selector above (our effect, or the game's dome).
@reshade.generic_depth.label = ReShade depth map (Generic Depth)
@reshade.generic_depth.tip = ReShade's Generic Depth add-on finds the game's depth buffer every frame. Off saves GPU time, but the fog, the sky, the ceiling and the 3D from the depth need it. Applies when the game is started again.
ceiling.enabled.label = Ceiling in caves (via ReShade)
ceiling.enabled.tip = A stone vault over the black void in dungeons, first person only.
ceiling.game_ceiling.label = Who draws the ceiling
ceiling.game_ceiling.tip = Our effect: the vault through the fog shader - ReShade's, or D2R VR's own without ReShade. The game: a slab of the game's own cave rock, made from your game's files, that the game draws and lights itself - its torches and your light on it, its fog over it, fire and spells in front of it - laid over you every frame, no frame time of ours (a test: VR F4 only). Each room the game's own stone matched to the picture chosen for it: rock in the caves, tall slabs in the crypt, smooth stone in the barracks, catacombs and cathedral, ornamented marble in the palace; a room with no picture matched its own floor's stone (the act 2 sewers, the corrupt harem, the palace cellar). The other ceiling settings below are our effect's; the tile size sets the rock's too. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling.choice0 = Our effect (ReShade / D2R VR's own)
ceiling.game_ceiling.choice1 = The game (lit rock)
ceiling.steps.label = Ceiling relief steps
ceiling.steps.tip = Steps of the ray through the rock: more = finer relief, a dearer frame.
ceiling.torches.label = Torches light the ceiling (CPU heavy!)
ceiling.torches.tip = WARNING: very heavy on the CPU. To find the torches the mod reads all of the game's memory every 1.5 s while a ceiling is drawn (about a third of a CPU core) - on a weaker PC the game and VR stutter. Fire seen in the picture (torches, braziers, fire spells) then lights the ceiling over it.
ceiling.fire_from_picture.label = Any fire lights the ceiling (ReShade, from the picture)
ceiling.fire_from_picture.tip = Fire found in the picture by ReShade lights the ceiling: torches, braziers, fire spells, burning monsters - any fire on the screen, as the first ceilings did. No reading of the game's memory, so light on the CPU (a little GPU). A fire out of sight is remembered for 8 s; one that goes out in plain view goes dark at once. In place of the torches above.
@game.Framerate Cap.label = Game frame cap, fps (0 = none)
@game.Framerate Cap.tip = The game's own frame cap (its Settings.json). Set from the headset's rate and the 3D choice (both on the Home page); can be changed by hand.
@status.perf_restart.label = Need to restart the game: the render distance (room rings, models), the headset rate and the frame cap take effect when the game starts again.

# ===== Tab: Draw distance =====

# --- Draw distance ---
group.draw_distance.help#2 = How far round you the world is drawn, in one slider: the room rings, the models' radius, the game's sky dome at its edge and the fog together, so the fog is full just before the drawn world ends. Nearer runs faster on a weak processor or graphics card. The single values are below (and where they were: Performance, World, Sky); changing one of them shows Custom on the slider.

# --- What the slider sets ---
group.what_the_slider_sets = What the slider sets
group.what_the_slider_sets.help = Each value the Draw distance slider writes, to set by hand. The fog's are greyed while the distance fog is off, the sky dome's while the game does not draw the sky (Sky tab: "Sky and fog drawn by"), the cave dome's while it is off.
render.big_radius.label = Big objects: trees, houses, walls farther (0 = off)
render.big_radius.tip = Trees, houses and walls stay drawn farther than the model visibility radius - the bigger, the farther (30 times its height or half its width), out to this many units (300 - 1000; 100 and 200 count as 300). Stones, grass and monsters keep the model visibility radius. Needs room rings 3 or more (past the rooms the game builds there is nothing to draw), and the full fog and the sky dome past it to be seen. Costs frames in forests and towns. From D2R VR Unleashed (bearstonem). Visual only. Live. 0 = off, as before.
sky.game_sky_radius.label = The game's sky: dome radius, units
sky.game_sky_radius.tip = How far round you the game's sky dome is laid, in the game's units (live). 200: a near horizon - the dome cuts the far world off in a clean circle, the game's fog over it. Farther the sky comes out of the fog. The log says the radius in use with each change.
fog.enabled.tip#2 = A distance fog. Who draws it: the Sky tab's selector (our effect, or the game itself). With the sky on, it fades into the sky.
sky.game_dome_caves.label = A black dome round you in caves
sky.game_dome_caves.tip = Underground the game draws a black dome round your head at the models' visibility radius: no void past a ceiling's rim, the game's fog fades into black walls - no glow behind the fires. The sky dome's own files (made by this program at its start). VR F4. Live.
sky.game_dome_caves_size.label = The cave dome: radius x model visibility radius
sky.game_dome_caves_size.tip = 1: the dome at the model visibility radius ([render] model_radius); 0.5: half of it (the radius as a diameter). Live.

table.bounds.label = Diorama size (1 = as much as the game shows)

table.background.label = Background round the game
table.background.tip = What the void round the game is filled with: Virtual Desktop's passthrough cuts it by colour and shows your room there - set its chroma key to the same colour. Black by default; a pure colour (green #00FF00, blue #0000FF, magenta #FF00FF) if black cuts holes in the game. Empty (x) = black.
table.background.empty = black
table.floor.label = Lift the game off black
table.floor.tip = With a black background: the game's own dark parts are lifted this far off black, so the chroma key does not cut them too. Raise it if shadows show the room, lower it if the picture looks washed out.

arms.hide_head.label = Hide the hero's head and neck
arms.hide_head.tip = Shrinks the hero's head and neck away, for a camera right at the eyes: looking down shows the chest. Keep "Camera ahead / behind" at 0 then - moved ahead, the camera leaves the hands out of reach.
arms.head_shadow.label = The hidden head still casts its shadow
arms.head_shadow.tip = F4: the head (and the helm) is hidden from your eyes as before, but the hero's shadow on the ground keeps it - the game's shadows are drawn from his whole pose, only what your eyes see has the head shrunk away. Visual only. Off: the head is shrunk in the pose itself and his shadow has no head, as before. Live.
arms.scale.label = Arm length (scale)
arms.scale.tip = Arm reach on top of the hero-to-your-height ratio.
arms.full_reach.label = Hands always reach the controllers
arms.full_reach.tip = F4: a hand farther from the hero's shoulder than his arm is long - a slash across the body, the second hand on a two-handed hilt at the far hip, a hero with wider shoulders than yours - is drawn on its controller all the same: the shoulder comes along first (his collarbone turned toward the hand, at most 20 degrees, as a real shoulder reaches across), then the arm lengthens for what is still missing (at most 35 %: past that the controller jumped). The weapon in the hand goes with it, and a two-handed weapon's second hand stays on its place on the shaft. Drawn bones only. Off: the arm stops at its length and the hand, with the weapon, falls short of the controller, as before. Live.
arms.up.label = Hands up (+) / down (-), cm
arms.forward.label = Hands forward (+) / back (-), cm
arms.side.label = Hands right (+) / left (-), cm
arms.follow_camera.label = Hands follow the camera shift, %
arms.follow_camera.tip = With "Camera ahead / behind" off 0: at 100% the hands hang off the camera and match your real ones, but a camera moved ahead puts them out of the arms' reach. At 0% they hang off the hero's eyes: the body stays put, the hands always reach, a little nearer than your real ones.

# --- Measured height and arm span (T-pose) ---
group.measured_height_and_arm_span_t_pose = Measured height and arm span (T-pose)
group.measured_height_and_arm_span_t_pose.help = Fit the hero to you: measure your height and arm span with a T-pose in the headset (native OpenXR, F4), or set the arm span by hand. Pick Standing or Seated, and tick "Use the measured height and arm span" to use it.
calibration.seated.tip = Standing: in native OpenXR F4 with a measurement in use, the hero's eyes are at your measured eye height over the floor, whatever height a recenter was taken at; a recenter sets straight ahead and where you stand. Seated: the hero's eyes are where your head is when you recenter (F11, the headset's own recenter, the headset settings' Recentre view) - sit as you play and recenter; the crouch counts from there. The measurement then reads only your arm span (no floor needed) and keeps a stored eye height for the world's scale (none stored: "My height" / BodyWalk's Body Height). Also on the headset settings' Body page. Live.
calibration.seated.choice0 = Standing
calibration.seated.choice1 = Seated
calibration.use.label = Use the measured height and arm span

Unticked: those, exactly as before. A good measurement ticks it. F4 only: the other views keep the old numbers. Native OpenXR: standing upright you also look from the hero's eyes, whatever height the last recenter was taken at.
calibration.measure.label = Measure my height and arm span...
calibration.measure.tip = Native OpenXR only, with the game running and the headset on: a panel in front of you says what to do. Stand upright, look straight ahead, stretch both arms out sideways at shoulder height, let go of both triggers, then squeeze both and hold still for a second. Needs the room's floor set up in your headset. The game goes on behind the panel: measure somewhere safe. F4 only. Seated ("How you play"): sit upright - only the arm span is measured, no floor needed.
calibration.arm_span_m.label = Arm span by hand, m (grip to grip)
calibration.arm_span_m.tip = The span the hero's arms are fitted to: move it to make his arms longer or shorter while you watch them (F4, live). It is the measured arm span - a new measurement sets it again, and this slider moves with it. "auto": nothing stored, the span for your height is used ("Not measured: arms of a person's length"). Moving it ticks "Use the measured height and arm span"; with no measured eye height the world's scale stays "My height" / BodyWalk's Body Height. Also in the headset: the Body page's Arm span, under Calibrate body.
@run.calibration_forget.label = Forget the measurement
@run.calibration_forget.tip = Clears the stored measurement: the height from BodyWalk / "My height" and "Arm length (scale)" apply again.
calibration.strict_tpose.label = Measure only with the arms straight out to the sides
calibration.strict_tpose.tip = The T-pose is taken only with the arms straight out sideways: no hand more than 6 cm ahead of your eyes, and a span under 0.88 of your eye height is read as arms not stretched - the panel says "Arms straight out to the sides ..." and waits. Arms swung forward or elbows a little bent read a span 10 - 15 cm short, and the hero's arms came out short of the controllers. Off: the hands may be up to 22 cm ahead, as before.
calibration.default_span.label = Not measured: arms of a person's length for your height
calibration.default_span.tip = F4, with no measurement in use (none stored, or "Use the measured height and arm span" unticked): the hero's arms are fitted to the span a person of your eye height has (0.95 of it, grip to grip - what measurements of stretched-out arms give), the way a measurement fits them, and "Arm length (scale)" counts as 1 (the hands 1:1 with the controllers). Off: the hero's own arm length times "Arm length (scale)", as before. Live.

# --- First-start guide (in the headset) ---

# --- Body ---
group.body.help = How the hero's body moves under you in F4: no game animation above the pelvis, legs kept under the body, staying under the camera in a leap, crouching when you crouch, and turning to where you look.

body.under_camera.label = Body stays under the camera in a leap (F4)
body.under_camera.tip = A Leap or a Leap Attack lifts the hero's model several metres up on its arc, and played with a pad the game's camera trails him when he moves fast (a leap, a knockback): his body flew up and out from under your eyes. On: the drawn body is kept where the camera stands: the camera stays on the ground and the body with it (or, with the box below, the camera goes up with the leap's arc). Only the drawn body and the camera: where he stands, his hit box, his path and the leap itself stay the game's. VR first person (F4) only. Off = as before. Live.
body.leap_camera_up.label = Camera rises with the leap's arc

body.crouch.label = Hero crouches when you crouch (F4)

Only the drawn body: where he stands, his hit box and his walking stay the game's. Needs a camera that follows your head's height (native OpenXR, or FlatVR with the head's position). VR first person (F4) only. Unticked: exactly as before. Idea from bearstonem/d2r-pcvr.
body.crouch_cm.label = Crouch: head lower than this, cm

The standing eye height is your measured one over the floor ("Use the measured height and arm span", native OpenXR); without it, or seated ("How you play"), your head's height at the last recenter: recenter as you play (standing upright, or sitting).
body.turn.label = Hero turns to where you look (F4)
body.turn.tip = In the other first-person views the whole hero always turns with you.
body.turn.choice0 = No (the game's facing)
body.turn.choice1 = Above the pelvis
body.turn.choice2 = Whole body
body.turn_third.label = From behind too (the right stick turns him)
body.turn_third.tip = In the view from behind the whole hero faces where the camera looks, so the right stick turns him. Off: the right stick only swings the camera round him, and he faces where he last walked.
body.gait_legs_third.label = From behind: his legs step the way he moves
body.gait_legs_third.tip = In the view from behind (flat or VR), while he faces the camera, his legs step along where he really goes - backward steps when you walk back, side steps when you strafe - instead of the game's run along his path (which runs the wrong way while he faces the camera). Feet planted while they bear him; standing, he stands. Needs the gait library d2r_vr_gait.dll. The drawn legs only. Live.
body.gait_cone_deg.label = Steps: the game's own walk within +- this of where he faces, ° (half the cone)
body.gait_cone_deg.tip = Half of the cone about the way the hero faces (45 = 90 of the 360: 45 to one side and 45 to the other). Going within it, the game's own walk and run show - they look best going forward; outside it - sideways past it, backward - the gait's steps. Crossfaded over a moment, with a few degrees of hysteresis so it never flickers. For your own hero (the two boxes here) and the other players' heroes alike. Live.
body.gait_legs_f4.label = F4: your legs step the way you move
body.gait_legs_f4.tip = Your own first-person body: the whole body turns with your look and the legs step along where you really go - back, sideways, forward - instead of the game's run along the path. Needs the gait library d2r_vr_gait.dll. The drawn legs only. Live. F4 only.
body.walk_back.label = Walking backwards, the legs step backwards
body.walk_back.tip = With the whole hero turned to your look ("Hero turns to where you look": Whole body, and "From behind too") and walking the other way - more than 100° from where he faces - his legs step backward (how: the box below), each planted foot standing on the ground. Off: the game's forward walk turned with him - his legs walk forward while he goes back, and look crossed. Not with "your legs step the way you move". The drawn legs only. Live.
body.walk_back_reverse.label = ... by the game's own walk played backwards
body.walk_back_reverse.tip = On: his pelvis and legs exactly as the game drew them while he walked (the last 2.5 seconds of his walking are kept, also through standing), shown in reverse order - the heel lifts behind him and the toes reach back to land, every joint the game's own; the trunk rides on that pelvis (held still with "lock"). Off: as 0.185 - each foot's place mirrored front to back and the knees solved again: the foot lifts high in front of him and lands behind toes up, which still looked like crossed legs. The drawn legs only. Live.
body.yaw.label = Body turn correction, °
body.yaw.tip = Added to where the hero faces (the arms too) if he stands sideways: try 90, -90 or 180.

# --- Effects around the hero (F4) ---
group.effects_around_the_hero_f4 = Effects around the hero (F4)
group.effects_around_the_hero_f4.help = Effects on the hero that get in the way in first person, such as Bone Armor round your eyes: draw them fainter, make them turn slower or move them lower. Visual only: the buff and its numbers stay the game's.
render.dim_own_effects.label = Draw the hero's own effects fainter
render.dim_own_effects.tip = Bone Armor wraps round the eyes of the first-person view and blinds. On: the effects that sit on the hero - the overlays of his own states (Bone Armor, Frozen / Shiver / Chilling Armor, Energy Shield, Blade Shield, Fade ...), each with its casting flash, and the aura rings at his feet - are faded to the percentages below, with the effect's own "Fade" parameter (the one the game fades an overlay with when its unit fades; 0 % hides the effect). Solid effects - Bone Armor's bones, Blade Shield's blades, Energy Shield, the shrines' overlays: an opaque mesh the Fade does not reach - cannot be fainter, so under 100 % they are not drawn at all. Off in the settings that come with the mod. Visual only: the buff and its numbers are the game's; monsters', mercenaries' and other players' effects, hits and skills' casts are drawn as ever, and so is everything in F1 - F3. Holy Shield is a colour on the shield, not an overlay: not covered. An effect already on when you tick this is dimmed at once; the log says, for every effect, what was found and what was done. First person (F4) only. Live.
render.dim_own_effects_pct.label = Own effects left, %
render.dim_own_effects_pct.tip = The value the effect's Fade parameter gets: 100 = as the game draws them, 0 = hidden (the effect is switched off). The armors and the like. Bone Armor and the other solid effects are hidden under 100. Live.
render.dim_own_auras_pct.label = Aura rings at the feet left, %
render.dim_own_auras_pct.tip = The rings of the paladin and barbarian auras and the like, at the hero's feet. The value the effect's Fade parameter gets: 100 = as the game draws them, 0 = hidden. Live.
render.slow_own_effects.label = Bone Armor turns slower
render.slow_own_effects.tip = Bone Armor's bones whirl round the eyes of the first-person view. On: Bone Armor and the hero's other solid effects (Blade Shield, Energy Shield, the shrines' overlays) turn at the speed below - the effect's own playback speed, the one the game pauses an overlay with. Visual only: the buff and its numbers are the game's; other players, F1 - F3 and flat see it as ever. With "Own effects left" under 100 (above) the solid effects are hidden instead. First person (F4) only. Live.
render.own_effects_speed_pct.label = Bone Armor's speed, %
render.own_effects_speed_pct.tip = How fast Bone Armor and the other solid effects turn, in % of the game's speed: 100 = the game's, 1 = barely turning (never 0: they must still turn). Live.
render.lower_own_effects.label = Bone Armor's height
render.lower_own_effects.tip = Bone Armor circles round the eyes of the first-person view. On: Bone Armor and the hero's other solid effects (Blade Shield, Energy Shield, the shrines' overlays) are drawn the height below lower (or higher) than the game puts them - lower, they circle below the eyes. Where the renderer draws them, nothing else: the buff and its numbers are the game's; other players, F1 - F3 and flat see them as ever. The log says, per effect, whether it was moved. First person (F4) only. Live.
render.own_effects_height_cm.label = Bone Armor's height, cm
render.own_effects_height_cm.tip = How far from where the game puts them: 0 = the game's place, negative = lower (-60: about the waist), positive = higher. Live.

stick.rotate.tip = The left stick is turned by the camera's yaw, so forward is forward in the view.
stick.exact.label = Exact mode
stick.exact.tip = The stick goes through the real camera axes; the direction and diagonal settings below are then unused.
stick.sign.label = Reverse walking direction
stick.sign.tip = Tick if after a head turn forward on the stick walks the wrong way.
stick.angle_scale.label = Turn strength
stick.angle_scale.tip = Approximate mode: the stick is turned by the camera's yaw times this (0.5 = half).
stick.squash.label = Diagonal correction
stick.squash.tip = Below 1 if diagonals drift after a turn (the isometric screen squash). 1 = off.

# --- Turning (right stick) ---
group.turning_right_stick = Turning (right stick)
group.turning_right_stick.help = Turn the body with the right stick: smooth turning at a set speed, or snap turns of a set angle at each flick. Tick reverse if pushing right turns you left.
turn.right_stick.label = Turn with the right stick
turn.right_stick.tip = Right stick X turns the body (the camera and walking); the game no longer gets the right stick.
@turn.smooth.label = Smooth turning
@turn.smooth.tip = On: the right stick turns continuously, as fast as you push it up to the speed below. Off: one snap of the angle below each time you flick it. Switching keeps both the speed and the angle.
turn.speed.label = Smooth turn speed, °/s
turn.speed.tip = Degrees per second at full deflection; used while smooth turning is on.
@turn.snap.label = Snap turn angle, °
@turn.snap.tip = Degrees turned by one flick; used while smooth turning is off.
turn.sign.tip = Tick if pushing right turns you left.

# --- Thumbsticks: dead zone (stick drift) ---
group.thumbsticks_dead_zone_stick_drift = Thumbsticks: dead zone (stick drift)
group.thumbsticks_dead_zone_stick_drift.help = For VR controller sticks that drift or never quite reach a full push: raise the dead zone until the stick rests, lower the full-push point if it never reaches the rim. Each stick on its own; not for a gamepad.
direct.stick_deadzone_left_pct.label = Left stick dead zone, %
direct.stick_deadzone_left_pct.tip = A left stick that drifts (walks or moves the menu by itself, or the belt flick does not re-arm): raise this until it rests. Inside this much of a full push the stick reads as centred; past it the push starts again from zero, so there is no jump, and it is measured on the stick's length, so diagonals are cut no sooner than a straight push. 0 = none (as before). The VR controllers only (native OpenXR, and FlatVR with its raw controllers), not a gamepad. Live.
direct.stick_outer_left_pct.label = Left stick full push at, %
direct.stick_outer_left_pct.tip = A left stick that never quite reaches a full push: from this much of its throw on it counts as fully pushed (the walk runs, a flick counts). 100 = only the rim (as before). Live.
direct.stick_deadzone_right_pct.label = Right stick dead zone, %
direct.stick_deadzone_right_pct.tip = A right stick that drifts (the view turns by itself, or a snap turn or flick does not re-arm): raise this until it rests. Inside this much of a full push the stick reads as centred; past it the push starts again from zero, so there is no jump. 0 = none (as before). The VR controllers only, not a gamepad. Live.
direct.stick_outer_right_pct.label = Right stick full push at, %
direct.stick_outer_right_pct.tip = A right stick that never quite reaches a full push: from this much of its throw on it counts as fully pushed (the fastest smooth turn, a snap). 100 = only the rim (as before). Live.
direct.walk_by_lean.label = Left stick: walk, run only when pushed far
direct.walk_by_lean.tip = First person (F4) with the plugin's own controllers: the hero walks while the left stick leans up to the limit below and runs past it - small steps get easy, and walking spends no stamina. It is the game's own walk and run (its run threshold and its Run key), no speed of ours; out of stamina the game walks as ever. The room walk and BodyWalk's walk are left as they are. Off = as before (the game walks only on a light push and runs as its Run / walk switch says). Live.
direct.walk_by_lean_pct.label = ... run from this much of a push, %
direct.walk_by_lean_pct.tip = How far the left stick must lean before the hero runs; up to here he walks. 80 = the last fifth of the stick runs. Live.

input.flat_pad_on_touch.tip = With the box above: the pad is hidden only until you use it - a button, a trigger or a stick pushed (not a stick's drift); from then on the game sees it. Unticked: hidden for good, the gamepad does nothing in flat mode.
camera.stick_pitch_flat.label = Flat: the gamepad's right stick looks up and down
camera.stick_pitch_flat.tip = In first and third person (F3, F2) the right stick's up / down looks up and down as the mouse does; left / right turns, as ever. A push more sideways than up / down only turns. Needs "Turn with the right stick". Unticked: the right stick only turns.
input.flat_aim_ground.label = Flat: aim on raised ground (stairs, ledges) where you look
input.flat_aim_ground.tip = With our camera (first or third person) a click, the hover and a skill's point go to the ground drawn under the crosshair, raised floors too. Unticked: the game's own point, made for its view from above - from first person it lands cells off on stairs and ledges.
input.flat_body_pick.label = Flat: click a monster, an NPC or a chest by its body
input.flat_body_pick.tip = Third and first person: monsters, NPCs, doors, shrines, chests and portals near you are clicked by their body, not only by their feet (from sajmonsoft's flat fork). Unticked: by the feet, as the game's own view from above has it.
input.flat_portal_no_oval.label = Flat: no black oval in the town portal
input.flat_portal_no_oval.tip = Third and first person: the portal's black oval, which stands still while the blue ring turns to the camera, is not drawn; the ring is (from sajmonsoft's flat fork). For portals seen from then on. Unticked: drawn as the game has it.
input.vr_keys_walk.label = VR view F2 like flat: mouse look, crosshair, W A S D
input.vr_keys_walk.tip = Third person with the mouse and keyboard, as in flat mode: the mouse turns the camera, the pointer is the crosshair in the middle (its depth: UI: F2 behind tab), a click goes there - on a monster an attack, on an item a pick-up, on the ground a shot - and W A S D walk where the camera looks, not north on the game's map. F9 frees the pointer for menus; W A S D keep walking. Needs the game in mouse mode: after a pad stick, click once.
input.crosshair.label = Crosshair picture
input.crosshair.tip = The pointer while the mouse looks: your own picture (png, jpg, bmp), its middle is where you aim; it is fitted into 32-64 pixels by the window's height. A picture with no transparency: its black is see-through. A bare name is looked for in reshade-shaders\Textures; a full path works too. Empty (x) = the built-in one.

# --- Input ---
group.input = Input
group.input.help = How BodyWalk's controls reach the game: the gamepad and the walk straight from BodyWalk, which pad button "D2R: Inventory" presses, whether A only attacks, and picking up one thing per press.
input.bodywalk_pad.label = Gamepad straight from BodyWalk
input.bodywalk_pad.tip = The game's gamepad is BodyWalk's own report, read directly: no virtual gamepad (ViGEm) needed.
input.direct_walk.label = Walk straight from BodyWalk, not through the gamepad
input.direct_walk.tip = Views F2-F4: BodyWalk's stick moves the hero through the game's own walking code, turned by the camera, in mouse mode and in controller mode alike; the gamepad's left stick is kept from the game outside menus (it would walk twice and switch the interface to the controller). Off: the hero walks through the gamepad's stick.
input.bodywalk_walk_lift.label = BodyWalk's walk starts from (stick length, 0 = off)
input.bodywalk_walk_lift.tip = F4: walking in place with BodyWalk, the hero starts sooner. BodyWalk's steps reach its stick through its averages and speed curve, so from standing its stick climbs for the better part of a second, and the game walks only once it is past its dead zone (0.32). With a length here, BodyWalk's stick from that length on counts as just past the game's dead zone (the slowest walk the game has, its direction kept), so the hero starts while BodyWalk is still climbing; past the dead zone nothing changes. Too low and a leg twitch while standing walks a step: 0.10 - 0.15 is a start. Only BodyWalk's stick, never the controller's. 0 = off, as before. [debug] walk_start_log tells the gain. Live.
input.inventory_button.label = "D2R: Inventory" presses
input.inventory_button.tip = The pad button BodyWalk's "D2R: Inventory" action sends to the game. In D2R's pad layout View opens the map.
input.inventory_button.choice0 = Menu (Start)
input.inventory_button.choice1 = View (Back)
input.a_attack_only.label = A button only attacks
input.a_attack_only.tip = Picking up, opening and talking then go to the BodyWalk action "D2R: Pick up / interact".
input.interact_one_press.label = Pick up / interact: one thing per press
input.interact_one_press.tip = VR first person (F4): "pick up / interact" (the right A without BodyWalk, or BodyWalk's action) acts on what is under it when you press it, and on nothing else: a chest opened by a press does not also give you its loot, a press held over a pile takes one item - let go and press again for the next. A press on nothing does nothing, even if something comes under it while held, and a press held while a menu opens or closes counts only after you let go. Off: held, it takes whatever is under it, as before. F1, F2, F3: as before. Live. (After bearstonem/d2r-pcvr, by CalMac91.)

# --- Gestures (native OpenXR) ---
group.gestures_native_openxr = Gestures (native OpenXR)
group.gestures_native_openxr.help = Gestures in F4 with native OpenXR: swap weapon sets by pressing the grip behind your shoulder (pick the hand), and draw gesture runes and their trails in the headset.
hands.shoulder_swap.label = Swap weapon sets: the grip behind the shoulder
hands.shoulder_swap.tip = Native OpenXR: reach a hand behind either shoulder and press its grip once - the game's own "Swap weapons" (not while "The shoulders hold your weapons" is ticked on Weapon Weight: then that zone draws instead) (weapon set I / II) is pressed, as its key would be, with all of the game's gates. The hand has to rest there for a moment first; the grip pressed there is the swap's and takes no belt potion; reaching back without the grip (a javelin's wind-up) does nothing. The game's weapon set says whether it took: a swap that did not is not repeated by itself. Off: as before. With FlatVR, bind BodyWalk's "D2R key: Swap weapons" to a gesture behind the shoulder instead. Live. F4 only.
hands.shoulder_swap_hand.label = Swap weapon sets: hand
hands.shoulder_swap_hand.tip = The hand that reaches behind the shoulder and presses its grip. Live.
hands.shoulder_swap_hand.choice0 = Right
hands.shoulder_swap_hand.choice1 = Left
openxr.runes_draw.label = Draw gesture runes and trails in the headset
openxr.runes_draw.tip = Native OpenXR, first person (F4), with BodyWalk running. A gesture you draw in the air with a hand (a circle, a rune) is shown the way a spell rune is: its picture hangs in the room in front of you and lights up as your hand draws it, and the path of your hand is a glowing trail that ends in a bright blob at the hand. When the shape is complete the picture flashes and fades (the gesture's own binding fires - that is set in BodyWalk, not here); a stray attempt just fades. BodyWalk recognises the shape and decides what to show; this only draws it, in the headset, over the game. Off, or in the other views (F1 - F3), or with no BodyWalk: nothing is drawn, the game as before. Live.
