Along the arm: a surface across the forearm, from the elbow side (or the hand side). Across the hand: a surface across it, from the thumb side or the little finger's. Level in the world: always horizontal, whatever the hand does. (Replaces the older Liquid level: along the arm is the first, level in the world the last.) Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice0 = Along the arm: the elbow side full
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice1 = Along the arm, the other way: the hand side full
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice2 = Across the hand: the thumb side full
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice3 = Across the hand: the little finger side full
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice4 = Out of the hand: from the skin up, the level parallel to the back of the hand
hud.hand_vitals_orb_fill.choice5 = Level in the world
hud.hand_vitals_orb_disc.label = Disc faces
hud.hand_vitals_orb_disc.tip = The game's own globe as a ball (Shape: Full glass ball) is a flat picture: it can turn to face your eyes all the time, or stay fixed on the wrist - a disc lying on the back of the hand, its up along the hand - and turn with it. On the medallion it is always on the base. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_disc.choice0 = The eyes (as before)
hud.hand_vitals_orb_disc.choice1 = Fixed on the wrist
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.label = Which wrist
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.tip = The game's own globes have life on the left and mana on the right. Both on one wrist puts them side by side across the hand. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.choice0 = Life on the left, mana on the right
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.choice1 = Life on the right, mana on the left
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.choice2 = Both on the left
hud.hand_vitals_orb_hands.choice3 = Both on the right
hud.hand_vitals_orb_size_cm.label = Size, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_size_cm.tip = The ball's diameter. 5 is a medallion's size. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_mirror.label = Right wrist mirrors the left
hud.hand_vitals_orb_mirror.tip = The right wrist's ball takes the left wrist's three numbers (the same along, the same across toward the thumb, the same up), so the two sit as mirror images. The right wrist's own sliders keep their values, greyed, for when it is unticked. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_on_bone.label = On the forearm bone itself (no numbers)
hud.hand_vitals_orb_on_bone.tip = Ticked: each ball sits on its forearm bone - on the surface of the forearm's own mesh (read off the hero's model, again when the armour changes), out of the back of the wrist next to the hand, turned with the bone - wherever the arm is drawn: by your controllers, held on a body, by the game's animation. The place and turn numbers below and the class depths are not used (a shield still rolls it to the inner side). A forearm whose mesh gives no size: the numbers, as before (the log says which). Unticked: the numbers. VR F4. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_drawn_hand.label = Ride the hand as drawn
hud.hand_vitals_orb_drawn_hand.tip = Ticked: the balls sit on the hero's hand exactly as it is drawn - laid on a body or a prop your hand holds, fitted onto the weapon - so they stay on the hand while it holds on and your real hand moves. A bottle held in the palm rides it the same way. Unticked: the hand as the controller first put it, before those steps, as before (holding an NPC, the balls kept the controller's turn). VR F4. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_along_cm.label = Left wrist X, along the arm, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_along_cm.tip = From the wrist joint along the hand's axis: + toward the knuckles, - toward the elbow. 0 is at the wrist. Turns with the hand. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_side_cm.label = Left wrist Y, across the hand, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_side_cm.tip = Across the hand: + toward the thumb, - toward the little finger. 0 is in the middle of the back of the hand. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_up_cm.label = Left wrist Z, up off the hand, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_up_cm.tip = Out of the back of the hand, from the wrist's axis (- into it). The arm's skin is about 2 - 3 cm out: 4 sinks the ball a little into the skin, 6 or more floats it above. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_along_cm.label = Right wrist X, along the arm, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_side_cm.label = Right wrist Y, across the hand, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_side_cm.tip = Across the hand: + toward the thumb, - toward the little finger (the same way as on the left wrist, so the same number is the mirror image). Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_up_cm.label = Right wrist Z, up off the hand, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_up_cm.tip = Out of the back of the hand, from the wrist's axis (- into it). Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_x_deg.label = Left wrist rotation X, round the arm, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_x_deg.tip = Turns the whole medallion - its base, its dome and the way the liquid fills - about its own middle, round the wrist's axis along the hand: + turns its face toward the thumb, - toward the little finger. Anatomical: the same number on the other wrist is the mirror image. 0 keeps it flat on the back of the hand. (For the game's own globes as a ball facing your eyes it has no effect.) Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_y_deg.label = Left wrist rotation Y, across the hand, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_y_deg.tip = Turns the whole medallion about its own middle, round the axis across the hand: + turns its face toward the elbow, - toward the knuckles. Anatomical: the same number on the other wrist is the mirror image. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_z_deg.label = Left wrist rotation Z, up off the hand, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_left_rot_z_deg.tip = Turns the whole medallion about its own middle, round the axis out of the back of the hand (like turning a watch face on the wrist): + turns its "up" from the knuckles toward the little finger. Anatomical: the same number on the other wrist is the mirror image. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_rot_x_deg.label = Right wrist rotation X, round the arm, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_rot_y_deg.label = Right wrist rotation Y, across the hand, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_right_rot_z_deg.label = Right wrist rotation Z, up off the hand, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_under_shield.label = Under a shield: the ball goes to the other side of the wrist
hud.hand_vitals_orb_under_shield.tip = The wrist that wears the shield (the left arm, or the right one after the shoulder draw swaps your hands) rolls its ball half a turn round the arm to the inner side of the wrist, so the shield does not cover it, and rolls it back when the shield leaves that arm - a short smooth turn. Only in VR F4. Unticked: the ball stays on the back of the hand under a shield. The sliders below tune the new place and are added to the wrist's own numbers above. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_turn_deg.label = Under a shield: turn round the arm, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_turn_deg.tip = How far the ball rolls round the wrist's axis when a shield is on that arm. 180 is the opposite side of the wrist (the inner side); a smaller number stops short of it. + sends the back of the hand over the thumb side, - over the little finger side (the same on both wrists, so the roll is the mirror image). Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_along_cm.label = Under a shield: X, along the arm, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_along_cm.tip = Added to the wrist's own X while a shield is on that arm: + toward the knuckles, - toward the elbow. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_side_cm.label = Under a shield: Y, across the hand, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_side_cm.tip = Added to the wrist's own Y while a shield is on that arm, measured in the rolled frame: at the full half turn + points toward the little finger (the thumb has gone round to the other side). Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_up_cm.label = Under a shield: Z, up off the skin, cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_up_cm.tip = Added to the wrist's own Z while a shield is on that arm, measured out of the skin where the ball now sits: + floats it higher, - sinks it. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_x_deg.label = Under a shield: rotation X, round the arm, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_x_deg.tip = Added to the wrist's own rotation X while a shield is on that arm (see the wrist rotation sliders above for the meaning). Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_y_deg.label = Under a shield: rotation Y, across the hand, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_y_deg.tip = Added to the wrist's own rotation Y while a shield is on that arm. Live.
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_z_deg.label = Under a shield: rotation Z, up off the skin, °
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_rot_z_deg.tip = Added to the wrist's own rotation Z while a shield is on that arm. Live.
@status.hero_class_shield.label = The hero playing now
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_up_cm_amazon.label = Amazon, under a shield: depth (Z), cm
hud.hand_vitals_orb_shield_up_cm_amazon.tip = Added - while a Amazon wears a shield - to the shield's own Z above, measured out of the skin where the ball now sits, on the inner side of the wrist: + floats it off the arm, - sinks it in. The forearm's model differs with the class, so one depth fits one hero only. 0 = no value of its own: the shield's Z above, as before. Edit the row of the hero you play - the line above says which one the game has now. Live.

Anatomical: the same number on the other wrist is the mirror image. It eases in and out with the roll. 0 = no value of its own. Live.

hud.wrist_status.label = Wrist status: summons, mercenary, buffs, auras, curses (F4)
hud.wrist_status.tip = Small icons and counters that come up beside the medallions when the BACK of a wrist is turned to your eyes (VR first person, F4, native OpenXR). By default the left wrist shows what is ON you - the auras and buffs you have (Might, Holy Shield, Frozen Armor, Battle Orders, a potion, a shrine ...) with the curses and ailments that hurt you (Amplify Damage, Decrepify, Chilled, Poisoned ...) under a red rim - and the right wrist what you COMMAND: how many skeletons, mages, golems, wolves, ravens, vines, sentries, hydras, demons you have, and your mercenary (a red 0 when it is dead). Read from the game's own lists, nothing is changed. The skill icons come from the local icon cache (see the skill wheel); without it the chips show initials. Needs the plugin and the effect of this version; the wrists as such are the medallions above. Live.

The left hand by default: the right one is usually the working hand. Show or hide it from a button or a gesture: BodyWalk's app action "FlatVR Game Map".

tab.world = World

# --- Fog ---
group.fog = Fog
group.fog.help = The distance fog, and fixes for the game's depth effects seen from our camera. Set where the fog is complete, its falloff, fog in caves and its colour, whether fire and spells are spared, and fixes for the game's own fogs, walls in front of the hero, roofs and lighting at a square window.
fog.game_fog_mist.label = The game's fog over its mist too
fog.game_fog_mist.tip = The game's own fog pass adds its volumetric mist (lit by torches and the like) after the fog, never fogged by distance: in a cave our dark fog turned the far walls black and the mist stayed, a light band behind the fires. Ticked: the mist fades with distance as everything else does. Without ReShade only. Live.
fog.game_fog_caves_black.label = The game's fog darkens to black in caves
fog.game_fog_caves_black.tip = Underground the game's fog fades to black, whatever the caves' fog colour says, and the void past a cave ceiling's rim is left alone - the game's fog pass laid its torch-lit mist over it whole, a light band behind the fires. Distance darkens, never glows. Without ReShade only. Live.
fog.game_fog_our_curve.label = The game's fog by our curve
fog.game_fog_our_curve.tip = The game's own fog pass fades the fog in as our effect does - from Fog start to Full fog by the Curve below (in caves their own start, end and strength) - instead of its own exponential, which puts nearly all of the fog right after the start and leaves the far range one grey. A few instructions in its pass, nothing added. Without ReShade only. Live.
fog.fog_keeps_colour.label = The game's fog keeps the act's colour at night
fog.fog_keeps_colour.tip = While the game draws the fog: its colour is the act's own (the colours above) at every hour - the far fades into a light haze of it, never toward black. Our own effect's fog is not changed. Off: it darkens with the game's light, as before. Live.
fog.fog_into_sky.label = The game's fog fades the far into the sky behind it
fog.fog_into_sky.tip = In the open air the fog's colour at each point is the sky straight behind it, as in the Arcane Sanctuary: the far land, the world's edge and tall far buildings fade into the sky, not into one flat colour (the sky's low part is the act's fog colour, as it is drawn). Far objects show the sky through them. The game's fog only (with "The game's fog as thick and as coloured as ours"); our own effect's fog is not changed. Underground as before. Live. Off: one fog colour, as before.
fog.game_fog_match.label = The game's fog as thick and as coloured as ours
fog.game_fog_match.tip = The game's fog came out darker than the act's fog colour (the area's colour grading) and thinner than ours (it thins above the eye, and without our curve it is the game's own): in act 4 the far land stood as a dark silhouette and hid nothing. Ticked, the effect measures what the game's fog shows where it is complete, moves each fogged pixel toward the act's colour by the game's share, and makes up the share the game left out to our own fog's - the far land, the world's edge and far planes hidden as by our old fog. Never on the game's sky. Our effect's pass, which runs anyway for the sky. Live. Off: as the game lays it.
fog.game_fog_before_fx.label = The game's fog before smoke and fire
fog.game_fog_before_fx.tip = The fog laid on the scene before the game adds its smoke, mist and fire, so they lie over the fogged world unfogged - without it the game's fog pass fogs them by the wall behind them (haze cut into black holes in front of far walls). One pass of ours on the graphics card (its cost in the log's 10 s line). Without ReShade only. Applies when the game is started again.
fog.game_fog_height.label = The game's fog thins with height
fog.game_fog_height.tip = The game's own fog pass leaves the sky clear: the fog as it is up to the fog's top less its softness, fading out above that, none above the top (world units above your eyes). For the game's sky dome, so its sky shows above the fogged horizon. Its own pass, nothing added. Outdoors only (underground no sky to keep clear). Without ReShade only. Off: the game's fog as it is. Live.
fog.game_fog_top.label = The game's fog: its top, units above the eyes
fog.game_fog_top.tip = How high the game's fog reaches: none above this, world units above your eyes (the hero is ~7.5 tall; the sky dome at its radius). Live.
fog.game_fog_soft.label = The game's fog: softness of its top, units
fog.game_fog_soft.tip = How far below its top the game's fog fades out: small, a sharp edge; large, a long soft fade. Live.
fog.game_fog_top_from_floor.label = The game's fog: its top counted from the hero's floor
fog.game_fog_top_from_floor.tip = The top above is counted from the floor the hero stands on, not from your eyes: a camera high over the hero (third person, the view from above) no longer moves where the fog ends, and land below your eyes is not all fogged with a line at eye height. Off: from the eyes, as before. Unticking "thins with height" instead gives the fog by distance alone, as our own fog. Live.
fog.end.tip#2 = Where the fog is complete. World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall).
fog.curve.label = Falloff
fog.curve.tip = 1 = linear; more = a clearer middle distance.
fog.blur.label = Depth blur, px (0 = off)
fog.blur.tip = The fog over a 5x5 grid this many pixels apart: holes and specks in the depth melt away.
fog.spare_effects.label = Fog spares fire, spells and smoke (test)
fog.spare_effects.tip = Fire, spells, smoke and glows are fogged only as much as the scene behind them is not: a torch or a Fire Bolt in front of a far wall stays bright instead of fogged like the wall. The game's own transparent layers of each frame are copied for it (VR F4 only). Applies when the game is started again; off = the fog as before.
render.fog_in_frame.label = Fog drawn inside the game's frame (test)
render.fog_in_frame.tip = The fog is drawn into the game's own picture before its fire, spells and smoke, and the game lays them over the fogged scene: a torch, a Fire Bolt or an Inferno in front of a far wall is not fogged like the wall. The sky and the black beyond the world keep the fog as before. With an act's own fog colour (World > Sky); VR F4 only. Applies when the game is started again; off = the fog as before. Over "Fog spares fire" when both are on.
fog.caves.label = Fog in caves and dungeons
fog.caves.tip = Off: no fog underground (every area that is not outdoors); the open air keeps it. The Arcane Sanctuary has its own switch (Sky > Arcane Sanctuary: fog fades into its sky).
fog.ease_in.label = Fog eased in, no hard ring
fog.ease_in.tip = The fog fades in softly over its first 40 units past its start: no sharp edge round the clear ground at your feet. Wherever our curve draws the fog: our effect, and the game's fog with "The game's fog by our curve" on (not the game's own curve). From D2R VR Unleashed (bearstonem). Live. Off: the fog as before.
fog.no_fog_river.label = No fog in the River of Flame
fog.no_fog_river.tip = No added fog in the River of Flame, though it is open air: its lava's own glow and haze stay the game's. Our effect's fog and the game's fog alike. From D2R VR Unleashed (bearstonem). Live. Off: the fog there as everywhere outdoors.
fog.caves_strength.label = Fog strength in caves
fog.caves_strength.tip = How much the full fog covers in caves: 1 = the far end is gone in the fog colour, less = it shows through.
fog.color_caves.label = Fog colour in caves
fog.color_caves.tip = Caves, dungeons, crypts: every area that is not outdoors. Empty (x) = that act's colour.
fog.color_caves.empty = same as the act
render.game_height_fog.label = The game's own height fog
render.game_height_fog.tip = Only the act 2 town has it. From our camera its edge is a hard line across the picture with a pale veil above it (the game's camera never sees that edge). Off: vrcam sets it to 0.
render.game_depth_fog.label = The game's own depth fog
render.game_depth_fog.tip = Every outdoor area has it, from its camera's distance out: a grey haze in the four corners of the picture (from above too), over the near ground from our camera. Off: vrcam sets it to 0.
render.depth_fix.label = The game's effects measure depth from our camera
render.depth_fix.tip = The game keeps a copy of the depth for its fog, height fog, ambient occlusion, reflections and water, made for its camera from above (550 to 1060 units away). From ours everything is nearer and read as one flat wall 550 away: the act 2 town's straight line with a pale veil above it, the haze in the corners. On: that depth runs from our camera. Off: the game's own.
render.own_depth.label = Depth for the effects
render.own_depth.tip = Where the fog, the sky and the cave ceiling get the scene's depth. Our own (the default): the game's scene depth-stencil, picked once and kept until it goes away or the window or render size changes, copied for each eye before its effects - one copy on the graphics card an eye, nothing for the game to wait on. Needed in a square window and with a render size: there ReShade alone takes the 4096 shadow map and the fog flickers with a view from above. ReShade's own: ReShade's Generic Depth picks it (fine in a window that is not square). VR only. Live.
render.own_depth.choice0 = ReShade's own depth
render.own_depth.choice1 = Our own, picked once
render.depth_fix_mode.label = How that depth is set
render.depth_fix_mode.tip = In each pass as it is bound (D2R VR's way, as before): every constant buffer the game binds gets our depth range - a pass that gets its constants another way keeps the game's. It works through ReShade alone: without ReShade it does nothing, and the game's ambient occlusion, reflections, water, lights and height fog keep its own camera's depth - murkier, flatter stone, weaker light from braziers and torches (the game's fog chosen sets the next one by itself). Once a frame where the game makes it (found by bearstonem/d2r-pcvr): the range is written right after the game builds the frame's constants, before any pass reads them, so every pass - fog, ambient occlusion, particles, grass - reads the same depth; it runs from the near plane of our camera to the game's own far end (the distance below is not used). To compare: the act 1 grass, the act 2 town's veil, the haze in the corners. Off: the game's own depth, as "The game's effects measure depth from our camera" unticked. Live.
render.depth_fix_mode.choice0 = Off (the game's own)
render.depth_fix_mode.choice1 = In each pass as it is bound (with ReShade only)
render.depth_fix_mode.choice2 = Once a frame where the game makes it
render.depth_range.label = How far that depth reaches
render.depth_range.tip = World units (the hero is ~7.5 tall). Farther counts as sky to the game's fog; shorter is finer near the hero.
render.solid_walls.label = Walls in front of the hero
render.solid_walls.tip = The game draws a wall between its camera and the hero at half alpha. From inside every wall you look at was see-through; from above it hid the hero.
render.solid_walls.choice0 = See-through (the game's)
render.solid_walls.choice1 = Solid, see-through only in F1
render.solid_walls.choice2 = Solid in every view
render.keep_roofs.label = Keep the roof when you walk into a building (F4)
render.keep_roofs.tip = For its camera high above the game takes away the roof of a building the hero walks into (Kurast Docks, the town's huts); from the eyes that showed the sky through the ceiling. On: the game's request to fade the roof out is answered with the roof kept, in VR F4 only - F1, F2, F3 keep the game's cut-aways. Nothing else that fades is touched. Idea: bearstonem/d2r-pcvr. Off: the game's own.
render.roofs_two_sided.label = Roofs: their underside, not the sky
render.roofs_two_sided.tip = The game draws a roof only from above, so from under a kept roof the sky showed through it. On: the materials of the roofs (a roof model's material named "roof") are built double-sided, and their underside is drawn. A material is built when its area loads: the change shows in the next area you go to (what is loaded now keeps its sides until the game loads it again, at the latest the next start). The same for the walls and stairs of the Kurast sewer entrances (Act 3), whose backs showed the sky from the stairs. VR only. Nothing else is changed. From bearstonem/d2r-pcvr (MIT). Off: the game's own.
render.portal_no_oval.label = No black oval in the town portal (F2 - F4)
render.portal_no_oval.tip = The town portal's black oval stands still while its blue ring turns to the camera, so from any view but the game's own from above it stands beside the ring. On: the oval is not drawn in F2, F3 and F4, the ring is; F1 keeps it. For portals seen from then on (a new area, or after a restart). From sajmonsoft's flat fork. Off: drawn as the game has it.
render.light_bounds_fix.label = Fix the game's lighting at a square or wide window
render.light_bounds_fix.tip = The game cuts the picture into 32 x 20 tiles and finds each tile's depth range for its lights with a shader that is right only at a 16:10 window. At a square or wide one (the VR window, 16:9) it misses rows: lights vanish in hard rectangles and a roof's shading flickers as the head moves. On: our own shader does that one job right while VR renders, with ReShade or without it (at 16:10 the numbers are the same as the game's). Off at once; ticked on again it takes effect at the next start of the game. Off: the game's own.
render.light_bounds_flat.label = ... in flat mode too
render.light_bounds_flat.tip = The same fix in flat mode (a monitor or a window, native OpenXR's flat picture too): the game's shader is wrong at 16:9 and at a square window as well, not only in VR. Follows the mode at once. Off: flat mode keeps the game's own shader, as before.

# --- Render distance ---
group.render_distance = Render distance
group.render_distance.help = How far around the hero the world is drawn: more room rings and a bigger model radius show more of the world and cost more processor time. With fog, 4-6 rings are enough.

# --- Scenery ---
group.scenery = Scenery
group.scenery.help = Fixes to the game's scenery for first person: floors that keep their height when you come back to a room, and the Kurast Docks canoe laid on the water instead of hanging in the sky. Only the picture changes.
render.floors_stay.label = Floors stay where they were (no ground that slides on a way back)
render.floors_stay.tip = The game gives each room of a level a height when it starts drawing it, matched to the rooms drawn round it at that moment, and forgets it when the room is out of sight. Its tiles' edges do not agree all the way round, so a room you come back to by another way (or after another area or town) can be a step higher or lower - from the game's camera above nobody sees it, from ours the floor slides: blocks pushed up, down and aside, the void showing between them. On: every room keeps the height it was first drawn at until you leave the game. The trade: the game also mends a room drawn at the wrong height (a step seen from afar, as by the Pandemonium Fortress's gate) when it draws it again as you come near - with this on, that mend does not come. Only the picture; nothing of the fight or the paths changes. Live. Off (the default): the game's own heights.
world.kurast_boat.label = Kurast Docks: the canoe in the sky sits on the water
world.kurast_boat.tip = The town's HD scenery places one canoe 50 units up, where the view from above never looks; in first person it hangs over the huts. On: it lies on the water by the western docks, where its prefab was built - one number of the town's scenery file changed (found by bearstonem/d2r-pcvr). This program makes that file from your game's own when it opens (Home: Kurast Docks canoe) and keeps it inside the mod (mods\D2R-VR\D2R-VR.mpq); nothing of the game itself changes, nor anything you play with. Takes effect at the next start of the game (a game already running keeps the canoe where it was). Off: the file is taken out again, the canoe as the game has it.

# --- Sky and fog ---
group.sky_and_fog = Sky and fog
group.sky_and_fog.help = Who draws the sky and the distance fog: the game itself (new) or our effect (old) - one choice for both.
render.game_drawn_flat.label = The game draws them in the flat game too
render.game_drawn_flat.tip = The sky dome, the cave dome and ceiling and the fog the game draws itself, also when you play on the monitor without a headset (the flat first and third person views; from above stays as it is). Off: only in VR first person (F4). Live.

# --- Sky ---
group.sky.help = A sky in the black void beyond the world, only in the open air. Set the clouds, whether the sky turns slowly, the sky over the dark rim round roofs and trees, and the Arcane Sanctuary's own stars all round and its fog.
sky.enabled.tip#2 = A sky in the black void beyond the world. Only in the open air; hidden while a menu or side panel is open.
sky.clouds.label = Clouds (0 = clear)
sky.clouds.tip = Times each area's own cloud cover.
sky.drift.label = The sky turns slowly (clouds drift)
sky.drift.tip = The painted sky goes slowly round you. Off: it stands still - the stars painted into the night skies went round with the clouds.
sky.cover_rims.label = The sky over the dark rim round roofs and trees
sky.cover_rims.tip = The game draws anything against the sky a pixel larger than its depth, its edge blended into black, and the sky was not painted there: a thin dark outline round every roof, treetop and far building, which the eyes by turns also moved off them every other frame. Ticked: the sky goes over that pixel when it is dim (a glow's light edge stays); silhouettes come out a pixel thinner. First person (F4) only. Unticked: as before. Live. Install the DLL and D2R_DepthFog.fx together. From bearstonem/d2r-pcvr.
sky.dome_fog_horizon.label = The game's sky: its horizon into the fog
sky.dome_fog_horizon.tip = The game-drawn sky's low part sinks into the act's fog colour, as our own sky's did: the fogged land meets the sky with no hard edge, and the colours match where they meet. Only while a fog is drawn. Off: the sky as the game draws it. Live.
sky.game_sky_closed.label = The game's sky: a whole sphere, one colour below
sky.game_sky_closed.tip = The game-drawn sky ended 12 degrees under the horizon: past a cliff's edge its rim stood as a hard line with a hole under it, the void and the fog showing through. Ticked, it closes into a whole sphere and its lower half is one colour - the sky's own at the horizon (with a fog drawn, the fog's: they meet in one colour). In every act, VR and flat. This program makes the dome's models again at once; the game takes them at its next start. Off: the open dome, as before.
sky.game_skybox.label = Arreat Summit: the sky dome far out
sky.game_skybox.tip = At the Arreat Summit (level 120) and the uber Summit (137) the game-drawn sky dome is laid as far out as the depth buffer holds it, so the game's mist along the cliffs stays in front of it however far. Off: the Summits as any open-air act 5 area - the dome at its usual radius. Live.
sky.summit_backdrop_hidden.label = Arreat Summit: no ground picture in first person
sky.summit_backdrop_hidden.tip = Below the Arreat Summit (level 120) and the uber Summit (137) the game puts a picture of the ground far below, made to be seen from above; in first person it stands as a flat wall. Ticked, it is hidden in VR first person (F4) and flat first person (F3): our sky and fog show in its place and the game's sea of clouds stays. The views from above keep it. Off: as the game draws it. Live.
sky.weather_first_person.label = Rain and snow in first person
sky.weather_first_person.tip = The game lays its rain and snow in a box round its own camera, high above and behind the hero for its view from above; in first person that box hangs in the air (the Arreat Summit's snow). Hidden: no rain or snow in VR first person (F4) and flat first person (F3). Round you: the box laid at your head there, so it falls round you. The other views keep the game's. The game's: as before.
sky.weather_first_person.choice0 = The game's (at its camera)
sky.weather_first_person.choice1 = Hidden
sky.weather_first_person.choice2 = Round you
sky.arcane_sky.label = Arcane Sanctuary: its own stars all round
sky.arcane_sky.tip = In the Arcane Sanctuary the void round the platforms shows the game's own star layers and clouds in every direction, below the platforms too (after bearstonem/d2r-pcvr). The pictures are made from your game's files when this program opens (Home: Arcane Sanctuary sky) and live inside the mod (mods\D2R-VR); nothing of the game is changed. Not in the views from above. Works with the outdoor sky off too. Off: the void as the game draws it.
sky.arcane_fog.label = Arcane Sanctuary: fog fades into its sky
sky.arcane_fog.tip = The distance fog ([fog] on, World > Fog) in the Arcane Sanctuary too: the far platforms dissolve into the sky behind them - its dark and its nebula, not its stars. Off: no fog under that sky, the platforms sharp to the end.

sky.light_night.tip = From this down: full night. In between the sky goes from one to the other.

# --- Cave ceiling ---
group.cave_ceiling = Cave ceiling
group.cave_ceiling.help = A stone vault drawn over the black void in caves, at its true depth in both eyes; first person only. Set the tile size and relief, a far wall and a floor below to close the void, the stone's contrast, detail and wet shine, and how torches and monsters with fire light it.
ceiling.enabled.tip#2 = A stone vault over the black void in caves, at its true depth in both eyes. First person only; for now act 1's caves, crypts, barracks, catacombs and cathedral and act 2's sewers and palace.
ceiling.game_ceiling_wall.label = The game's ceiling: bent down into a wall at its rim
ceiling.game_ceiling_wall.tip = A ring of the same lit rock round you where the game's ceiling ends (about 215 units out at tile size 10), from the ceiling down to below the floor (the floor's depth below): the black void past the ceiling's edge - a band between it and the far floor, lit by the fog behind fires - is closed by stone, as our effect's far wall closed it. Off: the flat ceiling. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling_beams.label = The game's ceiling: the barracks' own wooden beams
ceiling.game_ceiling_beams.tip = The game ships a wooden ceiling frame for the barracks (and its jail) that it never places: a grid of beams whose bottom sits at the barracks walls' top. Ticked, the game draws that frame over you in a grid of whole frames fixed in the world - its own model, wood and size, lit by its torches - with the barracks' stone over the beams to close the gaps between them. Made from your game's files. VR F4 only. Off: the flat stone ceiling. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome.label = The game's ceiling: the cathedral's dome over the chapel
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome.tip = In the Cathedral the game's ceiling rises into a dome over the chapel, as our effect's vault did there: one even dome standing on the four pillars round the altar, just high enough to pass over the altar's canopy. Where, how wide and how high come from the game's own pieces (measured from your game's files, the canopy found in the game as it is drawn); the cathedral's own stone, lit by its candles. The rest of the cathedral keeps the flat ceiling at its height. VR F4 only. Off: the flat ceiling. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome_size.label = The cathedral's dome: size
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome_size.tip = Times the dome measured from the game's pieces (1: standing on the chapel's four pillars), round the same middle. The whole vault grows or shrinks with it - its stone's pattern too - and the dome's height follows, so it still passes over the altar's canopy (0.7 at the least: smaller would cut through it). VR F4. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome_rise.label = The cathedral's dome: height
ceiling.game_ceiling_dome_rise.tip = Times the least height that passes over the altar's canopy (1: just over it). Higher only - lower would cut through the canopy. VR F4. Live.
ceiling.game_ceiling_domes_over_tall.label = The game's ceiling: a dome over every tall piece
ceiling.game_ceiling_domes_over_tall.tip = The cathedral's dome, wherever one of the game's pieces stands at least twice as high as its room's ceiling with pillars round it: the ceiling rises in a dome over just that piece, on those pillars, high enough to clear its top - the Worldstone in the Worldstone Chamber (level 132), the throne room's arch (131), Travincal's council hall. Where, how wide and how high come from the game's own pieces and models (measured from your game's files, the piece found in the game as it is drawn); the room's own stone. The rest of the room keeps the flat ceiling. The dome's size and height above apply to these too. VR F4 only. Off: the flat ceiling there, as before. This program makes their vaults again at once; the game takes them at its next start.
ceiling.height_from_walls.label = Ceiling height from the room's walls
ceiling.height_from_walls.tip = A room whose own height below is not set (0) has its ceiling on its own walls: where the walls the game builds that room with end (the middle of its wall, pillar and cliff pieces' tops, measured from your game's files). A room's own height, once you set it, always wins. Our effect's vault and the game's ceiling both; the game's rock that hangs lower rests its lowest point on the walls. Off, or a room built with no walls of that kind: 18 over the floor where no height is set. The log says each room's height and where it comes from. Live at the next area change.
ceiling.scale.label = Tile size
ceiling.scale.tip = World units per tile of the relief; the stone picture spans 4 tiles.
ceiling.steps.label#2 = Relief steps
ceiling.wall_distance.label = Far wall distance (0 = none)
ceiling.wall_distance.tip = A wall of the same stone this far round the hero, world units: the black void past the floor's edge is closed. It sinks in the fog like the rest.
ceiling.floor_depth.label = Floor below the floor (0 = none)
ceiling.floor_depth.tip = Stone this far under the hero's floor, world units: looking down past the drawn floor's edge shows it, not the void.
ceiling.contrast.label = Stone contrast
ceiling.contrast.tip = The picture's fine detail times this: more = crisper, harder rock, like the walls.
ceiling.detail.label = Detail relief
ceiling.detail.tip = How far the picture's grains and cracks stand out of the rock: they catch the light.
ceiling.wet.label = Wet shine
ceiling.wet.tip = Glints of the hero's and the torches' light on wet rock, as on the walls (0 = dry).
ceiling.torch_brightness.label = Torch glow
ceiling.torch_brightness.tip = How bright the torches' light on the ceiling is. A small flame gives less light than a big one.
ceiling.torch_radius.label = Torch light reach
ceiling.torch_radius.tip = World units from a fire where its light on the ceiling is down to half.
ceiling.fire_nearer.label = Fire light nearer to you
ceiling.fire_nearer.tip = A flame is drawn without depth, so the fire found in the picture is put where the wall or the floor behind it is, and its light on the ceiling sits behind the fire. This brings it nearer to you, world units along your line of sight to the flame (the hero is ~7.5 tall). 0 = where the depth says.
ceiling.torch_warmth.label = Torch warmth (yellow)
ceiling.torch_warmth.tip = 0 = the game's own pale torch colour; more = the orange-yellow of fire on the stone.
ceiling.torch_distance.label = Torch light distance
ceiling.torch_distance.tip = Only torches this near the hero light the ceiling; farther ones fade out - those of the next hall shone over the walls.
ceiling.monster_lights.label = Monsters with fire light the ceiling
ceiling.monster_lights.tip = The torches the Fallen carry and their shamans' fire. Off: the monsters are not looked at at all.
ceiling.monster_brightness.label = Monsters' fire glow
ceiling.monster_brightness.tip = The torches the Fallen carry and their shamans' fire, times the torches' glow. 0 = none.
ceiling.torch_halo.label = Torch halo in caves
ceiling.torch_halo.tip = How much of the game's own glow round a flame shows over the ceiling and the far floor (1 = all). The flame itself always stays.

# --- Light in caves ---
group.light_in_caves = Light in caves
group.light_in_caves.help = Brighter caves and dungeons through the game's own light, for a headset that loses the darkest shades. Set the hero's light circle, its strength and falloff, and the fill light. Only the drawing changes, nothing the game plays by. Works without the ceiling.
cave_light.enabled.label = Brighter caves and dungeons
cave_light.enabled.tip = The game's own light in caves, dungeons and crypts (every area that is not outdoors), given before the game makes its colours, so they keep their strength - not a lifted black level. Underground there is no sun: the hero's circle of light, the torches and the light that fills the place, which lights only inside that circle. Drawing only: the light radius and everything the game plays by stay as they are. For a headset that loses the darkest shades (an LCD, such as Meta Quest); an OLED (PS VR2) shows them as they are. Works without the ceiling.
cave_light.hero_reach.label = Hero's light circle (times the game's)
cave_light.hero_reach.tip = How far the hero's own light reaches, times the game's: a wider circle round him. 1 = as the game has it.
cave_light.hero_power.label = Hero's light strength (times the game's)
cave_light.hero_power.tip = How bright the hero's own light is, times the game's. 1 = as the game has it.
cave_light.hero_falloff.label = Hero's light falloff (times the game's)
cave_light.hero_falloff.tip = The game's attenuation of the hero's light (5.5), times this: how it fades with the distance. Past about 10 the circle above grows no wider - the light has faded before its edge; this changes that fading. 1 = as the game has it.
cave_light.ambient.label = Fill light (times the area's own)
cave_light.ambient.tip = The light that fills the place, inside the hero's circle: brighter, not wider. 1 = as the game has it. Each dungeon has its own: the act 2 tombs 0.12, the act 2 sewers 0.5, crypts and catacombs 1, act 1's caves 2, the maggot lair 12.5.
cave_light.ambient_min.label = Fill light at least
cave_light.ambient_min.tip = Whatever the dungeon has, at least this much: only for the darkest ones (the act 2 tombs: 0.12). Where the area's own times the slider above is more already (act 1's caves: 2 x 2 = 4), it does nothing. 0 = no floor.

# --- Shield (first person) ---
group.shield_first_person = Shield (first person)
group.shield_first_person.help = The shield in first person (F4). Tick to strap it to your forearm, so it goes and turns with the arm, then move and turn it with the sliders. Blink the strapped shield checks which shield the sliders act on; a Necromancer's head can hang from its cord.
shield.forearm.label = Shield strapped to the forearm
shield.forearm.tip = First person (F4): the shield on your left arm is strapped to the forearm as the model was made, not hung on the hand from the game's animation - it goes where the forearm goes and turns as it turns (with "Forearm turns with the wrist", rolling the hand rolls the shield). The weapon's sliders above never move it; the ones below do. A shield bash ("Shield bash casts Smite") is felt where the shield is drawn. Off: on the hand, as before. Live.
shield.x.label = Shield: move along X, cm
shield.x.tip = The shield moved on the forearm, along its own axes.
shield.y.label = Shield: move along Y, cm
shield.z.label = Shield: move along Z, cm
shield.pitch.label = Shield: turn about X, °
shield.pitch.tip = The shield turned on the forearm about its own axes.
shield.yaw.label = Shield: turn about Y, °
shield.roll.label = Shield: turn about Z, °
debug.shield_blink.label = Blink the strapped shield (a check: does the shield you see move with these?)
debug.shield_blink.tip = A test, not a setting: the bone the strapped shield hangs on is hidden for half a second in every two. If the shield on the screen blinks, it is the one these sliders, the put-away behind the left shoulder and the jump to the other arm act on. If it does not blink, the shield you see hangs on something else - say so. Live.
shield.heads_hang.label = Necromancer's heads hang from their cord
shield.heads_hang.tip = First person (F4): a Necromancer's shrunken head in your hand hangs down from its cord - from the point the game hangs it by, the knot or the handle in your fist - whatever the hand's angle. Moving the hand swings it like a weight on a string: it lags, swings out and settles; turning the hand about the cord twists it after, a little late. It is the game's own head model turned about that point; the item, its block and its stats are the game's. It is not strapped to the forearm (the shield sliders above do not move it). Off: as a shield - strapped to the forearm, or on the hand - stiff at the hand's angle, as before. Live.

# --- Attack along the hand (A button) ---
group.attack_along_the_hand_a_button = Attack along the hand (A button)
group.attack_along_the_hand_a_button.help = How the A button's attack is aimed along your hand, and how attacks stay in place in F4. Pick the aiming mode, and tick the options that keep attacks and stray clicks from walking or running the hero off. An experimental option lets you walk on after a spear or bow blow.
bow.mode.label = Aiming
bow.mode.tip = Shift + click works, but flips the game's interface to the mouse. Turn first: the stick turns the hero to the hand, then A goes through (gamepad only). Attack vector: while A is held the game's own attack points along the hand - turn the hand while firing.
bow.mode.choice1 = Left stick while A is held
bow.mode.choice2 = Shift + click along the hand
bow.mode.choice3 = Turn the hero to the hand first
bow.mode.choice4 = Attack vector along the hand
bow.turn_ms.label = Turn before the attack, ms
bow.turn_ms.tip = "Turn the hero first" only: how long the hero is turned before the attack. More if he does not turn in time.
gameplay.attack_in_place.label = Attacks never walk the hero (stand still)
gameplay.attack_in_place.tip = VR first person (F4) only. An attack the plugin presses - the trigger, a swing by touch, a throw, a shot from the bow's draw, a skill button when the skill panel knows its skill - is pressed together with the game's own Stand still (the Shift key's command), so with nothing under the point it is a swing or a shot in place and the hero never walks forward. The press waits a few milliseconds until the game has Stand still down. Skills that move the hero (Teleport, Charge, Leap, Whirlwind, Dragon Flight) and picking things up are left alone. While an attack is held the hero stands. A mouse click (or the laser's) on bare ground is the same: a skill in place, never a walk there; a click on a monster, item, door or NPC is the game's own. F1, F2, F3 (where a click on the floor walks) and the flat modes: as before. Off: attacks and clicks as they were. Live.
gameplay.move_while_attacking.label = Spear and bow: walk on as soon as the blow is out (changes the game)
gameplay.move_while_attacking.tip = EXPERIMENTAL - this changes how Diablo II plays. In the game a hero stands still until his attack's animation is over, also after the blow or the arrow is already out; that stop is the game's own rule, not the mod's. With this on, in VR first person (F4) with a spear, polearm, javelin, bow or crossbow, the left stick's walk goes on as soon as the blow lands or the arrow or javelin leaves - you can step back while you fight. The stand before the blow (the thrust, the draw) stays. The attack itself stays the game's: hit chance, damage, mana, arrows and attack speed - your next attack still waits until the animation would have ended. Swords, axes, maces and other weapons keep the game's stop. In a network game the host's setting applies to everyone: hosting a TCP/IP game with this ticked, every hero in it walks on after the blow (their next attack still waits for the animation); joined to someone else's game, this tick does nothing - the host decides. F1, F2, F3 and the flat modes: as before. On by default (the author, 2026-10-26). Off: the game's own stop. Live.
gameplay.block_stray_clicks.label = No stray mouse clicks in the world
gameplay.block_stray_clicks.tip = VR first person (F4) only. While you play in the world with no panel or menu open, the game gets no mouse button at all - a click that comes from outside the plugin (a mouse, the headset's or the streaming software's controller-to-mouse, a driver: the log says 'from a device') used to run the hero forward in the middle of a bow shot. Panels, menus, the title and character screens (the laser clicks there), mouse look and [bow] mode 2's own Shift + click are untouched. F1, F2, F3 and the flat modes: as before. Off: every click reaches the game. Live. The log names the origin and the controllers' trigger of each dropped click.
gameplay.block_stray_walk.label = No stray walks (a run to a point out of a click)
gameplay.block_stray_walk.tip = VR first person (F4) only. The game's client sends every command of the player through one funnel; a walk or run to a POINT that comes out of a click on bare ground is dropped there, before the hero starts it. Never touched: the left stick's walk, walks to a monster, item, door, NPC or waypoint, every skill (Teleport, Leap, Charge are skills), the stick's stop and the game's Force Move. A walk to a point from any other place is only written to the log. F1, F2, F3 (where a click on the floor walks) and the flat modes: as before. Off: commands as they were. Live.
gameplay.block_attack_run.label = An attack never runs the hero off (a bow shot, a blow, a throw)
gameplay.block_attack_run.tip = VR first person (F4) only. A shot aimed at a point in the air made the game RUN the hero toward that point, in the middle of the shot, even with Stand Still held (the log shows the run starting 3 ms after the pad's A went down). With this on, a walk or run to a point out of the pad's cast of an attack of ours is dropped; the shot itself, its animation and damage are the game's. Walks to a monster, an item or a door are never touched. Off (the default): such a run is only written to the log. CAUTION: when the game turns an aimed shot into that run, dropping it leaves NO shot - the cause is being fixed. Live.
gameplay.aim_no_chase.label = A shot along the hand never sends the hero after a monster
gameplay.aim_no_chase.tip = VR first person (F4) only. Why the game ran the hero off after a shot: before every cast it asks the pad's target (the monster nearest the aim); with one found, it takes Stand Still off the cast so the hero can attack that monster. A shot along the hand has its target taken away (that is the aim), and what is left is a click on the ground: a run to the point. With this on, that first question gets no target either, so the cast keeps Stand Still and is the same shot in place as with no monster near. Aim point, damage, animation and rate stay the game's. Off: as before. Live.

# --- Bow ---
group.bow.help = The bow in first person (F4, native OpenXR): draw the string with both hands and let go to shoot. Set the grab zone and pull, what the release presses, aiming up and down, the bow and string hand's pose, the arrow drawn in flight, a quiver of orbs to pick arrow skills, and arrow effects.
hands.bow_draw.label = Bow: draw the string with both hands
hands.bow_draw.tip = Native OpenXR: with a bow in hand, press the trigger of the hand without the bow at the bow's nock point (about 16 cm behind its grip), pull back along the line to the bow and let go - the game's own button is pressed once, aimed along the draw line. The game does the rest: its animation, attack rate, mana and arrows; the length of the pull adds nothing. A trigger pressed away from the string shoots nothing (the next box) or, with that box unticked, is the plain trigger as before. Needs native OpenXR and the first person view (F4): the other views keep everything as before. Off: the trigger as before. Live.
hands.bow_draw_only.label = Bow: a press away from the string shoots nothing
hands.bow_draw_only.tip = On: with a bow in hand (F4) the bow shoots only by a draw and a release. In the green grab zone the free hand's trigger (and the grip, if it starts the draw) is the draw's: nothing you bound to it in the controls (a pad button, a key command, an action) fires there - at the press, during the pull or at the release. Away from the zone only its shots are dropped - the game's attack, pad A and RT, and the skill the skill wheel picked - and everything else bound to it works as bound. The draw's own release still presses its attack or skill button. Other weapons, other views and the menus are as before. Off: a trigger pressed away from the string is the plain trigger as before. Live.
hands.bow_draw_button.label = Bow draw: the release presses
hands.bow_draw_button.tip = The attack: a bow's own arrow. A skill button: that slot of the controller's skill bar, whatever skill is on it - Magic, Fire, Cold, Ice, Exploding, Immolation, Freezing or Guided Arrow, Multiple Shot (its fan is the game's), Strafe (its own volley). Pressed once, 65 ms, as a thumb would. Live.
hands.bow_draw_button.choice0 = The attack
hands.bow_draw_button.choice1 = The skill on B
hands.bow_draw_button.choice2 = The skill on X
hands.bow_draw_button.choice3 = The skill on Y
hands.bow_draw_button.choice4 = The skill on RB
hands.bow_draw_button.choice5 = The skill on LT + B
hands.bow_draw_button.choice6 = The skill on LT + X
hands.bow_draw_button.choice7 = The skill on LT + Y
hands.bow_draw_button.choice8 = The skill on LT + RB
hands.bow_draw_start.label = Bow draw: the string is taken with
hands.bow_draw_start.tip = The trigger: as before. The grip: the natural grab - squeeze it at the string, pull, let go to shoot; a grip pressed away from the string keeps its other duties (the belt's potions, the shoulder swap, the wheel); at the string it is the draw's. Both: whichever is pressed first, and the draw is that one's. Live.
hands.bow_draw_start.choice0 = The trigger
hands.bow_draw_start.choice1 = The grip
hands.bow_draw_start.choice2 = The trigger or the grip
hands.bow_draw_nock.label = Bow draw: where the string is
hands.bow_draw_nock.tip = The string of the bow in your hand, read off the model where it rests (used when it lies 5 to 45 cm from the grip), or a fixed point 16 cm behind the grip along the bow. The touch radius round it is 28 cm either way. Debug > "Draw the bow draw's vectors" shows both points. Live.
hands.bow_draw_nock.choice0 = 16 cm behind the grip
hands.bow_draw_nock.choice1 = The bow's own string
hands.bow_draw_reach_cm.label = Bow draw: grab zone radius, cm
hands.bow_draw_reach_cm.tip = The radius of the green zone round the string (Debug > "Draw the bow draw's vectors" draws it at exactly this size, red outside, green once the free hand is in): the free hand has to be inside it when the trigger or grip is pressed. 28 = as it was. Smaller = nearer the string (a press elsewhere is not a draw more often). Live.
hands.bow_draw_nock_shift_cm.label = Bow draw: grab zone shift, cm
hands.bow_draw_nock_shift_cm.tip = Moves the centre of the green zone along the bow's axis: + away from the bow's grip (further toward you), - toward the grip. For the bow's own string and the fixed point alike - set it with the debug vectors on until the zone sits on the string you see. 0 = as it was. Live.
hands.bow_draw_min_pull_cm.label = Bow draw: the least pull that shoots, cm
hands.bow_draw_min_pull_cm.tip = How far the string hand has to be pulled back from where it took the string for a release to shoot (it also has to be 16 cm + this far from the bow hand, and held for 0.12 s). 12 = as it was; less = a short pull shoots, more = a longer one is needed. A shorter pull shoots nothing and the bow goes back to rest. Debug > "Draw the bow draw's vectors" draws a ring round the bow hand at the radius from which a release shoots: red until the free hand has pulled far enough, green after. Live.
bow.pitch_aim.label = Bow and crossbow: aim up and down (the shot goes to what its line meets)
bow.pitch_aim.tip = First person (F4), a bow or a crossbow in hand. The game's world is flat and raised ground is drawn pushed sideways - a monster a floor below you is drawn up to 2 m off its place in the game - so a shot aimed by its heading on the ground alone (as before) misses up and down the stairs. On: the shot's line (the draw's from the arrow, a crossbow's or a bow's from the hand) is followed until it meets a hostile monster's body or the ground, and the shot is turned to THAT monster's or that spot's place in the game. The game's own attack, animation, rate, mana and arrow, which flies on past the point as always - only its heading is chosen; no target is handed to the game, so the hero never runs after one. A line into the air: as before. Debug > "Bow: draw where the arrow goes" ends on what was met. Off: as before. Live.
bow.draw_shoots_arrow.label = Bow draw: the release shoots the bow's own arrow, whatever is on the A slot
bow.draw_shoots_arrow.tip = The bow draw's release presses the game's attack - the pad's A. The game casts whatever skill its A slot holds: a spell, a warcry or a melee skill there is cast instead, and no arrow flies (the string draws, nothing comes out). On: for the release's own press a skill on A that is not a bow skill is read as the plain Attack, the bow's own arrow; a bow skill on A (Multiple Shot, Strafe...) stays, and a skill armed from the quiver comes first. The A button itself, other weapons and the other slots are the game's as ever. Off: the release casts what the A slot holds. Live.
bow.arrow_flight.label = Bow: draw the shot arrow ourselves, from the bow along the shot's line
bow.arrow_flight.tip = First person (F4). The game draws its arrow flat, from the hero's chest. On: the arrow (or bolt) you shoot leaves the bow and flies along the shot's line - with "aim up and down" on, up or down to what the line met: a monster's body, or the ground (where it stays stuck when something stands near). It arrives when the game's own arrow does. It is the game's own arrow model, put where we draw it; the game's missile - its flight, its hit, its damage - is the game's. Multiple Shot's side arrows, Strafe's and Guided Arrow leave the bow and join their own path. Off: the game draws its arrows. Live.
bow.arrow_flight_straight.label = Bow: the drawn arrow flies straight along the shot's line
bow.arrow_flight_straight.tip = With "draw the shot arrow ourselves": an arrow whose line met nothing (aim up and down off, a shot into the air) flies straight along the line it was drawn along, from the bow - no bend. Off: it leaves the bow and swings onto the game's own path, which runs from your body beside the line, over the first 2.5 m. Side arrows of Multiple Shot and Strafe, and Guided Arrow, swing onto their own paths either way. Live.
bow.shot_line_hold.label = Bow draw: the shot keeps the line it was drawn along until the game takes it
bow.shot_line_hold.tip = The game reads a shot's aim when it takes the press - at once when the hero is free, else when his last attack is over. Until 0.179 the drawn line was the aim for 0.4 s and not while a new draw was held: a later shot took the bow hand's own pointing instead, and flew off to the side. On: the released shot's line stays its aim for 1.5 s, a new draw or not. The game's own attack, as ever. Live.
bow.rig_pose.label = The bow's string and limbs follow the drawing hand
bow.rig_pose.tip = On: with a bow in hand, while the string is drawn (the draw gesture), the game's own bow bones are posed from your hands - the string at the hand, the limbs folded to it, the arrow on the string - and snap back at the release. No bow is drawn over the game's: it is the game's bow, its bones moved; the shot, its aim and damage are the game's. Any bow a hero holds (15 models); a rig it does not know keeps the game's animation. Off: the game's own animation. F4 only.
bow.aim_along_hands.label = The bow lies along the line between the hands
bow.aim_along_hands.tip = On: while the string is taken, the bow, its arrow and the bow hand are turned until the bow points along the line from the string hand through the bow hand - the line the shot goes along - as a real bow does, instead of sitting in the hand turned the way the controller is. The hand and the forearm turn with it. It comes in and goes out smoothly at the take, the release and a cancel. The shot itself is as before. Off: the bow is turned like the controller. F4 only.
bow.aim_blend_ms.label = Bow along the hands: blend, ms
bow.aim_blend_ms.tip = How long the bow takes to swing onto the line when the string is taken, and back when it is let go or the pull is cancelled. Live.
bow.aim_roll.label = Bow along the hands: the bow's roll
bow.aim_roll.tip = About its own axis: the roll the bow controller has, or the limbs kept as upright as the aim lets them be. Live.
bow.aim_roll.choice0 = Follow the controller's roll
bow.aim_roll.choice1 = Keep the bow upright
bow.arrow_rest_model.label = The arrow rests where the bow model rests it
bow.arrow_rest_model.tip = On: the nocked arrow lies on the bow where the bow's own model lays its arrow - across the riser on the line from the string's place at rest, read off the bow's skeleton - beside the grip, not through it; the bow is turned along the line from the string hand through that point, and the shot goes along it. The three offsets below are only the fallback while the bow's bones are not read. Off: the point the offsets set in the hand's frame. Live. F4 only.
bow.arrow_rest_x_cm.label = Arrow rest X: along the bow, cm
bow.arrow_rest_x_cm.tip = The point the nocked arrow passes the bow hand at is FIXED in the hand's own frame, so it does not slide about as the hands move (now on the hand as it should be, now through the middle of the palm): this far from the hand's reference point. X: along the bow - + toward the target. The arrow, and the bow lying along the hands, lie on the line from the string hand through that point. Debug > "Draw the bow draw's vectors" shows it as an orange dot. All three 0 = through the reference point itself, as it was. It comes in and goes out with the draw over the blend time above. Live. F4 only.
bow.arrow_rest_y_cm.label = Arrow rest Y: across the bow, cm
bow.arrow_rest_y_cm.tip = Across the bow, the arrow's rest point on the bow hand: + toward the archer's left (the bow arm's side, for a bow held upright), - toward the right. See X above. Live.
bow.arrow_rest_z_cm.label = Arrow rest Z: up off the hand, cm
bow.arrow_rest_z_cm.tip = Up the bow's limbs, the arrow's rest point on the bow hand: + toward the upper limb, off the hand - the arrow lies above the knuckle and the thumb like on a real bow's shelf instead of through the palm. 5 is about the top of the fist. See X above. Live.
bow.arrow_rest_clear.label = Keep the arrow clear of the hand and the forearm
bow.arrow_rest_clear.tip = On: where the arrow's line would still pass through the bow hand, the wrist or the forearm - the string hand low or far to a side, the hand turned out - the arrow, and the nock with it, is lifted off the arm up the bow's limbs, by as little as clears it and at most 8 cm, parallel to the line (so the aim is not changed). Off: the point exactly as the three offsets put it. Live. F4 only.
bow.arrow_rest_aims.label = The shot goes through the arrow's rest point too
bow.arrow_rest_aims.tip = On: the shot's aim is the line from the string hand through the arrow's rest point - the line the arrow lies on and the bow is turned along, so the shot goes where the arrow points. Off: the shot as before - through the bow hand's reference point. Only matters while an offset above is not 0. Live. F4 only.
bow.hand_pose.label = The hand that takes the string: relaxed, fingers hooked on it
bow.hand_pose.tip = On: with a bow in hand, the hand that takes the string is relaxed (not the game's animation of it) and its fingers close on the string, the thumb loose: they follow the controller's trigger and grip, and the moment the string is taken they are hooked whatever the controls read; let go, they open. Without the draw gesture, as its grip closes. The bow hand keeps the game's animation. Off: the game's animation, as before.
bow.hook_game_pose.label = String hand: the game's own draw pose
bow.hook_game_pose.tip = On: the moment the string is taken the hand takes the pose of the game's own bow-draw animation - the fingers hooked on the string (the knuckles open, the last two joints of each finger curled), the thumb turned in - held as it is whatever the controller's grip and trigger read, and let go on the release. Not a fist. The Amazon's right hand only; any other keeps the closing below. Off: the hand closes by the amount below, as before. Live.
bow.hook_close.label = String hand: how far the fingers close, %
bow.hook_close.tip = The bend of the fingers on the string, 100 = a full fist's, from the same table the free hand's fist uses (it looks like a fist - the game's own pose above does not). Used with the game's draw pose off, for a rig that pose is not measured for, and for the squeeze before the string is taken. The thumb stays loose.
bow.hook_curl_pct.label = String hand: finger curl, % of the game's pose
bow.hook_curl_pct.tip = How far the four fingers bend in the game's draw pose: 100 = exactly as the game's own animation has them (the last two joints of each finger curled round the string), 0 = the open hand, more = tighter. For looking at it; the thumb has its own slider. Live.
bow.hook_thumb_deg.label = String hand: thumb in (+) / out (-), °
bow.hook_thumb_deg.tip = The thumb's base turned further in toward the palm and the fingers (+) or out (-) than the game's own draw pose has it, degrees. 0 = as the game's animation. Live.
bow.string_anchor.label = The string is held at the fingers' first joints
bow.string_anchor.tip = On: while the string is drawn it runs to the first joints of the index, middle and ring fingers instead of to the controller's grip point in the middle of the palm, a hand's length behind them (the string then met the base of the hand and hooked nothing). With the string hand's pose on (above) the joints are those of the hooked pose - the game's own draw pose, the Amazon's right hand; with it OFF they are those of the fingers as the game animates them, which for a bow in hand is the hook already. The arrow's nock and its line, and the bow's turn along the hands, start there. It comes in and goes out with the draw; the three offsets below move it. Off: the grip point, as before. Live. F4 only.
bow.string_anchor_along_cm.label = String at the fingers: along them, cm
bow.string_anchor_along_cm.tip = The string's place moved along the fingers: + toward the fingertips, - toward the wrist. 0 = at the middle of the first joints of index, middle and ring. Live.
bow.string_anchor_across_cm.label = String at the fingers: across them, cm
bow.string_anchor_across_cm.tip = The string's place moved across the hand: + toward the thumb and the index finger, - toward the little finger (the same on both hands). Live.
bow.string_anchor_palm_cm.label = String at the fingers: out of the palm, cm
bow.string_anchor_palm_cm.tip = The string's place moved out of the palm, the way the fingers curl: + into the crook of the curled fingers, - toward the back of the hand. 0.8 puts it on the finger's inner side, not through the middle of the bone. Live.
bow.quick_release.label = Quick release: the arrow leaves earlier in the attack (changes the game's timing)
bow.quick_release.tip = A CHANGE OF THE GAME'S TIMING (off when the key is missing; on in the settings that come with the mod). The game makes a bow's arrow at one frame of its attack animation (for an Amazon frame 6 of 14: 0.24 s after the animation starts, ~0.3 s after the release). On: that frame is moved earlier in the game's animation table, so the arrow is created ~0.2 s sooner INSIDE THE SAME ATTACK: the animation's length and the attack rate stay (the next attack cannot start earlier), the damage, mana and arrows are the game's, but they happen earlier, and a monster's hit in those first ~0.2 s no longer cancels the shot (it has left already). Only in VR first person with a bow in hand, and only offline (this game's own tables); it is put back exactly when you switch it off, change weapon or view, or leave the game. Live. [debug] bow_latency shows the arrow's create time.
bow.quick_release_frame.label = Quick release: the frame the arrow is made at
bow.quick_release_frame.tip = The animation frame (a frame is 0.04 s) the arrow is made at instead of the original (6 for an Amazon's bow; 7 to 11 for the others). 1 = the arrow leaves at once, 2 = as soon as the draw starts. A value at or past the original changes nothing. Live.
bow.quiver.label = Quiver: pick the arrow of the next shot (a bow)
bow.quiver.tip = On: the bow skill the next shot fires - Magic, Fire, Cold, Exploding, Ice, Guided, Freezing or Immolation Arrow, Multiple Shot, Strafe - is picked without the skill panel, from the skills the hero has learned (points or items; none learned: a short buzz and nothing else). It is the game's own skill setter, the one the skill panel uses: the same as picking the skill there, on the slot the shot presses (a bow's release: "Bow draw: the release presses" below). The arrow glows in the skill's colour while the string is drawn and the controller ticks at each change. The shot is the game's own - mana, arrows, attack rate unchanged. With the string draw: a button of the string hand while the string is drawn (B = the next, A = the previous; the [direct] quiver_next / quiver_prev lines of the ini change that), or the energy orbs along the bow below. Idea from the fork d2r-pcvr (bearstonem, MIT). Needs the game's controller layout. F4 only. Live.
bow.quiver_orbs.label = Quiver: energy orbs along the bow - touch one to pick the arrow
bow.quiver_orbs.tip = On: with a bow in hand, a row of glowing orbs hangs along its stave - one for the plain shot and one for every bow skill the hero has learned (points or items), each in its skill's colour; the skill the next shot fires is the bigger, brighter one. Reach the free hand to an orb and pull its trigger (below: or squeeze the grip): that skill is the next shot's (the game's own skill setter, as picking it in the skill panel; no direct cast). At an orb the trigger is the orb's - no shot, no draw - and the string is not taken there; anywhere else the trigger and the string are as always. The orbs sit on the bow's own stave (read off its bones, so they follow the bow) and never go: at rest, while the string is drawn, at the release (nothing is taken from them then). Needs the game's controller layout and the effect D2R_DepthFog.fx of this version. F4 only. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_trigger.label = Orbs: pick with the trigger (off: with the grip)
bow.quiver_orb_trigger.tip = On: the free hand's TRIGGER at an orb picks it; the grip does nothing there. The trigger a press took an orb with stays the orb's until you let go, so moving the hand off the orb with it down does not start the game's attack. Off: the grip picks, as the orbs first did (the trigger is then the string's and the game's as ever). Live.
bow.quiver_orb_size_cm.label = Orbs: size (radius), cm
bow.quiver_orb_size_cm.tip = How big each orb is drawn: its radius. The orb the skill slot holds is a quarter bigger, the one your hand is at is 1.6 times. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_reach_cm.label = Orbs: grab radius, cm
bow.quiver_orb_reach_cm.tip = How near your hand's grip point (the middle of the palm) has to be to an orb's middle for the orb to be the one your hand is at - it grows and brightens, and the grip takes it. Bigger than the orb on purpose: the fingers reach further than the palm's point. Where two reaches overlap the nearer orb wins. The log says how far the hand was when it found, left or took an orb. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_start_cm.label = Orbs: start up the stave, cm
bow.quiver_orb_start_cm.tip = Where the first orb (the plain shot) hangs, measured from the bow's grip along its stave toward the limb that points up. The others follow it up the stave. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_spacing_cm.label = Orbs: distance between orbs, cm
bow.quiver_orb_spacing_cm.tip = How far apart the orbs hang along the stave. A row that does not fit between the start and the limb's end is squeezed to fit. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_x_cm.label = Orbs: shift across the bow (x), cm
bow.quiver_orb_x_cm.tip = The whole row moved across the bow, + to the right of an upright bow. Along the bow's own axes, so it follows the bow when it is tilted. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_y_cm.label = Orbs: shift along the stave (y), cm
bow.quiver_orb_y_cm.tip = The whole row moved along the stave, + toward the limb that points up (up for an upright bow). Live.
bow.quiver_orb_z_cm.label = Orbs: shift toward the archer (z), cm
bow.quiver_orb_z_cm.tip = The whole row moved toward you (+) or away from you (-), on top of the clearance that keeps the orbs off the limb. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_rot_x_deg.label = Orbs: turn about x (across the bow), °
bow.quiver_orb_rot_x_deg.tip = The row turned about the axis across the bow, on its first orb (where the shifts above put it): + swings the far end of the row toward you, - away from you. The turns are about the bow's own axes, so they follow the bow when it is tilted. Applied in the order x, y, z. 0 = the row lies along the stave. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_rot_y_deg.label = Orbs: turn about y (along the stave), °
bow.quiver_orb_rot_y_deg.tip = The row turned about the stave's own axis, on its first orb. A row lying along the stave does not move for this alone; it swings a row that the x or z turn has tilted round the stave (+ toward the right of an upright bow, when the tilt is toward you). Applied after x, before z. Live.
bow.quiver_orb_rot_z_deg.label = Orbs: turn about z (toward the archer), °
bow.quiver_orb_rot_z_deg.tip = The row turned about the axis that points at you, on its first orb: + leans the far end of the row to the left of an upright bow, - to the right. Applied last, after x and y. 0 = the row lies along the stave. Live.
bow.arrow_fx_needs_mana.label = Arrow effects: out while the mana is short for the chosen arrow
bow.arrow_fx_needs_mana.tip = On: with an arrow skill chosen that the hero cannot pay - by the game's own numbers, the same as for the plain arrow below - the arrow looks plain: the fire, the frost or the arcane light goes out (and the small coloured glow), and lights again when the mana is back, at rest as much as while you pull. It is believed after 0.3 s and eases over 0.2 s, so it does not flicker when the mana is at the edge. Off: the effect stays whatever the mana. F4 only. Live.
bow.quiver_plain_no_mana.label = Quiver: no mana for the chosen arrow - shoot the plain arrow
bow.quiver_plain_no_mana.tip = On: with an arrow skill chosen (an orb, a button, the skill panel) and too little mana to pay it, the release is the game's plain attack: a normal arrow flies instead of the game's refusal (the hero saying "not enough mana" and nothing shot). The skill stays chosen, so when the mana is back the next release is the skill again. Whether the hero can pay is the game's own arithmetic on the game's own numbers - the skill's row in Skills.txt and its level against the hero's mana, less what our last cast took if the mana read has not caught up - never a guess; a skill this does not know is left to the game. The plain attack is pressed the game's way (its own attack button, the cast reading the slot as Attack): its checks, animation and arrows are the game's; nothing is called on the server. Off: the game's refusal, as it is. F4 only. Live.
bow.quiver_icon.label = Quiver: show the chosen arrow skill in the mana medallion
bow.quiver_icon.tip = The bow skill you chose (an orb, a quiver button, the skill panel) shows its icon - the game's own - on the bottom of the MANA medallion on your wrist, under the liquid, the way an armed melee skill does. Full while the hero can pay a shot with it (the release's own check: the skill's mana cost at his level against his mana); faint when he cannot. The plain arrow: no icon. Its size, depth and the two opacities are the sliders on the Skills tab ("Skill icon in the mana"). Needs the hand vitals as the medallions (the glass orbs look, the medallion shape) and the skill icons made from your game. Unticked: the medallion as before. Live. F4 only.
bow.arrow_fx.label = Arrow effects: fire, frost and arcane light on the arrow
bow.arrow_fx.tip = On: the arrow burns, freezes or crackles by the skill that is chosen - from the moment you choose it (an orb, a button, the game's own slot), nocked at rest, and through the draw; the plain shot has none - flames and rising embers for Fire, Exploding and Immolation Arrow; frost, ice crystals, glints and a falling mist for Cold, Ice and Freezing Arrow; an arcane glow with sparks circling the shaft for Magic Arrow. It is light the effect draws in the picture (D2R_DepthFog.fx of this version; nothing of the game's is created), in front of what is behind it and hidden by what is nearer: a hand, a sleeve. The skills that have no element of their own (the plain shot, Guided Arrow, Multiple Shot, Strafe) keep the small coloured glow, and with this off every skill does (while the string is drawn). It costs a few hundredths of a millisecond per eye on a fast card. The idea is bearstonem/d2r-pcvr's (MIT). F4 only. Live.
bow.arrow_fx_size_pct.label = Arrow effects: size, %
bow.arrow_fx_size_pct.tip = How big the flames, the frost and the glow are: 100 is a flame 4.5 cm round the arrow's head. Live.
bow.arrow_fx_bright_pct.label = Arrow effects: brightness, %
bow.arrow_fx_bright_pct.tip = How bright the effect is, on every skill together. The heavier skills (Exploding, Immolation, Ice, Freezing) are a little brighter than the rest already. Live.
bow.arrow_fx_along_cm.label = Arrow effects: along the arrow, cm
bow.arrow_fx_along_cm.tip = Moves the effect's centre along the arrow's shaft: more is forward, toward the arrowhead; less is back toward the string. 0 = where it is found. Fire, frost and arcane alike, on the arrow at rest and on the drawn one. Live.
bow.arrow_fire_cut.label = Arrow effects: out at the release
bow.arrow_fire_cut.tip = On: the fire, the frost or the arcane light goes out when the shot goes - the release of the string - and not a moment later when the game hides the arrow in your hand. It lights again on the next arrow: a new draw, the game showing an arrow again after the shot, another skill chosen. The delay below keeps it on the shot arrow that long. Only our own light on the arrow: the game's missile, its effects and its damage are the game's. Off: the effect stays until the game hides the arrow, as before. F4 only. Live.
bow.arrow_fire_cut_ms.label = Arrow effects: out at the release - after, ms
bow.arrow_fire_cut_ms.tip = How long after the release the effect goes out: 0 = at the release. A new draw, or the next arrow shown, before then lights it on that arrow. Live.

group.bow_without_the_string_draw_the_a_button_mode_above.help = Aiming a bow with the A button instead of the string draw. Tick to send arrows exactly along the hand with no auto-target, set how far out the aim point is, and correct the aim if arrows land beside where the hand points.
hands.bow_aim.label = Arrows along the hand, no auto-target
hands.bow_aim.tip = On: with a bow or a crossbow in hand, the attack and the bow's arrow skills go exactly along the hand: the game's auto-target and aim assist are off for that shot; its animation, attack rate and arrows stay the game's. Off: shots as before, the game may still snap to a monster near the aim.
