# --- Throws ---
group.throws = Throws
group.throws.help = Throwing javelins, knives, axes and potions in first person (F4): a swing of the hand by trigger or by grip, from either hand, with a gentle auto-aim cone. Set how far potions fly and where they explode, pick a javelin skill from your quiver, and let the missile leave earlier.
hands.throw_aim.label = Throws along the hand, no auto-target
hands.throw_aim.tip = On: javelins and throwing weapons (and their skills) go exactly along the hand, no auto-target. Off: the game's auto-target helps a throw find its target - a throw is hard to aim in VR.
hands.throw_gesture.label = Throw a javelin with a throwing motion
hands.throw_gesture.tip = Native OpenXR. On: with a javelin or a throwing weapon in the hand, hold the right trigger, swing the hand and let go - the hero throws it along the way the hand was going. The throw is the game's own attack: its missile, speed, ammunition and animation stay; the gesture only presses the attack at the release and aims it, no auto-target. A hand at rest, a slow swing, a jab with the trigger up or a trigger held too long throw nothing. The right trigger is the gesture's while such a weapon is in the hand - it does not attack on its own. Put the game's Throw skill on one of the pad's skill buttons (B X Y RB, or with the left trigger; the skill wheel does it): the throw presses that button - the game's Throw skill, a cast at a spot with no monster needed. The A attack cannot throw a potion at all and needs an enemy at the point for a knife, axe or javelin. Off: as before. F4 only.
hands.throw_by_grip.label = Throw by the grip: hold = in the hand, let go at the end of a swing = thrown
hands.throw_by_grip.tip = Native OpenXR with "Controls without BodyWalk", first person (F4). On: with a javelin or a throwing weapon in the hand the right GRIP is the weapon in your hand - squeezed, it is held, as long as you like. Swing the hand with the grip squeezed and let go of it at the end of the swing: the hero throws it along the way the hand was going - the game's own attack: its missile, speed, ammunition and animation stay; the gesture only presses the attack and aims it. A grip let go with the hand at rest, or after a slow movement, throws nothing. The right grip is the throw's while such a weapon is wielded: no belt bottle with it, no weapon swap behind the shoulder with that hand (the right stick click still swaps). On by default (it does nothing without native OpenXR and "Controls without BodyWalk"). The throw casts the game's own Throw skill by itself (the tick box below) - no skill button needed. Instead of the trigger gesture above. Off: as before.
hands.throw_left_hand.label = Throw from the left hand when the weapon is in the left hand
hands.throw_left_hand.tip = On: a javelin, throwing knife or axe in your LEFT hand is thrown with the LEFT controller - its grip or trigger and its swing, with the same rules as the right. Hand it over: take it with the left grip and let the right one go; the left grip is then the weapon in your hand (let go while the other hand still holds it and it is only handed back, not thrown). Hit by touch with it reads the left grip too. Without the weapon weight, a weapon put in the left slot. A weapon in each hand: a javelin beside an axe is thrown by its own hand (the other grip stays the axe's); with two javelins each hand throws its own. The game throws from its RIGHT slot whenever that slot holds a weapon: a javelin in the left slot beside an axe in the right cannot be thrown ("Impossible") - put the javelin in the right slot and hand it over to the left hand. That control is the throw's while its hand holds the javelin: no belt bottle, no shoulder swap, no quiver step with it; a hand that holds none (put down, thrown and not yet back) is free and takes a belt bottle. The game's own throw, as always. Off: as before - every throw is the right controller's. F4 only.
hands.throw_auto_skill.label = Throws use the Throw skill by themselves (no skill slot needed)
hands.throw_auto_skill.tip = The pad's A button is the game's Attack, which cannot throw a potion at all and throws a knife, axe or javelin only at an enemy. With a throwing weapon or potion in your hand the game's mouse already turns the plain attack into its Throw skill - a throw at a spot, no monster needed; this does the same for the throw's A press, so you do not have to put Throw on a skill button. The game's own cast, checks, animation and ammunition. Unticked: the throw presses the pad button of the skill slot that holds Throw (put it there with the skill wheel).
hands.throw_autoaim_deg.label = Throw auto-aim: cone round the throw's line, °
hands.throw_autoaim_deg.tip = A throw flies along the line your hand was going. This is a gentle help inside a narrow cone around that line - the HALF-angle of the cone, in degrees: a hostile monster that stands within it (and within the game's range, ahead of you) snaps the throw's aim point to itself - the one nearest the line. Nothing in the cone: exactly along your hand, no help at all. 0 = off, purely along the hand. The game's own attack takes the point: its range, line of sight and who counts as hostile stay the game's. For a throwing potion only monsters within a quarter of its landing distance count. One setting for the trigger and the grip throw. Live.
hands.throw_potion_reach_pct.label = Throwing potions: how far, % of the real throw
hands.throw_potion_reach_pct.tip = A throwing potion (Rancid Gas, Oil, Choking Gas, Exploding, Strangling Gas, Fulminating) is thrown to a spot on the ground: where a real object would land, thrown the way your hand moved at its fastest just before the release, from the height of your hand. This scales that distance: 100 = as it would really fly (a gentle swing in a room lands a few steps away on the game's screen); 800 (the default, the same as the weight tab's reach) = a comfortable swing of 3 - 5 m/s lands 15 - 25 m away; more if it still falls short. At least 3 and at most 48 cells (about 30 m) whatever it says - the game refuses a point farther off. With the weapon-weight tab on, the weight model works the throw out itself and this is not used. Live.
hands.potion_throw_ours.label = Throwing potions: our potion flies, the game's throw is hidden, the explosion where it lands
hands.potion_throw_ours.tip = ONE tick for a thrown potion that is only YOURS to see. A thrown potion is two things: your potion (the weapon-weight model's model) and the game's own throw - a missile that leaves the hero a third of a second after the release and flies straight to the spot. This turns on the three things that make it one: your potion flies the whole trajectory you threw it on and is the only potion you see (the tick "Your potion flies all the way" on the Weapon Weight tab); the game's own flying potion is not drawn ("The game's own flying potion is not drawn" below - only what is drawn changes, never the game's missile, its damage or its stack); and the game's own explosion (damage, gas, sound - the game's, untouched) happens where and when your potion lands ("explode where and when the potion lands" below, experimental). With it ticked the three are on whatever their own ticks say; unticked, each one decides by itself (the separate ticks stay for tuning). The weapon-weight tab must be on, the throw by gesture or by grip too. VR first person only. Live.
hands.potion_hide_game.label = The game's own flying potion is not drawn (while yours flies; experimental)
hands.potion_hide_game.tip = EXPERIMENTAL (off when the key is missing; on in the settings that come with the mod): its hide has not been proven in the game. A thrown potion's model is yours; the game also draws its own potion flying to the spot - a second one, a moment late. This takes that one out of the picture: only what is DRAWN changes - the game's missile still flies, hits, spends the stack and explodes as ever; its explosion is drawn. Only the hero's own thrown potion in the throw you just made, in VR first person, and only while your potion flies (the weapon-weight tab on and "Your potion flies all the way" ticked, or the tick above); another's missile, a trap's, an arrow are never touched. Needs the renderer's two functions to be found; if they are not, or one faults, it turns itself off for the session and the game's potion is drawn as before. The log says how many entities of it were hidden. Live.
hands.potion_throw_mode.label = Throwing potions: when the game's own throw happens
hands.potion_throw_mode.tip = A thrown potion is two things: the potion in your hand (the weapon-weight model's model) and the game's own throw - the Throw skill, a missile that leaves the hero's body after his throw animation (about a third of a second), flies straight to the spot at 25 cells a second and explodes there (the game's own explosion, damage and gas). "At once": the game's throw happens at the release; your potion is taken by it and vanishes. "When the potion lands": your potion flies the trajectory you threw it on (the weapon-weight tab must be on; its flight time is the wait) and when it lands the game's throw is made at the spot - the game's missile still has to fly there, so the explosion comes a moment after the landing (the throw animation, then the flight: about a second for a spot 20 cells away). Without the weight tab: at once. Live.
hands.potion_throw_mode.choice0 = at once (the game's potion flies and explodes)
hands.potion_throw_mode.choice1 = when the potion lands (it flies first, the game's throw follows)
hands.throw_direct.label = Throwing potions: explode where and when the potion lands (experimental)
hands.throw_direct.tip = A thrown potion is two things: your potion's model and the game's own missile. This ties them together: the game's throw is pressed at the release, so the hero's throw animation plays while your potion flies (the least input lag), and the one place in the game that creates its potion missile is told to start it on the way, so that it reaches the landing spot exactly as your potion lands - the game's own explosion (damage, gas, sound) happens there and then. Everything else is the game's own (the animation, the line-of-sight and mana gates, the stack). The weapon-weight tab must be on. Offline only. If the game's code is not found, or it faults once, it turns itself off for the session and the throw is as before. When your potion flies longer than the game's own potion would, the game's own flight is left alone. Unticked: as before. Live.
hands.throw_stand_still.label = Throws are pressed with the game's Stand Still
hands.throw_stand_still.tip = Like every attack of ours in first person, a throw's press holds the game's Stand Still (Shift), so it can never walk the hero. A throw is a cast at a spot and does not walk anyway: unticked, it is pressed without Stand Still. Live.
hands.javelin_quiver.label = Javelin quiver: choose the skill of the next throw
hands.javelin_quiver.tip = Native OpenXR with "Controls without BodyWalk", first person (F4). With a javelin or a throwing weapon in your weapon hand and a skill it allows learned (an Amazon's Poison Javelin, Lightning Bolt, Plague Javelin, Lightning Fury and the spear skills Jab, Power Strike, Impale, Charged Strike, Fend, Lightning Strike; a Barbarian's Double Throw with a thrown weapon in each hand; a Necromancer's Poison Dagger with a throwing knife), you pick the skill of the next throw from your quiver: reach a hand behind a shoulder (the javelin bag on your back) and tap its trigger - the right hand steps to the NEXT skill, the left to the PREVIOUS one, with a pulse in that hand (two pulses: back at the plain Throw). Only skills the hero has and the weapon in hand allows are offered; the choice is dropped when the weapon changes. The game's own cast does it: the pad's attack is read as the chosen skill, so mana, range, ammunition and the attack rate stay the game's. A blow in reach (Jab ...) is for the plain attack and the hit by touch; a throw by gesture stays the Throw then. A button bound in [direct] to action:quivernext / action:quiverprev steps it from anywhere. Needs the skill panel's reads (they run by themselves while a thrown weapon is in hand). On by default; it does nothing without native OpenXR and "Controls without BodyWalk". F4 only.
hands.javelin_quiver_reach.label = Javelin quiver: tap a trigger with a hand behind the shoulder
hands.javelin_quiver_reach.tip = On: the reach behind a shoulder (the volume of the weapon swap over the shoulder) with a trigger tap steps the choice - the trigger of a hand in the reach is the quiver's, not the attack's. Off: only a button bound to action:quivernext / action:quiverprev in [direct] steps it. Live.
hands.quick_throw.label = Quick throw: the missile leaves earlier in the throw animation (changes the game's timing)
hands.quick_throw.tip = A CHANGE OF THE GAME'S TIMING (off when the key is missing; on in the settings that come with the mod). The game makes a throw's missile - a potion, a javelin, a knife, an axe - at one frame of its throw animation (for an Amazon frame 9 of 16: 0.36 s after the animation starts), so after your own wind-up swing the hero winds up AGAIN before it flies. On: that frame is moved earlier in the game's animation table, so the missile is created ~0.3 s sooner INSIDE THE SAME THROW: the animation's length and the attack rate stay, the stack, mana and damage are the game's but happen earlier, and a monster's hit in those first ~0.3 s no longer cancels the throw (it has left already). It applies to every throw of your class whatever you hold, in VR first person only, and only offline (this game's own tables); it is put back exactly when you switch it off, change view, or leave the game. Never the bow's or a melee attack's animation. Live. [debug] bow_latency shows the missile's create time.
hands.quick_throw_frame.label = Quick throw: the frame the missile is made at
hands.quick_throw_frame.tip = The animation frame (a frame is 0.04 s) the missile is made at instead of the original (7 to 11 for the classes' throws). 1 is the earliest the game can act: frame 0 is never looked at when an animation starts, so it would throw nothing. A value at or past the original changes nothing. Live.
hands.quick_throw_potions.label = Quick throw: throwing potions too
hands.quick_throw_potions.tip = Off (the default): a throwing POTION keeps the game's own timing - the quick throw is put back while a potion is in your hand and back on with a javelin, knife or axe. A potion's missile is made at the throw's action frame and flies 25 cells a second, so its explosion comes about when your potion (the weapon-weight model's) lands; cut to the start, it comes ~0.3 s BEFORE your potion lands. On: potions are cut like the rest. Live.

# --- Crossbow ---
group.crossbow.help = How the crossbow is held and aimed in first person (F4): held like the staff with the left hand on the stock, where the left hand sits, shooting along the drawn barrel or a shot line, and the aim point and correction. Some options are not finished yet and are off in the settings that come with the mod.
bow.xbow_two_hands.label = Crossbow held like the staff
bow.xbow_two_hands.tip = The right hand holds the crossbow on the stock and aims it alone; the left takes it with the grip (ahead of the right) and then it aims along the line from the right hand to the left. Off: as a bow, the game's own animation.
hands.xbow_hand.label = The game hangs the crossbow on
hands.xbow_hand.tip = For its grip: if the crossbow sits wrong or turns away when the left hand takes it, try the other.
hands.xbow_hand.choice0 = the right wrist
hands.xbow_hand.choice1 = the left wrist
hands.xbow_hold_grip.label = Crossbow: the right hand holds it by its grip
hands.xbow_hold_grip.tip = The crossbow sits in the holding palm by its trigger grip - where the game's own trigger hand holds it in the game's two-handed hold (learned from the game's pose a moment after the crossbow is in hand) - not by the bone it hangs on. The log says once how far the two are apart. Unticked: as before. F4 only. Still being corrected: in a test (2026-10-18) the crossbow's grip was still off.
hands.xbow_support_game.label = Crossbow: left hand on the game's own fore-grip
hands.xbow_support_game.tip = The left hand takes the crossbow at its fore-grip, where the game's own hand that carries it holds it in the game's two-handed hold - learned from the game's pose a moment after the crossbow is in hand, nothing set by hand. Until then (and unticked) the place under the drawn barrel, or the shot line. The log says once where it is and how the game's palm faces the stock. F4 only. Not finished: in a test (2026-10-18) it did not work yet, so it is off in the settings that come with the mod.
hands.xbow_support_close.label = Crossbow: the left hand closes on the stock
hands.xbow_support_close.tip = On the game's own fore-grip the left hand takes the game's own fore-grip hand's turn and finger pose (the game's left hand; mirrored when the right hand supports) - the palm toward the stock, the fingers closed round it - instead of the controller's turn with an open hand. Unticked: as before. F4 only. Not finished: in a test (2026-10-18) it did not work yet, so it is off in the settings that come with the mod.
hands.xbow_barrel_forward.label = Crossbow: its barrel along the controller
hands.xbow_barrel_forward.tip = The crossbow is laid by its own drawn barrel: the barrel points where the controller points and the crossbow's top is the controller's top - not by a bone axis, which tilted it about 34 degrees up and a little aside in the hand. Until the barrel is read (a moment after the crossbow is in hand) as before. F4 only. Not finished: in a test (2026-10-18) it did not work yet, so it is off in the settings that come with the mod.
hands.xbow_handover.label = Crossbow: pass it from hand to hand
hands.xbow_handover.tip = Take the crossbow with the free hand anywhere (the fore-grip) and let go of the grip of the hand that held it: it stays in the other hand. Or squeeze the free hand's grip anew near the holding hand (within 25 cm, nearer it than the fore-grip), and the crossbow is in that hand; the other one lets go and is free - squeeze it at the fore-grip to support the crossbow there (mirrored). The shot follows the barrel of the hand that holds it. Only how it is held and aimed: the game's weapon slots and attack are its own. Another weapon or the tick off: back in the right hand. F4 only. Not finished: in a test (2026-10-18) the hand-over did not work yet, so it is off in the settings that come with the mod.
hands.xbow_aim_barrel.label = Crossbow: shoot along the drawn barrel
hands.xbow_aim_barrel.tip = The bolt goes where the crossbow you see points: along its barrel as the model is drawn (its bolt helper bone, as bearstonem/d2r-pcvr aims) - no correction by hand, raised or rolled alike. The game's own bolt, damage, ammunition and rate of fire are unchanged: only the direction of the game's attack is steered, as the shot line does. While the barrel is not read (an unknown model, a moment after a swap) the shot line below is used. Unticked: the shot line. F4 only.
hands.xbow_line_pitch.label = Crossbow: shot line, tilt up/down, °
hands.xbow_line_pitch.tip = Turns the line the bolt flies along and the left hand takes - the red line ([debug] phantom_ray) - not the model. Lay it on the crossbow. With "shoot along the drawn barrel" ticked it is only the stand-in while the barrel is not read.
hands.xbow_line_yaw.label = Crossbow: shot line, turn left/right, °
hands.xbow_left_at_cm.label = Crossbow: left hand ahead, cm
hands.xbow_left_at_cm.tip = The one place the left hand takes the crossbow (under the stock, just behind the bow); it does not slide. The grip takes it only with the left hand that near this place.
hands.xbow_left_roll.label = Crossbow: left hand roll, °
hands.xbow_left_roll.tip = The left hand on the crossbow turned round the stock: from below, palm up, holding it up.
hands.xbow_left_x.label = Crossbow: left hand X, cm
hands.xbow_left_x.tip = The left hand on the crossbow moved along its own axes, until it sits under the stock.
hands.xbow_left_y.label = Crossbow: left hand Y, cm
hands.xbow_left_z.label = Crossbow: left hand Z, cm
hands.xbow_grip_latch.label = Crossbow: left grip lets go cleanly
hands.xbow_grip_latch.tip = The left hand holds the crossbow while the left grip is squeezed - it may be squeezed first and then brought to the stock. It lets go at once when you swap weapons or the hero's model changes, and when the left controller loses tracking (the hand stays free: no jump onto the stock). A squeeze still held from the shoulder weapon swap takes nothing: let go and squeeze again. No grip reading from the bridge = not held. Unticked: as before (the grip takes it near the place; a lost controller puts the hand on the stock). F4 only. The shot is not changed.
hands.xbow_wrist_tracked.label = Crossbow: left wrist follows the controller
hands.xbow_wrist_tracked.tip = The left hand on the crossbow keeps your controller's turn - hold the stock from below, palm up, or from above, as you like - and its palm's middle sits on the place. Unticked: the hand is turned into the game's grip round the stock (the roll slider turns it). The left hand X/Y/Z and roll sliders still act on top. F4 only.
hands.xbow_grip_wide.label = Crossbow: take the grip right after a swap
hands.xbow_grip_wide.tip = The game's grip of the crossbow is taken even from a pose with the hands far apart (the idle right after a swap from a shield set), since the crossbow is placed by the controller anyway - before, the left hand could not take it until a pose with the hands together (a shot). Needs "left wrist follows the controller". F4 only.
hands.xbow_support_model.label = Crossbow: left palm under the drawn barrel
hands.xbow_support_model.tip = The left palm goes under the crossbow's barrel as the model is drawn (its bolt helper bone), "palm behind the limbs" behind the front of the stock and "palm below the barrel" under it - each crossbow its own. Unticked: on the shot line set by eye. The bolt still flies along the shot line: only the hand moves. The log says whether the barrel was read ("crossbow barrel"). F4 only.
hands.xbow_support_drop_adj_cm.label = Crossbow: palm lower (+) / higher, cm
hands.xbow_support_drop_adj_cm.tip = A fine adjustment around 0: the palm's middle sits 7 cm under the drawn barrel (as d2r-pcvr); + lower, - higher.
hands.xbow_support_back_adj_cm.label = Crossbow: palm back (+) / forward, cm
hands.xbow_support_back_adj_cm.tip = A fine adjustment around 0: the palm sits 6 cm behind the front of the stock, where the bow's limbs meet it (as d2r-pcvr); + farther back, - forward. With the palm under the drawn barrel ticked, "left hand ahead" is not used.
bow.xbow_range_one.label = Crossbow aim point, one hand, cells
bow.xbow_range_one.tip = How far out along the aim the attack point is with the right hand alone: nearer = rougher, the crossbow sways more.
bow.xbow_range_two.label = Crossbow aim point, two hands, cells
bow.xbow_range_two.tip = The same with the left hand on it too: farther = finer, held in two the aim is steady.
bow.xbow_aim_yaw.label = Crossbow aim correction, ° (+ = right)
bow.xbow_aim_yaw.tip = The same for a crossbow, in place of the bow's: it is held like a gun, not round a bow's grip.

# --- Staff: aim point and correction ---

group.staff_aim_point_and_correction.help = How far out along a staff, wand, orb or bare hand a spell's aim point goes, in cells, with one hand or two. Farther = finer aim; below 3 the game's own point is used.
bow.staff_range_one.label = Staff aim point, one hand, cells
bow.staff_range_one.tip = The staff's, with the right hand alone.
bow.staff_range_two.label = Staff aim point, two hands, cells
bow.staff_range_two.tip = The staff's, with the left hand on it too.
bow.caster_range.label = Wand or orb aim point, cells
bow.caster_range.tip = VR first person (F4), with Auto-target's "Aim spells by the drawn hand or staff": how far out along the wand or orb a spell's point goes - farther = finer steps of the aim (the game's own point is about 3 cells, a 20-degree staircase). Below 3: the game's own point. A staff has the two above.
bow.hand_range.label = Bare hands aim point, cells
bow.hand_range.tip = The same for a spell cast with bare hands (or with any weapon that is not a staff, wand or orb): how far out along the hand its point goes. Below 3: the game's own point.

# --- Aim distance by the arm ---
group.aim_distance_by_the_arm = Aim distance by the arm
group.aim_distance_by_the_arm.help = In F4 a spell's aim distance follows how far your arm is stretched: at the body it lands near (a wide fan of Teeth), stretched out at the weapon's own distance. Set the near distance, and correct a staff's aim if spells land beside where it points.
bow.aim_distance_by_arm.label = A spell's aim distance follows how far the arm is stretched
bow.aim_distance_by_arm.tip = VR first person (F4), spells only: a wand, an orb, a staff held in one hand, bare hands. As in flat Diablo, where a click near the hero spreads Teeth wide and one far away keeps it in a tight cone: here an arm held at the body gives the near distance below, an arm stretched out along the aim gives the weapon's own distance (the wand, orb and bare-hand sliders above; for a staff the two-hand one). The stretch is measured on your own arm - the drawn shoulder and the length to the grip, fitted to your T-pose span or your height - and smoothed a little. A staff with only one hand on it follows the arm too; a staff held in BOTH hands always aims at its far distance, the tightest cone, whatever the arm does. A bow, a crossbow and throws keep their fixed distance. It only chooses where the game's own spell is aimed, as a click would. Off: the distances above, as before. Live.
bow.aim_near_cells.label = Aim point with the arm at the body, cells
bow.aim_near_cells.tip = How near a spell's aim point comes with the arm at the body (the far end is the weapon's own distance). Smaller = a wider fan of Teeth and the like. Live.
bow.staff_aim_yaw.label = Staff aim correction, ° (+ = right)
bow.staff_aim_yaw.tip = The same for a staff, in place of the one above: turns its aim about the vertical, if spells land beside where the staff points. In VR F4 with Auto-target's "Aim spells by the drawn hand or staff" on, only when that has no fresh pose (the staff's own axis needs no correction).

hands.forearm_twist_share.label = Forearm's share of the roll
hands.forearm_twist_share.tip = How much of the wrist's roll the forearm takes at the elbow end: 0 = none there (the hand and the wrist end turn), 1 = the whole forearm turns as one with the hand. Toward the wrist it always grows to all of it. Live.

# --- Barbarian Leap ---
group.barbarian_leap = Barbarian Leap
group.barbarian_leap.help = Where the Barbarian's Leap and Leap Attack land, in VR first person (F4) only. Ticked, they go where you look instead of where the hand or cursor points; the second tick lets you hold for an arc and let go to leap into its circle.
gameplay.leap_by_gaze.label = Barbarian: Leap and Leap Attack go where you look
gameplay.leap_by_gaze.tip = VR first person (F4) only. Cast Leap or Leap Attack with its own key or slot as ever: the hero leaps to where the headset's gaze meets the ground, not where the hand or the game's cursor points. Leap Attack leaps at the monster the gaze is on, if there is one. A gaze that meets no ground within the skill's range (looking ahead or up) leaps the full range that way. Only the cast's point (or monster) is ours: its range, cooldown, mana and the leap itself are the game's. Off: the game's own aim, as before. Live.
gameplay.leap_arc.label = Barbarian: Leap and Leap Attack by the arc too
gameplay.leap_arc.tip = VR first person (F4) only. On (with the point skills below on): Leap and Leap Attack work like them - hold for the arc from your weapon (or hand), let go to leap into the circle; Leap Attack goes at the monster at the circle. A tap stays where you look. Off: Leap and Leap Attack go where you look, as before. Live.
gameplay.leap_arc_head.label = Barbarian: the leap's arc from the belly, aimed by the head
gameplay.leap_arc_head.tip = With the leap's arc on: it leaves from the middle of the hero's belly and you aim it with your head - raise the head to land farther, lower it to land nearer, turn it to turn the landing (never past the leap's own range). Off: the arc leaves your weapon or hand, as the other point skills'. Live.
gameplay.leap_head_gain.label = Barbarian: how far a tilt of the head reaches
gameplay.leap_head_gain.tip = The head's tilt is multiplied by this before it aims the leap's arc: 2 lands as far with half the tilt, so a small raise of the head already reaches far; 1 = the head's own tilt. The farthest is still the leap's own range. Live.

# --- Point skills (arc and circle) ---
group.point_skills_arc_and_circle = Point skills (arc and circle)
group.point_skills_arc_and_circle.help = Aim skills cast on a spot (Teleport, Fire Wall, Meteor, Blizzard, curses...) with an arc in F4: a tap casts where you look, hold to see an arc and a circle, let go to cast into it. The sliders set how far the circle goes, how high the arc rises, its colour and how strongly it is drawn.
gameplay.teleport_circle.label = Point skills (Teleport, Fire Wall, Meteor...): hold for an arc and a circle
gameplay.teleport_circle.tip = VR first person (F4) only, the skill on one of the pad's skill buttons (B, X, Y, RB, A or RT, with or without the left trigger). A tap casts where you look. Held, nothing is cast yet: a red arc leaves the tip of your staff (or your hand) and a circle sits where it lands - raise the hand to throw it farther, lower it to bring it nearer; let go and the skill is cast into the circle. Teleport, Fire Wall, Meteor, Blizzard, Hydra, the curses, Bone Wall, the golems, Fissure, Volcano, the Assassin's traps and Mind Blast, the Warlock's sigils and demons (the list: [gameplay] point_skills in the ini). gameplay.point_max_cells.label = Point skills: the circle's farthest, cells
gameplay.point_max_cells.tip = How far from the hero the circle may go, in the game's cells (about 0.6 m each). The game refuses a point 50 cells off, so 48 is used at most. Live.
gameplay.point_arc_height.label = Point skills: how high the arc rises, %
gameplay.point_arc_height.tip = How high the arc is drawn above the straight line from the staff to the circle: 100 = a real throw's height (it rose about 8 m at the farthest), 0 = a straight line. Only the drawing - where the circle lands stays the same for the same hand. Live.
gameplay.point_arc_color.label = Point skills: one colour for all
gameplay.point_arc_color.tip = With "a colour for each skill" off: the colour of every skill's energy beam and glowing circle. Empty (x) = red. Live.
gameplay.point_arc_opacity.label = Point skills: the arc's opacity, %
gameplay.point_arc_opacity.tip = How strong the arc and the circle are drawn: 0 = not at all, 100 = full. Live.
gameplay.point_arc_by_skill.label = Point skills: a colour for each skill
gameplay.point_arc_by_skill.tip = On: each skill's arc and circle in its own colour - the one below (set for every skill: fire orange, lightning light blue, cold a deep icy blue, the curses plum and blood red ...); a row emptied (x) takes its element's from the game's data. Off: every skill in the colour above. Live.

# --- Melee skills armed by their button (F4) ---
group.melee_skills_armed_by_their_button_f4 = Melee skills armed by their button (F4)
group.melee_skills_armed_by_their_button_f4.help = With Hit by touch in F4, a melee skill's pad button (Bash, Zeal, Jab...) arms it instead of casting it: your next hits are that skill, paid with its mana. Choose one blow or every blow, show the armed skill's icon in the mana medallion, and tick below which skills are armed this way.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed.label = A melee skill's button arms it: every hit is that skill
gameplay.melee_skill_armed.tip = Hit by touch on (F4 only), a melee weapon or fists swung. A press of a pad skill button (B, X, Y, RB, with or without LT) whose slot holds a melee attack skill - Bash, Stun, Concentrate, Berserk, Frenzy, Double Swing; Zeal, Smite, Sacrifice, Vengeance, Conversion; Jab, Fend, Impale, Power Strike, Charged Strike, Lightning Strike; Maul, Fire Claws, Hunger, Rabies, Fury, Feral Rage; Tiger Strike, Dragon Talon, Dragon Claw, Fists of Fire, Cobra Strike, Claws of Thunder, Blades of Ice, Dragon Tail, Royal Strike; Poison Dagger; Cleave (the skills the game's Skills.txt gives melee range) - no longer casts it: it ARMS it, like the bow's chosen arrow skill (a short buzz in both hands). Every touch of your blade is then the game's attack with that skill: its mana, cooldown, weapon check and animation are the game's, the monster you touched its target, one touch one cast. When the hero cannot pay its mana, that touch is the plain attack and the skill stays armed. The same button again, or a button with the plain attack on it, disarms; another melee skill's button arms that one. Which skills: the ticks of "Armed by its button" below (these are ticked; Whirlwind, Charge, Leap Attack and Dragon Flight are there unticked). Spells, buffs, warcries and an unticked skill cast from their buttons as ever, and a bow, a crossbow or a thrown weapon is not touched. Needs the plain attack on the attack button (A). The log says what was armed and what each touch was ("melee armed: ..."). Not tried in the game yet. Unticked: the skill buttons cast as before. Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_arm_once.label = ... for ONE blow: the next hit is the skill, then plain hits
gameplay.melee_skill_arm_once.tip = The skill's button arms it for the NEXT blow only: swing, and the first touch the game casts as that skill spends it - its icon leaves the mana medallion, and the hits after it are the plain attack until you press the button again. So you swing for the skill, and not every swing is the skill. With too little mana that touch is the plain attack and the skill stays armed. Not used within the seconds below, it disarms by itself (a soft buzz). The same button again disarms. Nothing is cast without a swing: the press never reaches the game. Warcries and spells cast from their buttons at once, as ever. Unticked: an armed skill stays armed and every hit is that skill. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_skill_arm_once_s.label = One blow: disarmed when not used within, s
gameplay.melee_skill_arm_once_s.tip = How long a skill armed for one blow waits for that blow. Then it disarms (a soft buzz) and the next hit is the plain attack. 0 = it waits for ever. Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon.label = Show the armed skill in the mana medallion
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon.tip = The armed skill's icon - the game's own, the one the skill panel shows - lies on the bottom of the MANA medallion on your wrist, under the blue liquid, cut to a circle inside the glass. Full while the hero can pay the next hit with it (the same check the hit makes: the skill's mana cost at his level against his mana); half see-through when he cannot - the next hit will be the plain attack - and bright again when the mana is back. Nothing armed: no icon. Needs the life and mana on the hands as the medallions (Hand vitals: the glass orbs look, the medallion shape) and the skill icons made from your game (the skill wheel's). Unticked: the medallion exactly as before. Not tried in the game yet. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_size_pct.label = Skill icon in the mana: size, % of the inner circle
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_size_pct.tip = How big the skill's icon in the mana medallion is: a percent of the medallion's inner circle (the glass dome's foot). 87.5 = as it first was; 100 = the whole floor under the glass. For the armed melee skill's icon and the bow's chosen arrow skill's (Weapon Adjust > Bow, "Quiver: show the chosen arrow skill in the mana medallion"). Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_depth_pct.label = Skill icon in the mana: depth, % (100 = the bottom)
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_depth_pct.tip = How deep in the medallion the icon lies: 100 = on the very bottom, under all the liquid (as it first was); 0 = as high as it fits - its rim just under the glass, over the liquid when the mana is low. It is the dome's own shape: the bigger the icon, the less room over it (at 100% size it can only lie on the bottom). Seen from the side it shifts against the floor like a real thing in the glass. Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_lift_mm.label = Skill icon in the mana: over the floor, mm
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_lift_mm.tip = How far over where the depth puts it the icon lies, in millimetres: 1 = just off the medallion's floor, so the floor's texture does not show through it; 0 = on the floor itself. Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_opacity_pct.label = Skill icon in the mana: opacity, %
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_opacity_pct.tip = How solid the icon is while the hero can pay the next hit (the shot, for a bow): 100 = fully (as it first was), 0 = not seen. Live.
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_faint_pct.label = Skill icon in the mana: opacity when the mana is short, %
gameplay.melee_skill_armed_icon_faint_pct.tip = How solid the icon is while the hero CANNOT pay the next hit - the hit will be the plain attack (the bow: the plain arrow, or the game's refusal). 35 = as it first was; 0 = it goes out until the mana is back. The icon eases between the two opacities. Live.

# ===== Tab: Strikes =====
tab.strikes = Strikes

# --- Hit by touch ---
group.hit_by_touch = Hit by touch
group.hit_by_touch.help = The main switch for hitting by swinging your weapon in F4: the blade passing through a monster presses the game's own attack at it. The sliders set how fast and how far the blade must move to count; you can also let thrown weapons hit by touch and stop the trigger from attacking.
gameplay.melee_touch.tip = First person (F4), the arms on the controllers, a melee weapon (or bare fists) in hand: the blade you swing through a monster's body picks the target and the moment of the game's own attack - it is pressed on the contact and aimed at the monster you touched. The game does the rest: its animation, its reach (out of reach it walks the hero up, as a click on a monster does), its hit rolls and speed. A blade held still or waved slowly does nothing; a swing hits a monster once. The skill on the attack button is what is pressed - a spell there is cast at the monster you touched. Works with BodyWalk's tracking and with native OpenXR. Off: as before. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_min_speed.label = Hit by touch: the least blade speed that hits, m/s
gameplay.melee_min_speed.tip = How fast the blade must be moving for a contact to count. A blade moving slower than this does nothing, however it touches a monster - so a gentle poke hits only if this is low. The same number for every weapon (the weapon's own blade is its only difference); the default 0.8 is what it always was. The speed is the BLADE's, measured on the weapon as drawn, frame to frame (the faster of its two ends - the tip of a sword - and at a touch the speed of the point that touches: the tip of a blade swinging about your hand is fast, the end you hold is not) - not your hand's, so a grip at the root or in the middle, a big arc with a still wrist and a poke all read what the blade really does. A monster is hit once per stroke, at its first contact. A normal swing's tip reads about 3-6 m/s: tick "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" (Debug group below) and the blade turns green while its fastest part moves at least that fast (a touch counts with the part that touches, the tip), back to cyan when it slows; the log line "melee boxes:" shows the blade's speed and its peak against this number. Lower, and the speed that may begin a stroke and the speed that counts as rest go lower with it; from 0.8 up the rest is as before. Only decides when the touch presses the game's own attack - never its reach, rolls or the attack itself. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_stroke_start_cm.label = Hit by touch: how far the blade moves to start a stroke, cm
gameplay.melee_stroke_start_cm.tip = A movement is a stroke - and can hit - only after the blade (its faster end: the tip of a sword, as drawn - not the hand) has moved this far within about a tenth of a second, and fast enough (above). Smaller: a short jab counts; larger: only a long swing does. A blade moving slower than the least speed above does nothing, a monster is hit once per stroke. Default 8 as before. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_touch_thrown.label = Thrown weapons hit by touch too (a point-blank throw)
gameplay.melee_touch_thrown.tip = A javelin, a throwing knife or a throwing axe in hand is swung like any weapon: its blade through a monster's body presses the game's own attack at it - for a thrown weapon that is the game's Throw at that monster, point blank, with the ammunition spent as the game spends it (never the Direct hit route). Throwing potions are not swung. The throw by gesture (Weapon Adjust > Throws: by the grip or the trigger) stays as it is and does not fire together with the touch: with the grip throw on, the touch counts only while the right grip is squeezed on the weapon; for 0.7 s after a throw is released the touch stands down; and a touch that pressed the attack drops the release of the same swing (one throw per swing). The blade's size per weapon is an estimate - tune it with the blade sliders of the Debug group below and "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch". Unticked: a thrown weapon does nothing by touch, as before. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_touch_barrels.label = Break barrels and pots by hitting them
gameplay.melee_touch_barrels.tip = A swing of the held weapon through a barrel, a pot, an urn or a basket breaks it the game's own way: the swing (one that would hit a monster) presses the game's interact on that object, as A does, so the hero kicks or breaks it with his own animation - its loot, traps and explosions are the game's. Chests, doors, shrines and quest objects keep their normal controls, and A still works. The object's size is an estimate from its footprint. Unticked: as before, only A breaks them. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_touch_thrown_held.label = A thrown weapon is the weapon in your hand from the start (no grip needed to hit)
gameplay.melee_touch_thrown_held.tip = A javelin, a throwing knife or a throwing axe is the weapon in your hand from the moment it is equipped, like a sword: it hits by touch at once - you do not have to squeeze the grip first. Put down (the grip squeezed and let go with the hand at rest) it hits nothing until a hand holds it again, as a sword. The throw is the same: squeeze the grip, swing, let go - the game's own throw; the touch still stands down for 0.7 s after a throw and one swing throws once. Unticked: as before - with the grip throw on, a thrown weapon hits by touch only while its grip is squeezed. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_touch_only.label = The trigger does not attack (only the blade's touch; a bow or a crossbow shoots with it)
gameplay.melee_touch_only.tip = A part of hit by touch, on with it: a trigger that attacks lets you skip the swing and just pull it, which is a bug of hit by touch, not an option. First person (F4), hit by touch on, the plugin's own controls (Stereo > Native OpenXR > Controls without BodyWalk): the trigger's attack is not passed to the game - only the blade's touch attacks. That is every weapon the touch swings: melee weapons, bare hands and throwing weapons (javelins, throwing knives and axes - the touch or the throw gesture throws them); only a BOW and a CROSSBOW keep the trigger (they are shot, not swung). Spells and skills on the other buttons (B, X, Y, RB, the skill wheel) are as they were. Only OUR controller press is withheld; nothing of the game is blocked or hooked, and everything else the trigger is bound to works as bound (a skill button, a command). The trigger works as ever where hit by touch does not run: no tracking, a menu or a panel up, another view, a throwing weapon with its touch off, a throwing potion. With BodyWalk's own input (not the plugin's) the trigger is BodyWalk's and this cannot reach it. The log says what it decided ("melee touch only: ..."). Unticked: the trigger attacks as it did before - the way back. Live. F4 only.

# --- Strike by force (F4, a weapon held with weight) ---
group.strike_by_force_f4_a_weapon_held_with_weight = Strike by force (F4, a weapon held with weight)
group.strike_by_force_f4_a_weapon_held_with_weight.help = A test: with a weapon that has weight, a hit counts by how hard the blow lands rather than by the blade's speed. The sliders set the threshold for blunt, edged and piercing weapons; Cleave lets a hard swing cut on into the next monster.
weight.strike_by_force.label = Hit by the strike's force, not the blade's speed (a test)
weight.strike_by_force.tip = Live. A weapon held with weight counts a hit by what its strike puts into the monster's body - the blow's arrival and your hands' drive in the first 0.15 s (two hands are stronger), for an edged weapon its cut along the body too - against a threshold from the weapon's own weight (the sliders below). A light touch is no hit; a weapon with no hand on it (falling, lying on a monster) never hits. The press is the game's own attack, once a strike on each monster; only the head hits, the butt and the monsters' shields stop it, as before. Unticked: the blade's speed judges, as before.
weight.strike_force_general_pct.label = Strike force: the threshold, %
weight.strike_force_general_pct.tip = Live. All weapons' thresholds at once: higher - only hard blows count; lower - lighter ones do too. 100: the author's recorded blows (every touch refused, three quarters of real blows counted).
weight.strike_force_blunt.label = Strike force: blunt (maces, staves, clubs), N s per kg
weight.strike_force_blunt.tip = Live. A blunt weapon's threshold: this x its steel kg ^ the mass exponent (a 1.2 kg club: 1.65 N s).
weight.strike_force_edged.label = Strike force: edged (swords, axes, polearms, daggers), N s per kg
weight.strike_force_edged.tip = Live. An edged weapon's threshold: this x its steel kg ^ the mass exponent (a 0.9 kg short sword: 1.03 N s; a 3 kg large axe 1.9). Its cut counts toward it.
weight.strike_force_piercing.label = Strike force: piercing (spears, javelins), N s per kg
weight.strike_force_piercing.tip = Live. A piercing weapon's threshold: this x its steel kg ^ the mass exponent (a 0.7 kg spear: 1.29 N s).
weight.strike_force_mass_exp.label = Strike force: how much the weight raises it
weight.strike_force_mass_exp.tip = Live. The power of the steel's kg in the threshold: 0 - one threshold for every weight; 1 - in proportion to it; 0.5 (the default) - the recorded blows: a heavy weapon's blow is not that much harder, your hands set most of it.
weight.strike_force_cut_weight.label = Strike force: an edge's cut, N s per J
weight.strike_force_cut_weight.tip = Live. What a joule of an edged weapon's cut (the body's push times the slide along it) counts for: higher - a cut drawn along the body counts sooner; 0 - only the blow into it.
weight.strike_force_floor_ns.label = Strike force: never under, N s
weight.strike_force_floor_ns.tip = Live. No weapon's threshold is lower than this (a touch is 0 - 1 N s).
weight.strike_force_shared.label = Strike force: a blow shared between monsters counts on each
weight.strike_force_shared.tip = Live. A blade caught between two monsters gives each less: their sum is judged, and each whose share is at least a quarter of it gets the hit. Unticked: each alone.
weight.strike_force_stuck.label = Strike force: stuck in and pushed - the hit repeats (a test)
weight.strike_force_stuck.tip = Live. Ticked: while the weapon stays in the body and you keep pushing it, the hit repeats - each when the game's own attack is over. Unticked: one hit a strike, however long it stays in.
weight.cleave.label = Cleave: a strong strike cuts through into the next monster
weight.cleave.tip = Live. A hard blow is not stopped at the first monster: its body takes the blow, gets its hit (the game's own attack) and the weapon goes on through into the next, a little slower - each monster passed spends some of the stroke's force, so a hard two-handed swing cuts through three Fallen, not a crowd of ten. A light blow stops on the first, a thrust still sticks into the first, a monster's shield or weapon still stops it. Only blades - a dagger, a sword, an axe, a polearm - and only a fast swing (the speed below); a staff, a maul, a mace or a club always stops on the body. Unticked: every monster stops the weapon, as before.
weight.cleave_over.label = Cleave: how hard, x the strike's threshold
weight.cleave_over.tip = Live. The blow's arrival a monster's body must take to be cut through, times the weapon's strike threshold (the strike force numbers above, whether that is ticked or not): higher - only the hardest blows cleave.
weight.cleave_cost.label = Cleave: what each monster passed spends, x the threshold
weight.cleave_cost.tip = Live. Each monster cut through spends this much of the stroke's force (its first monster's blow): higher - fewer monsters in one stroke; 0 - no end to it.
weight.cleave_min_speed.label = Cleave: only a blade this fast, m/s
weight.cleave_min_speed.tip = Live. The blade's speed into the monster at least, for it to cut through (real swings are 2 - 6 m/s): higher - only the fastest swings cleave; 0 - any speed (the force above still decides).

# --- Which contact counts as a strike ---
group.which_contact_counts_as_a_strike = Which contact counts as a strike
group.which_contact_counts_as_a_strike.help = Rules that refuse touches that are not real blows: the blade must move toward the monster, maces hit only with the head, and a swing must be big enough. The angle and amplitude sliders tune how strict each rule is.
gameplay.melee_toward.label = Toward the monster: the blade must move at it
gameplay.melee_toward.tip = For every kind of weapon (single kinds can be switched off in the table below): a contact counts as an attack only while the point of the blade that touches the monster is moving TOWARD it - the angle between that point's velocity and the line from the point to the nearest point of the monster's body axis is under the angle below. An overhead blow down, an uppercut from below, a sideways sweep into the monster and a thrust all go toward it. The wind-up (the head going up and back, away from a monster in front of you), the pull-back after a blow and a graze along its side do not count - and do not use the monster up: the blow that follows does. Only decides whether a contact counts as an attack: the game's own attack, its damage, rolls and reach are the game's, nothing is scaled. Unticked: every contact counts, as before. With "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" (Debug group below) a refused contact is RED (BLUE with the tick unticked). Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_toward_deg.label = Toward the monster: the widest angle, deg
gameplay.melee_toward_deg.tip = How far off the straight line to the monster a movement may be and still count as toward it: 60 = the cosine of the angle between the two directions above 0.5. Lower: only a movement straight at the monster counts; higher: a glancing blow counts too; 89: anything that is not away from it. Live.
gameplay.melee_amp_blunt_x.label = Blunt weapons: x piercing
gameplay.melee_amp_blunt_x.tip = The least swing amplitude of maces, hammers, clubs and scepters as a multiple of the piercing weapons' (below): 2 x 8 cm = 16 cm - a hammer needs a real swing, a flick or a tap does nothing, a shove of the head into the monster over that distance counts. The cm it makes is in the label. Each kind can have a number of its own in the table. Live.
gameplay.melee_head_only.label = Only the head of the weapon strikes (maces, scepters)
gameplay.melee_head_only.tip = For the kinds ticked in the table (maces, hammers, clubs and scepters by default): a contact counts only when the HEAD of the weapon touches the monster - the outer part of the blade, not the shaft or the handle. A touch with the shaft is refused (GREY in the debug) and does not use the monster up. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_head_pct.label = The head is the outer part of the blade, %
gameplay.melee_head_pct.tip = The head is this part of the blade's length, counted from the tip: 40 = the outer two fifths. Live.
gameplay.melee_amplitude.label = A swing must be big enough (the head's travel in the stroke)
gameplay.melee_amplitude.tip = For a contact to count, the head must have travelled at least the kind's amplitude in this stroke before it touched: a real swing, not a flick of the wrist or a tap. The base is the piercing weapons' number below (a dagger's or a spear's short jab can count); edged weapons, blunt weapons and staffs need it times their factor; any kind can have a factor of its own in the table. Not a speed - the least speed above, and each kind's own in the table, is separate. Unticked: no swing size is asked. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_amp_pierce_cm.label = Piercing: least swing amplitude, cm
gameplay.melee_amp_pierce_cm.tip = Wands, spears, daggers, claws, orbs, bare fists, javelins, throwing weapons and the rest: the least swing amplitude in cm - the base for all the other kinds. 8 = a jab of a hand's width. Live.
gameplay.melee_amp_edged_x.label = Edged weapons: x piercing
gameplay.melee_amp_edged_x.tip = Swords, axes and polearms: the least swing amplitude as a multiple of the piercing weapons'. 1.4 x 8 cm = 11.2 cm. The cm it makes is in the label. Live.
gameplay.melee_amp_staff_x.label = Staffs: x piercing
gameplay.melee_amp_staff_x.tip = Staffs: the least swing amplitude as a multiple of the piercing weapons'. 1.75 x 8 cm = 14 cm. The cm it makes is in the label. Live.

# --- Each kind of weapon (type a number; 0 = follow the general one) ---
group.each_kind_of_weapon_type_a_number_0_follow_the_general_one = Each kind of weapon (type a number; 0 = follow the general one)
group.each_kind_of_weapon_type_a_number_0_follow_the_general_one.help = A table to give each kind of weapon its own swing size, speed and stroke start, and to tick whether it must move toward the monster or hit only with its head. Type a number and press Enter; 0 follows the general setting.
@status.st_h0.tip = The kinds of weapon the touch swings (the game's own kinds: Maces are maces, hammers, clubs and flails). A bow or a crossbow is shot, not swung. The numbers of a row are for that kind alone; 0 in a number box = follow the general one.
@status.st_h1.label = Swing x
@status.st_h1.tip = The kind's least swing amplitude as a multiple of the piercing weapons' ("Piercing weapons: least swing amplitude, cm"). 0 = follow the kind's family: edged, blunt or staff, or the piercing x1. 0.25 to 8. Type a number and press Enter.
@status.st_h2.tip = What the kind's least swing amplitude comes to, in cm: the piercing weapons' cm times the kind's factor (its own, or its family's). A dash: the swing size is not asked.
@status.st_h3.label = Speed
@status.st_h3.tip = The least blade speed, m/s, for a contact of this kind to count. 0 = the general one ("Hit by touch: the least blade speed that hits"). 0.3 to 20.
@status.st_h4.label = Start cm
@status.st_h4.tip = How far the blade moves to start a stroke, cm, for this kind. 0 = the general one ("Hit by touch: how far the blade moves to start a stroke"). 2 to 30.
@status.st_h5.label = Toward
@status.st_h5.tip = Ticked: a contact of this kind must be toward the monster ("Toward the monster" above). Unticked: this kind counts whichever way the blade moves.
@status.st_h6.label = Head
@status.st_h6.tip = Ticked: only the head of this kind of weapon strikes - the outer part of the blade; a touch with the shaft or the handle is refused. Maces and scepters by default.

# --- Thrusts: a poke along the blade (spears, daggers, javelins) ---
group.thrusts_a_poke_along_the_blade_spears_daggers_javelins = Thrusts: a poke along the blade (spears, daggers, javelins)
group.thrusts_a_poke_along_the_blade_spears_daggers_javelins.help = Lets a quick poke along the blade hit with its own speed and distance, so a short stab with a spear or dagger counts while swings still need a real swing. Also blocks hits with the butt or shaft and on pull-backs; the debug ticks show each thrust's numbers in the headset.
gameplay.melee_thrust.label = A thrust counts: a poke along the blade, point first, with its own speed and distance
gameplay.melee_thrust.tip = For the weapons that pierce, a THRUST is a hit of its own kind: the blade moved along its own length, point first - a stab of a spear, a dagger, a javelin - counts with the two numbers below, apart from a swing's ("the least blade speed that hits", "how far the blade moves to start a stroke" and the swing's amplitude). So a short quick poke hits, while a swing still needs its usual speed and size. Which weapons thrust: the game's own data - the weapon's attack class, the one the game animates it with: 1ht (daggers, javelins, throwing knives) and 2ht (spears, tridents, pikes); if that cannot be read, spears, daggers and javelins. Each kind can be set to thrust always (a sword's tip, a polearm) or never in the table below. The strike rules above still judge a thrust (toward the monster, the head); a pull-back or a stab beside the monster does not count. A monster is hit once per thrust, and one movement that is both a swing and a thrust hits once. Only decides whether a contact counts: the game's own attack is pressed - its animation, reach, rolls and damage are the game's. With "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" a poke that counts turns the blade green. Unticked: a poke counts only as a swing, as before. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.melee_thrust_min_speed.label = Thrust: the least speed that hits, m/s
gameplay.melee_thrust_min_speed.tip = How fast the point must be moving where it touches for a thrust to count. A poke reads about 1 m/s, a swing's tip 2-6: 0.8 lets a quick short stab hit. Apart from the swing's least speed - a high swing number (only real swings) leaves pokes to this one. Each kind can have its own in the table. Live.
gameplay.melee_thrust_cm.label = Thrust: the least distance along the blade, cm
gameplay.melee_thrust_cm.tip = How far the point must have gone forward along the blade in this thrust before the touch: 5 = a short jab. Larger: only a real lunge counts; smaller: a tap counts too. Apart from the swing's start distance and amplitude. Each kind can have its own in the table. Live.
gameplay.melee_thrust_along_pct.label = Thrust: how much of the movement is along the blade, %
gameplay.melee_thrust_along_pct.tip = A movement is a thrust when at least this part of the WHOLE WEAPON's movement - where the hand holds it - went forward along its own length (and it still goes forward at the touch). The tip is not measured: on a long spear a small turn of the hand swings it sideways. The weapon may also turn at most 35 degrees during the thrust (more is a swing). 70 = mostly straight; higher: only a clean straight stab; lower: a stab with some sweep in it counts too. Live.
gameplay.melee_thrust_with_run.label = Thrust: running with the weapon counts (a charge)
gameplay.melee_thrust_with_run.tip = Every weapon that thrusts (spears, daggers, polearms, javelins...): the thrust is measured in the world, so the hero running or walking with the weapon held point first is the thrust's movement and acceleration too - run into a monster with the spear forward and it is a thrust. Still only along the weapon and without a big turn. The same for the stab (Weapon Weight > A pointed weapon sticks into the body): running in with any pointed weapon held forward sticks it in, the run counts as its speed against the body. Unticked: the thrust is your arms' alone (measured in the room), as before. Swings are always your arms' alone. Live.
gameplay.melee_not_butt.label = Never hit with the butt or the shaft behind your hands
gameplay.melee_not_butt.tip = Any weapon: a touch nearer its butt than your front hand on it is no hit, however fast - a poleaxe held in the middle does not kill with its back end on the return stroke. The front hand is where your hands hold it with weapon weight (held in the middle: the middle), else the game's own grip. It still stops on the monsters' bodies and pushes them. Unticked: the whole weapon strikes, as before. Live.
gameplay.melee_metal_head.label = Metal heads and blades: only the head hits, the shaft pushes
gameplay.melee_metal_head.tip = A weapon with a metal head or an edge hits only with it - a polearm's blade, an axe's or a mace's head, a spear's point, a sword's or a dagger's blade. A touch with the shaft or the handle below it is no hit, however fast; it still stops on the monsters' bodies and pushes them. Where the head starts is the game's own model's, for each base weapon (an item it gives nothing for: the kind's usual share, and the log says so). Staves, wands and plain clubs (wood) hit with their whole length; claws and orbs are not judged. Unticked: the whole blade hits, as before. Live.
gameplay.melee_head_volume.label = Heads as their own volume (an axe's blade beside the shaft)
gameplay.melee_head_volume.tip = A headed weapon - an axe, a polearm, a hammer, a pick, a mace, a spear - has its head as a volume of its own where the game's model has it: an axe's blade beside its shaft, a hammer's face and spike. Its shaft is as thin as the model's. A touch with the head volume is the head (with 'only the head hits' ticked, the only part that hits). Debug: melee boxes draws it with the blade. Unticked: one capsule along the weapon, as before. Live.
gameplay.melee_not_backward.label = Thrust weapons: never hit moving point-to-handle
gameplay.melee_not_backward.tip = A weapon that thrusts (spears, daggers, javelins...) never strikes with a movement from its point toward its handle - neither a thrust nor a swing: pulling the spear back, or a jerk back whose butt meets a monster behind you, is not a hit (the touching point moving within 60 degrees of the handle's direction along the weapon). Unticked: only 'Toward the monster' judges the way, as before. Live.
gameplay.melee_thrust_min_accel.label = Thrust: the least acceleration (jab, not push), m/s²
gameplay.melee_thrust_min_accel.tip = How sharply the point must have been driven forward along the blade: the PEAK acceleration of the thrust - the burst that started it - not the value at the touch (a jab meets the monster at its top speed, coasting, where a jab and a slow push both read about nothing). A sharp jab reaches tens of m/s², a slow push a few: about 10 - 15 keeps the jabs and refuses the pushes. 0 (the default) = not asked, as before. Each kind can have its own in the table. The log tells every thrust's numbers (speed, cm, the part along the blade, the peak acceleration) - the first ones always, every one with "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" - to tune it from. Live.
debug.thrust_debug.label = Thrust debug: the last thrust's numbers over the weapon hand
debug.thrust_debug.tip = To tune the thrust in the headset (F4): a small plate over the weapon hand shows the LAST TOUCH - a thrust's contact with a monster, COUNTED in blue or REJECTED in orange with the threshold that failed (not straight, too slow, too short, no accel, not toward the monster, not the head) - and the LAST JAB, touching or not: its peak speed, the cm its point went along the blade, how straight it was, its peak acceleration, each beside its threshold (green passes, red fails; "(own)" = the weapon kind's own number, else the general one), and whether it would count. So a real jab can be read before a monster is near. The blade (drawn as with "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch", which this switches on too) turns BLUE (counted) or ORANGE (refused) for a moment after each thrust - the thrust's own colours, apart from the swing's green / red - and the log has a line for each thrust and each jab ("thrust debug: ..."). Only a drawing and a log: nothing of what counts changes. Off by default. Live.
debug.thrust_debug_only.label = Thrust debug: only the thrusts (no swings, no blows from above)
debug.thrust_debug_only.tip = With the thrust debug on: ONLY the forward thrusts are shown. The swing's colours on the blade (green, red, amber), its contact marks, its log lines and the 5-a-second "melee boxes:" line are left out, and a movement that is not straight enough to be a thrust - a swing, an overhead blow - is neither shown on the plate nor tinted nor logged. The blade stays cyan until a thrust tints it blue or orange. Only what is shown changes; the swings hit as ever. Off by default. Live. F4.
debug.stab_debug.label = Stab debug: why a thrust sticks in or not, over the weapon hand
debug.stab_debug.tip = To tune the weapon sticking into monsters (Weapon Weight > A thrusting weapon sticks into the body) in the headset (F4): the plate over the weapon hand shows the LAST STAB - REFUSED with the reason (not a thrust, not the point, at an angle, too slow), IN or LOCKED with its depth against the deepest, or OUT with why it came out (drawn out, torn free, the body gone) - and the numbers it was judged on beside their sliders: the speed, the angle, how far from the tip it met, how far your hand is across the weapon's line. Drawn with the monsters' capsules (this switches "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" on): the entry an amber ball, the weapon's line to the deepest a grey rod, the depth reached a bar - green sliding, blue locked, red when it came out - and an orange ball where a refused strike met the body. Only a drawing: nothing of what sticks changes. Off by default. Live.
