# --- Two weapons: Double Swing by the hands (F4) ---
group.two_weapons_double_swing_by_the_hands_f4 = Two weapons: Double Swing by the hands (F4)
group.two_weapons_double_swing_by_the_hands_f4.help = For a Barbarian with a weapon in each hand: hitting the same monster with the other hand soon after the first casts the game's Double Swing (or Frenzy) from its pad slot. Choose pairs or a combo, the time window and which skill is pressed first.
hands.double_swing_by_hands.label = Double Swing by the two hands
hands.double_swing_by_hands.tip = A Barbarian with a melee weapon in each hand, hit by touch on (F4 only). The first hand's touch on a monster is the game's normal attack, as ever. When the OTHER hand then touches the SAME monster within the time below, that second strike is the game's own Double Swing instead of a normal attack: its pad button is pressed once (the skill must sit on one of the pad's ten skill slots - B, X, Y, RB with and without LT, A, LT + A) and the touched monster is handed to the cast as its target, the way the shield bash casts Smite. Only when the hero has a level in the skill and the mana for it (the game's own numbers: the skill's cost at its level against the hero's mana); otherwise the second touch is a normal attack too. Frenzy the same way when it is the skill on a slot. The swings, the damage, the animation and the mana are the game's; nothing is called that attacks. A pair is spent by the dual skill: the next touch starts a new one. With Double Swing on the attack button itself every touch casts it already and this adds nothing. The log says every decision once ("double swing: ..."). Not tried in the game yet. Unticked: both hands' touches are normal attacks, as before. Live.
hands.double_swing_combo.label = Double Swing as a combo: every blow after the first
hands.double_swing_combo.tip = Ticked: a COMBO instead of pairs. The first touch on a monster is the game's normal attack; EVERY following touch on the same monster - either hand - no longer than the window below after the last one is the game's Double Swing (or Frenzy), as long as you keep hitting it: normal, double, double, double... A touch on another monster, or one after a longer pause, starts a new combo with a normal attack. A touch the hero cannot pay (or with no level, no slot) is a normal attack and the combo goes on. Unticked: pairs, as before - the other hand's touch after the first is the dual skill, and the next touch starts a new pair. Live. Not tried in the game yet.
hands.double_swing_window_ms.label = Double Swing: the other hand within, ms
hands.double_swing_window_ms.tip = How long after one hand's strike on a monster the other hand's strike on the same monster is the second of a pair - the dual skill's. 700 ms is about one swing of the arm and back. Longer: a slower second blow still counts; shorter: only a quick one-two does. Live.
hands.double_swing_skill.label = Double Swing: the skill pressed first
hands.double_swing_skill.tip = Which of the two the second hand presses when both sit on pad slots: the first one that the hero has a level in and can pay. With only one of them on a slot, that one. Live.
hands.double_swing_skill.choice0 = Double Swing, then Frenzy
hands.double_swing_skill.choice1 = Frenzy, then Double Swing

# --- Direct hit ---
group.direct_hit = Direct hit
group.direct_hit.help = How a touch that counts becomes a hit. Off: the touch presses the game's own attack. By the rules: a direct hit for the first touch on a monster and for a real swing after the hero's attack time, otherwise the game's own attack. Fully on: every touch is a direct hit (the old experimental way). One place for single player, the host and a player who joined someone's game.
@directhit.mode.tip = Off: the touch presses the game's own attack (its animation, its attack rate, its reach). BY THE RULES: the FIRST touch on a monster is a direct hit. Then a touch on the SAME monster sooner than your hero's attack takes (measured from his own attack animation, so it follows his attack speed) is the game's own attack - poking fast wins nothing. After that, a touch on it is a direct hit again only for a real swing: the least speed, force and swing length (your controller's own path) below. Another monster is never too soon. A TWO-HANDED weapon needs both hands on it (the two-hand grip): in one hand its touch is the game's own attack. A touch that fails a rule still attacks: the game's own attack, never nothing. The two-handed cleave only with its own box below. FULLY ON (not recommended): every accepted touch is a direct hit, as the old experimental box did. What a direct hit is: in single player and as the host, the plugin calls the game's server attack itself (the hit roll, the damage and the wear are the game's; no animation, no wait for the attack rate, no walking up). As a player who JOINED someone's TCP/IP game, it sends the game's own command "attack this monster" - the one a click on it sends - and the host's server does the whole attack (the host needs nothing for that). Only while the skill on your attack slot is the one in the hero's hand and no melee skill is armed. Writes [gameplay] melee_direct and melee_direct_client. Live. F4 only, like hit by touch.
@directhit.mode.choice1 = By the rules
@directhit.mode.choice2 = Fully on (not recommended)
gameplay.melee_direct_min_ms.label = Direct hit (fully on): min gap between hits, ms
gameplay.melee_direct_min_ms.tip = Single player and the host, fully on: 0 = no limit beyond "a monster is hit once per stroke". More: after a direct hit, the touches within this time do nothing - to keep the rate near the game's own if hits come too fast. Live.
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_speed.label = Direct hit: least swing speed, m/s
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_speed.tip = How fast the blade must move where it touched for the touch to be a direct hit. Real swings are 2 - 6 m/s, pokes about 1. A strike judged by force counts its arrival's speed. For a repeat on the same monster, and for the cleave. A slower touch is the normal attack (the button). 0: no least speed. Live.
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_force.label = Direct hit: least strike force, N s
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_force.tip = How hard the strike must land: the weight model's strike score (the impulse in its first 150 ms, an edge's cut - the same measure as "Hit by the strike's force"). Needs the weapon's weight and the monster bodies on; not measured, it counts as too weak. For a repeat on the same monster, and for the cleave. A weaker touch is the normal attack. 0: no least force. Live.
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_length.label = Direct hit: least swing length (the controller's path), m
gameplay.melee_direct_client_min_length.tip = How far your CONTROLLER itself must have travelled in this swing - its own path, not the blade's tip, so a flick of the wrist that sweeps a long blade a long way does not pass it. A real swing, not a poke. A two-handed weapon: either controller's path counts. For a repeat on the same monster (the first touch on a monster is direct anyway). A shorter swing is the normal attack. 0: no least length. Live.
gameplay.melee_direct_client_cleave.label = Direct hit: a two-handed swing through a group hits each monster (past the game's rules)
gameplay.melee_direct_client_cleave.tip = GOES PAST THE GAME'S RULE OF ONE ATTACK AT A TIME. The game runs one attack at a time, so a swing through several monsters normally lands on the first only. On, with a TWO-HANDED weapon: the first monster gets the direct hit as above; every other monster the same swing touches while that attack plays, with the least speed AND force above, gets the game's server attack for your hero, once (the hit roll, the damage and the weapon's wear are the game's; no animation of its own) - in single player and as the host on this PC, as a joined player asked of the HOST over D2RLoader's network. No repeat on the same monster sooner than your attack takes. A one-handed weapon, or a touch too slow or too weak: the normal attack. JOINED: THE HOST MUST SET "By the rules" AND TICK THIS BOX TOO - it strikes only on its own say-so; with it off, those hits are dropped as without the box. Takes effect at the game's next start (the network channel). Off: as before.

# --- Quick strike ---
group.quick_strike = Quick strike
group.quick_strike.help = Makes your melee blow land earlier inside the game's attack animation, so the hit comes sooner after the touch. This changes the game's timing; VR first person and offline only. The slider picks the frame the blow lands at.
hands.quick_strike.label = Quick strike: the blow lands earlier in the attack animation (changes the game's timing)
hands.quick_strike.tip = A CHANGE OF THE GAME'S TIMING (off when the key is missing; on in the settings that come with the mod). The game's melee blow lands at one frame of the hero's attack animation - for a Paladin with a one-hand weapon frame 7 or 8, 0.28 - 0.32 s after the animation starts, in your log 317 - 339 ms after the touch pressed the attack (the Direct hit lands in 15 - 50 ms). On: that frame is moved to the frame below in the game's animation table, so the blow - its hit roll, damage and the monster's reaction - comes up to ~0.3 s sooner INSIDE THE SAME ATTACK. The animation's length and the attack rate stay (the next attack can still start only when the animation ends), mana and wear are the game's but happen earlier, and a monster's hit in the first ~0.3 s no longer cancels your blow. It applies to every melee attack of your class - the plain attack and the skills that play it (Zeal, Bash, Berserk, Sacrifice...), the Paladin's Smite too - in VR first person only and offline only (this game's own tables); put back exactly when you switch it off, change view or leave the game. Never the bow's, the crossbow's or a throw's animation. Live. [debug] bow_latency shows the animation row on the press-to-hit line.
hands.quick_strike_frame.label = Quick strike: the frame the blow lands at
hands.quick_strike_frame.tip = The animation frame (a frame is 0.04 s) the blow lands at instead of the original (6 to 14 for the classes' melee attacks). 1 is the earliest the game can act: frame 0 is never looked at when an animation starts. A value at or past the original changes nothing. Live.

# --- Shield bash ---
group.shield_bash = Shield bash
group.shield_bash.help = For a Paladin in F4 with native OpenXR: a hard swing of the shield through a monster casts Smite from its pad slot at that monster. The sliders set how fast and how far the shield must move for a bash.
gameplay.shield_smite.label = Shield bash casts Smite
gameplay.shield_smite.tip = Paladin, native OpenXR, first person (F4): with Smite on one of the pad's ten skill slots and a shield on your left arm, a hard swing or thrust of the shield through a monster casts one Smite at it - the game's own: the slot's button is pressed for a moment and the monster the shield touched is the cast's target. Reach, mana, cast rate, animation, damage, stun and knockback stay the game's. A shield at rest does nothing, nor does a bash with the right trigger down. Off: the shield casts nothing. F4 only.
gameplay.shield_smite_min_speed.label = Shield bash: the least speed, m/s
gameplay.shield_smite_min_speed.tip = How fast the shield must be moving for a bash to count. A shield moving slower does nothing, however it touches a monster. The default 0.8 is what the shield always used. This is the bash's OWN number - "Hit by touch: the least blade speed" does not apply to the shield. The speed is your left hand's: its movement plus its turn times the shield's length (0.4 m), frame to frame. Lower, and the speed that may begin a bash (1.5 x, at most 1.2) and the speed that counts as rest go lower with it; from 0.8 up they are as before. A movement is also a bash only after the shield has moved the distance below within about a tenth of a second. Tick "Draw what casts skills" (Debug group below) to see it: the shield turns green while a bash would count, the white and orange balls show where its speed reached this number and fell below it, and the log line shows the speed against it. Only decides when the press goes out - never the cast itself. Live. F4 only.
gameplay.shield_smite_stroke_cm.label = Shield bash: how far the shield moves to start a bash, cm
gameplay.shield_smite_stroke_cm.tip = A movement is a bash - and can cast - only after the shield has moved this far within about a tenth of a second, and fast enough (above). Smaller: a short thrust counts; larger: only a long swing does. Default 8 as it always was; the bash's own number, apart from "Hit by touch: how far the blade moves to start a stroke". Live. F4 only.

# --- Debug (the same ticks as on the Debug tab) ---
group.debug_the_same_ticks_as_on_the_debug_tab = Debug (the same ticks as on the Debug tab)
group.debug_the_same_ticks_as_on_the_debug_tab.help = Drawings and tests for tuning Hit by touch and the shield bash: draw the blade and monster capsules, colour refused contacts, try touches without attacking, and fit the blade's length, butt and thickness to the weapon you see.
debug.melee_touch_client_verdict.label = Hit by touch: decide hostile / wall from the client's own units
debug.melee_touch_client_verdict.tip = What a player who JOINED a TCP/IP game gets (the game's server runs on the host's PC there, so it cannot be asked), tried offline: a hireling or summon is not hostile, nobody in town is, the game's own line test stops a touch through a wall. Unticked: offline and as the host the server answers, as always. The log says once a second what the client's units answered ("melee touch: no server here"). A test tick - live.
debug.melee_touch_no_attack.label = Hit by touch: no attack (try the stab and the push)
debug.melee_touch_no_attack.tip = A touch that would attack presses nothing: the weapon still meets, sticks into and pushes the monsters (Weapon Weight's monster bodies, stab and weight), the debug still draws where it struck, and the log tells the first few ("would be attacked - not pressed"). To try them without killing the monster. The trigger's own attack is not touched. Unticked: a touch attacks, as always. Live.
debug.monster_ragdoll_view.label = Draw the monsters' weight and balance (ragdoll probe)
debug.monster_ragdoll_view.tip = First person (F4) with Weapon Weight's "Monsters' bodies give way by their weight" on: an amber arrow where your weapon pushed a humanoid monster - the way and how hard (5 cm per N s) - and over each humanoid a grey bar of its weight (1 cm per 2 kg) with a ball of its balance: green standing, amber swaying, red at the edge, leaning the way it was pushed. Drawn with the capsules of Hit by touch (this switches them on). A drawing only.
debug.melee_boxes.label = Draw the capsules of Hit by touch
debug.melee_boxes.tip = First person (F4) with "Hit by touch" on: the blade's capsule (cyan) and the capsule of every monster the touch looks at (yellow; pale where the game's own checks refuse it - not hostile, or a wall between), drawn through everything, so they can be seen against the monsters. The monster a touch was accepted on shows red for half a second when the game's own attack key was pressed for it, magenta when "Direct hit" took it. Five times a second the log gets a line of numbers: the nearest monsters' capsule size and height, how far the blade's tip is from them, the stroke speed. A drawing and a log only - it changes nothing in what the touch does. Live. The nearest three monsters are always drawn, hostile or not (pale where the game refuses them); with two melee weapons held (a Barbarian's, an Assassin's claws) both blades are drawn, the second one teal. While a contact would count (a stroke on, the blade at or above "Hit by touch: the least blade speed") the blade is green; a swing leaves marks: a WHITE ball where the blade's speed reached that least speed (and the start distance was met), an ORANGE ball where it fell below it again, and the tip's path as a thin trail, cyan where a contact would not count and green where it would - tune the least speed and the start distance by where they land in your swing. A contact is judged by the strike rules (the Strikes tab): the blade, the trail and the marks are green only while a contact with the monster nearest the blade would count now. At every contact that was REFUSED, for "Hit by touch: how long the speed marks and the trail stay": a BALL on the point of the blade that touched, an ARROW along the way that point was moving, a thin LINE from it to the nearest point of the monster's body axis, and the monster's capsule tinted with the colour of the reason - RED: not toward the monster (a wind-up, a pull-back, a graze; BLUE instead with "Not toward the monster in red" unticked - red is also the monster's flash when a blow is pressed); AMBER: the swing was too small for this kind, or too slow where it touched, or the blade entered the monster in a movement that never became a stroke; GREY: not the head (the shaft or the handle of a mace touched). A contact that counted leaves green marks and the monster's own red / magenta flash. The log says why, one line for each refused contact (the kind, the angle, the speed or the amplitude), at most one every 250 ms for each reason; the first twelve are always told.
debug.melee_mark_ms.label = Hit by touch: how long the speed marks and the trail stay, ms (0 = none)
debug.melee_mark_ms.tip = With "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" on: how long the white / orange balls (where the blade's speed reached the least speed and where it fell below it) and the tip's trail stay in the picture after a swing. 0 = no marks and no trail, the blade's colour only. Live.
debug.melee_direction_red.label = Hit by touch: not toward the monster in red (off: blue)
debug.melee_direction_red.tip = With "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" on: the colour of a contact the direction rule refused (the blade was moving away from the monster or across it - a wind-up, a pull-back, a graze). On (the default): RED. Off: BLUE - red is also the monster's flash when a blow is pressed, which a blue refusal cannot be taken for. The other reasons keep their colours: amber - the swing too small or too slow, grey - not the head. A drawing only. Live.
debug.skill_triggers.label = Draw what casts skills
debug.skill_triggers.tip = First person (F4): draws and logs the triggers that cast a skill, so they can be tuned by eye - for now the SHIELD BASH that casts Smite ("Shield bash casts Smite"): the shield's capsule (the one the bash tests monsters with) on the left arm in violet, green while a bash would count (a stroke on, at or above "Shield bash: the least speed", the right trigger up, Smite on a pad slot...); a WHITE ball at the shield's centre where its speed reached that speed and an ORANGE one where it fell below it; its path as a thin trail, cyan where a bash would not count and green where it would; the monsters near it (yellow) and the one a bash pressed Smite on, red. Five times a second the log gets a "skill trigger shield bash:" line: the shield's speed against the bash speed and its start distance, the right trigger, the pad button of Smite's slot, the mana against Smite's cost, the nearest monster, and why a bash would not count (too slow, no stroke yet, right trigger down, no Smite slot, no mana, not hostile...). It works with the shield bash off too (the line then says so). Other skill triggers (the bow's draw, a throw) can join it later. A drawing and a log only - it changes nothing in when anything fires. Apart from "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch", which is for the melee blade. Needs the D2R_DepthFog.fx of the same build (the old one draws the shield's capsule green). Live. F4 only.
debug.skill_mark_ms.label = Skill triggers: how long the speed marks and the trail stay, ms (0 = none)
debug.skill_mark_ms.tip = With "Draw what casts skills" on: how long the white / orange balls and the shield's trail stay in the picture after a bash. 0 = no marks and no trail, the capsule's colour only. Live.
debug.melee_blade_length_pct.label = Hit by touch: the blade's length from the weapon bone to its tip, % of the weapon's own
debug.melee_blade_length_pct.tip = Tunes the blade of Hit by touch - the capsule drawn by "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" is the blade the touch tests - to the weapon as you see it: 100 = the length the plugin has for this weapon, from the weapon bone (for a staff, spear or two-handed weapon the middle of the grip, not the end of the weapon) along the weapon to its tip. It only tunes where the touch counts a hit; it never changes the game's reach, rolls or attack. First person (F4) only. Live.
debug.melee_blade_butt_pct.label = Hit by touch: the blade's length behind the weapon bone (the butt end), % of the weapon's own
debug.melee_blade_butt_pct.tip = The other side of the weapon bone: how far the blade runs behind the grip to the butt of the staff, spear or pole-arm. 100 = what the plugin has for this weapon (a staff: as far behind as before), 0 = none, so that only the tip side counts. Same rules as the length: only where the touch counts a hit, never the game's reach or rolls. First person (F4) only. Live.
debug.melee_blade_radius_cm.label = Hit by touch: the blade's thickness (radius), cm (0 = the weapon's own)
debug.melee_blade_radius_cm.tip = 0: the radius the plugin has for this weapon (a staff's is thin, an axe's wide). Else the blade's radius in cm, 0.5 to 15. Only where the touch counts a hit - never the game's reach or rolls. First person (F4) only. Live.
debug.melee_thrown_length_pct.label = Hit by touch: a thrown weapon's blade, tip side (javelin, throwing knife and axe), %
debug.melee_thrown_length_pct.tip = The tip side of the blade of a JAVELIN, THROWING KNIFE or THROWING AXE only, on top of the general length above - those blades are estimates (the javelin's head side, 1.04 m from the weapon bone along its -Y, was measured on two screenshots; the others were not seen). With "Draw the capsules of Hit by touch" on, the capsule's far end - the HEAD side - should reach the weapon's real point, the spearhead's; raise or lower this until it does. Only where the touch counts a hit - never the game's reach or rolls. First person (F4) only. Live.
debug.melee_thrown_butt_pct.label = Hit by touch: a thrown weapon's blade, butt side (behind the weapon bone), %
debug.melee_thrown_butt_pct.tip = The side of the blade behind the weapon bone - the BUTT end, behind the hand - for a javelin, throwing knife or throwing axe only (the javelin's is 0.30 m, a guess; the bone is at the hand). Same rules as the head side. First person (F4) only. Live.
debug.melee_blade_flip.label = Hit by touch: the blade runs the other way along the weapon
debug.melee_blade_flip.tip = On: the blade's tip lies on the other side of the weapon bone than the plugin assumes, for every weapon (the dagger's already runs the other way by default). For a weapon whose capsule points away from its drawn blade. Only where the touch counts a hit. First person (F4) only. Live.

# ===== Tab: Weapon Weight =====
tab.weapon_weight = Weapon Weight

# --- Weight (F4, the arms on the controllers) ---
group.weight_f4_the_arms_on_the_controllers = Weight (F4, the arms on the controllers)
group.weight_f4_the_arms_on_the_controllers.help = The main switch for weapons with weight in F4: a weapon lags, sags and falls when both grips let go, and you take and pass it with the grips. The sliders set the weight, the hands' strength, gravity and damping; you can also use the weight and grip libraries instead.
weight.on.label = Weapons have weight; take and pass them with the grip
weight.on.tip = A melee weapon held alone is heavy: it lags behind a hard swing, a two-handed one wants both hands, a spear held by its end is slower than held where the game holds it. You hold it with the grips: let both go and it falls. First person (F4) only, with BodyWalk's tracking or native OpenXR (with or without "Controls without BodyWalk"). A grip next to the belt is still a potion, a grip behind a shoulder is still the weapon swap, and hit by touch follows the weapon as it is drawn - the hand that carries it swings it; one let go strikes nothing. Off: the weapon sits fast in the game's grip, as before.
weight.weapon_grip_no_chord.label = A grip holding the weapon blocks no button
weight.weapon_grip_no_chord.tip = You hold the weapon by its grip, so that grip is down the whole fight. Ticked, a grip that holds the weapon (or that another gesture holds: the bow's string, a javelin, the shoulder swap) is no modifier: the right grip on the weapon does not keep the right A and the right trigger from their A and RT skill slots ("The right trigger and A cast the RT and A slots" - a skill there casts with the weapon held), and the off hand's grip on the shaft does not make the skill wheel's grip + stick click chord (when the wheel opens that way, or with BodyWalk's controls). Two grips held mean nothing anyway, and the "with the grip held" lines of the Controls never saw a weapon's grip. Unticked: as before. Live. F4 only.
weight.feel.label = Weight, % of the real mass
weight.feel.tip = A dagger weighs 0.4 kg, a sword 1.2, a two-handed sword 2.5, a spear 1, a polearm or a maul 3.5. 50 by default (half the real mass); 100 = the real mass; 0: no weight, the weapon only goes from hand to hand.
weight.strength.label = Hands' strength, %
weight.strength.tip = How hard the hands pull the weapon after the controllers: stronger, it lags less and swings round less. With the gravity feel it also stiffens the wrists, so the weight sags them less.
weight.gravity_feel.label = Gravity feel: wrists the weight can sag
weight.gravity_feel.tip = Ticked: the weight is gravity. The wrist is soft near the line of your controller and firm far off it, so a sword held out level sinks a few degrees, a polearm or a two-hander in one hand sinks a lot (two hands hold it much better), a swing down is helped by the weight and lifting it up is slowed by it, and a hard cut is still followed. Unticked: the old stiff wrists, where the weight showed only as a lag. Gravity and Damping below work either way.
weight.gravity_pct.label = Gravity, %
weight.gravity_pct.tip = How hard gravity pulls the weapon's steel down (100 = the real 9.8 m/s2). Held out, a heavy weapon sinks by this; a swing down is helped by it and lifting up is slowed by it. 0: no gravity at all, only inertia (the weapon lags the same way up and down). A weapon you let go always falls at the real g.
weight.damping_pct.label = Damping, %
weight.damping_pct.tip = How much the wrists damp the weapon's motion against the controller's (100 = nearly critical, so it settles without a wobble). The damper follows the controller's speed, it is not a drag: lower, the weapon rings and lags more in a swing, higher, it follows more tightly.
weight.hands_model.label = Move the weapon with the weight-physics library (A/B)
weight.hands_model.tip = Ticked: the weapon and the hands are moved by the weight-physics library (d2r_vr_weight.dll, in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs) instead of the mod's own physics. Gravity %, Damping %, Weight % and Hands' strength % work with either. Switch it while you hold the weapon to compare. Greyed out while the library is not there: the mod then has only its own physics.
weight.hands_model_palm.label = Library: the weapon's weight in the palm
weight.hands_model_palm.tip = Takes the weapon's centre of mass into the palm while it is held: a heavy weapon turns about your hand, nothing sags, a swing needs far less effort. A comfort setting; unticked, the weight sits where the steel is. Only with the library.
weight.grip_model.label = Hold the weapon the grip library's way (A/B)
weight.grip_model.tip = Ticked: how a hand takes hold of the shaft and looks while it does is the grip library's (d2r_vr_grip.dll, in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs) instead of the mod's own: the hand sits on the wood with its palm touching it, the fingers close until they meet it, the second hand of a long shaft is held by its grip - tight, where it is - or, with the grip let go and the trigger squeezed, loose: it slides along the shaft and turns about it; the hand feels a pulse when it comes within reach, closes and lets go. The weight, the aim and the game's own attacks are not touched. Greyed out while the library is not there: the mod then has only its own way.

# --- Where the second hand takes the weapon (F4) ---
group.where_the_second_hand_takes_the_weapon_f4 = Where the second hand takes the weapon (F4)
group.where_the_second_hand_takes_the_weapon_f4.help = Lets the second hand take swords, axes, maces, scepters and daggers only on the hilt, leaving the grip free elsewhere. The lengths set each hilt in cm; 0 takes it from the weight model.
weight.grip_hilt_only.label = Swords, axes, maces: the second hand takes only the hilt
weight.grip_hilt_only.tip = Ticked: with one hand holding a sword, a dagger, a scepter, an axe or a mace, the OTHER hand takes it only on its hilt (the haft, for an axe or a mace), from the pommel to the guard and a few centimetres past - not on the blade or the head. A grip there takes nothing, so it is free for something else (a belt potion, for one). The staff, the spear, the polearm and the other long weapons keep the whole shaft. Works with the mod's own way of holding and with the grip library. Unticked: the second hand takes the weapon anywhere along it, as ever. The guard's place is not in the game's data, so it comes from the weight model's shape for the kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn; the lengths below set it by hand. The log says where the hilt ends for each weapon.
weight.grip_hilt_cm_sword.label = Sword: the hilt, cm (0 = from the model)
weight.grip_hilt_cm_sword.tip = Live. How long the hilt is, in centimetres from the pommel to the guard: the second hand takes the weapon only up to here (and a few centimetres past it). 0: the weight model's own - the first piece of its shape for this kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn (a two-handed sword about 30 cm, a one-handed one about 17).
weight.grip_hilt_cm_axe.label = Axe: the haft, cm (0 = from the model)
weight.grip_hilt_cm_axe.tip = Live. How long the hilt is, in centimetres from the pommel to the guard: the second hand takes the weapon only up to here (and a few centimetres past it). 0: the weight model's own - the first piece of its shape for this kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn (a two-handed axe about 90 cm).
weight.grip_hilt_cm_mace.label = Mace, hammer: the haft, cm (0 = from the model)
weight.grip_hilt_cm_mace.tip = Live. How long the hilt is, in centimetres from the pommel to the guard: the second hand takes the weapon only up to here (and a few centimetres past it). 0: the weight model's own - the first piece of its shape for this kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn (a maul about 90 cm).
weight.grip_hilt_cm_scepter.label = Scepter: the shaft, cm (0 = from the model)
weight.grip_hilt_cm_scepter.tip = Live. How long the hilt is, in centimetres from the pommel to the guard: the second hand takes the weapon only up to here (and a few centimetres past it). 0: the weight model's own - the first piece of its shape for this kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn.
weight.grip_hilt_cm_dagger.label = Dagger: the hilt, cm (0 = from the model)
weight.grip_hilt_cm_dagger.tip = Live. How long the hilt is, in centimetres from the pommel to the guard: the second hand takes the weapon only up to here (and a few centimetres past it). 0: the weight model's own - the first piece of its shape for this kind, scaled onto the weapon as it is drawn (about 10 cm).

# --- Monsters' bodies (F4) ---
group.monsters_bodies_f4 = Monsters' bodies (F4)
group.monsters_bodies_f4.help = Tests that give monsters bodies your weapon cannot pass through: it stops on them, a pointed weapon can stick in, monsters' shields and weapons stop it, two weapons clash, parries are felt, and bodies give way by their weight. Needs Hit by touch on; the hit itself is still the game's.
weight.monster_bodies.label = The weapon stops on monsters' bodies (a test)
weight.monster_bodies.tip = Ticked: a monster the game calls hostile has a body the weapon in your hands cannot pass through - a thrust or a cut stops on it, an edge (a sword, an axe, a spear) at a shallow angle glances off along it, a blunt weapon (a mace, a scepter, a staff) stops where it struck; a pulse in the hand at the strike. Your hand goes on, the weapon (and the hand as it is drawn on it) stays at the body until the hand comes back. The body is the monster's own skeleton: a capsule on each of its limbs as the game poses them, as thick as its model (where that cannot be read, the capsule the game gives the monster). The hit itself is still the game's attack pressed by hit by touch: needs Hit by touch on - its scan finds the monsters. Unticked: the weapon passes through them, as ever.
weight.stab_in.label = A pointed weapon sticks into the body (a test)
weight.stab_in.tip = Ticked, with the bodies above: a weapon with a point (a sword - one- or two-handed - a dagger, a spear, a javelin, a throwing weapon, a polearm, a claw) driven point first (within 60 degrees of straight) into a monster's body at 0.5 m/s or more goes IN instead of stopping at the surface. It only slides along its own length: the body holds it back - a harder skin for the first few centimetres, then softer flesh - no deeper than its blade; left still it locks where it is, and a steady pull frees it again. Draw it back along its length past where it went in and it comes out. Swung sideways or turned while it is in, it is held on its line - it drags and turns with the monster, it does not cut through; pull the hand far away and it comes free. A monster that walks carries it, one that dies lets it go. Only a movement point first counts (along the blade, not turned) - for any pointed weapon, whether or not Hit by touch counts it as a thrust. A cut with the edge, a mace, an axe, a staff or a fist stops at the surface as before. Only the weapon you see: the hit is still the game's attack pressed by hit by touch (a sword's stab still hits as the swing it was, unless Thrust is ticked for swords). Unticked: every weapon stops at the surface. Needs the weight library (d2r_vr_weight.dll 1.1 or newer in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs): the stab is its - without it every weapon stops at the surface (the log says so).
weight.stab_min_speed.label = Stab: the least speed to go in, m/s
weight.stab_min_speed.tip = Live. How fast the point must be moving against the monster when it meets the body for the weapon to go in. Lower: a slow push goes in too; higher: only a quick jab. (The thrust itself must still count as a thrust for Hit by touch.)
weight.stab_max_angle.label = Stab: the widest angle off straight in, degrees
weight.stab_max_angle.tip = Live. How far from straight into the body the weapon may point and still go in. A thin limb hit off its middle meets the point at a slant - raise this if stabs are refused 'at an angle' (the stab debug shows the angle of each one).
weight.stab_resist_pct.label = Stab: how hard the body resists, %
weight.stab_resist_pct.tip = Live. How strongly the body holds the weapon back as it goes in and comes out - a harder skin for the first 2.5 cm, then softer flesh. 100 = the VR toolkit's own numbers (made for stronger hands than ours: the point barely gets past the skin); lower goes in deeper and easier, 0 = no resistance at all.
weight.stab_depth_cm.label = Stab: the deepest it goes, cm (0 = the blade)
weight.stab_depth_cm.tip = Live. How far past the skin the point may go. 0: as deep as the weapon's point piece is long (a spear's head about 22 cm, a dagger's blade about 27 cm).
weight.stab_tear_cm.label = Stab: tear it free with the hand this far aside, cm
weight.stab_tear_cm.tip = Live. While the weapon is in, your hand may go on into the monster freely; moved this far ACROSS the weapon's line away from where the weapon is drawn in your hand, the weapon is torn free. Lower: it comes free easily; higher: it holds on.
weight.stab_unlock_n.label = Stab: the pull that frees a resting stab, N
weight.stab_unlock_n.tip = Live. A stab left still locks where it is; a steady pull along the weapon of more than this for a quarter of a second frees it to slide again. Lower: it slides out with a light pull; 0 = it never locks.
weight.monster_shields.label = Monsters' shields and weapons stop your weapon (a test)
weight.monster_shields.tip = Live. Ticked: what a monster holds - its shield, its weapons - stops your weapon as its limbs do, and your blade glances along them (a shield is four capsules across its face, a weapon one along it; Debug: melee boxes draws them violet and orange). A blow they stop is no hit: hit by touch presses the attack only once your weapon has reached the monster's body - the game's own block roll stays the game's for the blows that land. They push no doll and take no stab. Unticked: they are transparent to your weapon, as before.
weight.dual_collide.label = A weapon in each hand: the two strike each other (steel on steel)
weight.dual_collide.tip = Live. With a weapon in each hand the two weapons meet: each stops on the other and glances along it, as on a monster's weapon; a knock as hard as a blow is felt in both hands (and heard, with the clash sound below), resting one on the other is silent. With 'Heads as their own volume' ticked (hit by touch) an axe's blade, a hammer's face, a mace's head is steel of its own beside the shaft, where the game's model has it: a sword stops on it too. Only how they move, feel and sound - no hit, nothing of the game's. Unticked: they pass through each other, as before.
weight.clash_sound.label = Steel on steel sounds: the harder the knock, the louder
weight.clash_sound.tip = Live. The two weapons in your hands striking each other, and a parry's clash (a monster's weapon meeting your weapon or shield), play the game's own block sound - as loud as they met hard: a light tap quiet, a hard blow as loud as the game plays it, under 0.5 m/s nothing. The pulse in the hands follows the same rule. A sound only: nothing of the game's changes. Unticked: the knock is felt, not heard, as before.
weight.second_lets_go.label = A weapon in each hand: the second one can be let go too
weight.second_lets_go.tip = Live. With a weapon in each hand the second one is held by its hand's grip as the first is: let go, it falls and lies, and the first stays a full weapon in its hand (it strikes, stops on the bodies, its grip lets it go). 'After a drop' is the same for it: it lies on the floor or goes to the back; with the shoulder draw each is drawn from behind its own hand's shoulder (the right weapon from the right one, the left from the left) and both hang there. That hand's grip pressed away from the dropped one calls it back; the fist closing on it takes it up. Unticked: the second is held for good, as before.
weight.parry_feel.label = Parry: feel the clash of weapons
weight.parry_feel.tip = Live. Your weapon (or shield) meeting a monster's weapon while it attacks is a clash: a hard pulse in that hand, and your weapon knocked aside along its blow; heard with the clash sound, the pulse as hard as the two met. Whether the monster hits is never changed - the game rolls it. No spark yet. Unticked: nothing, as before.
weight.parry_block_show.label = Parry: feel the game's own block
weight.parry_block_show.tip = Live. When the game blocks a blow (your hero goes into his block), it is felt as a parry: a pulse in the shield's or the weapon's hand, harder the nearer it was to the attacking monster's weapon (needs 'Monsters' shields and weapons' to know where that is; without it, always the softer pulse). Reading only - the game's block roll is the game's. Unticked: nothing, as before.
weight.parry_claw_block.label = Parry: feel the Assassin's Weapon Block
weight.parry_claw_block.tip = Live. The same for the Assassin's Weapon Block (claws in both hands): both hands pulse. Unticked: nothing, as before.
weight.parry_shield_smite.label = Parry: shield into a monster's swing casts Smite
weight.parry_shield_smite.tip = Live. A Paladin's shield meeting a monster's weapon in its swing casts Smite at that monster - the shield bash's own press of the pad slot Smite is on (none on a slot: nothing), with the right trigger up. The game decides the rest: mana, reach, the cast. Works with 'Shield bash casts Smite' off. Unticked: nothing, as before.
weight.parry_counts_hit.label = Parry: a blow on a monster's weapon in its swing hits it
weight.parry_counts_hit.tip = Live. A real blow (as for its body: speed, the head, toward it) on a monster's weapon while it attacks counts as a blow on the monster: hit by touch presses the game's attack and the game's own rolls decide. A shield stays no hit. Unticked: a blow its weapon stops is no hit, as before.
weight.monster_ragdoll.label = Monsters' bodies give way by their weight (a probe)
weight.monster_ragdoll.tip = Ticked: the monsters' bodies above have weight - as heavy as their size says (a man of 1.75 m 70 kg, a fallen about 28). A push or a strike of your weapon moves the limb it meets and, less, the whole monster; its muscles bring it back in a moment. A light monster (a fallen) gives way far, a heavy one hardly at all. Humanoids only - zombies, fallen, skeletons, goatmen, told by their own bones; animals, insects, blobs stay as they are. Only the bodies your weapon meets move - see them with Debug: melee boxes - not the monster as the game draws it, and nothing of the game's: it stands, walks and attacks as the game has it. Needs the weight library (d2r_vr_weight.dll 1.2 or newer, in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs): without it this is greyed out, an older one does nothing (the log says so). Unticked: the bodies stand where the game poses them.
weight.monster_weight_pct.label = Monsters' weight, % of their flesh
weight.monster_weight_pct.tip = Live. How heavy the monsters are: each limb weighs as much as flesh of its size, times this. 200: twice as heavy - your weapon moves them half as far; 50: half as heavy. A fallen weighs about 20-30 kg at 100, a zombie about 70.
weight.monster_push_pct.label = Weapon's push on monsters, %
weight.monster_push_pct.tip = Live. How hard your weapon pushes a monster: the push its own weight and speed give, times this. 0: they do not move; 200: twice as far.
weight.monster_ragdoll_pose.label = The monster as drawn gives way too (a probe)
weight.monster_ragdoll_pose.tip = Ticked: a struck humanoid monster gives way as the game draws it - the limb you hit turns about its joint, the body leans away, and its own animation takes over again as it recovers. Only the drawing: where it stands, what it does and everything the game knows stay the game's. Unticked: only the bodies your weapon meets move (Debug: melee boxes shows them).
weight.monster_ragdoll_all.label = Every monster gives way, not only humanoids (a probe)
weight.monster_ragdoll_all.tip = Ticked: every monster your weapon pushes gives way by its weight - animals, insects, demons, flyers, not only the humanoid ones. A monster whose model has no body parts to read gets its limbs from its bones. A corpse never moves. Only the drawing. Unticked: humanoids only, as before.
weight.npc_bodies.label = Town NPCs and allies have bodies too
weight.npc_bodies.tip = Ticked, with the bodies above: the town's NPCs, hirelings and every other unit the game does not call hostile have bodies too - a capsule on each limb, from their own skeletons, the same as the monsters'. Your weapon stops on them, glances off them, sticks into them (with "A pointed weapon sticks into the body") and they give way by their weight (with "Monsters' bodies give way by their weight") - to try it all without a fight. They are only bodies for the weapon you see: Hit by touch never attacks them - it still presses only on a monster the game calls hostile. Unticked: the weapon passes through them, as before (the grab still takes them). Live. F4.

# --- Grab bodies (F4) ---
group.grab_bodies_f4 = Grab bodies (F4)
group.grab_bodies_f4.help = A test: squeeze the grip of an empty hand on a monster's or an ally's body and your hand holds on to it. Only what you see moves; nothing is attacked or moved in the game. Needs Hit by touch, a weapon in the other hand and the weight library.
weight.grab_bodies.label = Grab monsters and allies with your hand's grip (a test)
weight.grab_bodies.tip = Live. Ticked: squeeze the grip of an EMPTY hand (no weapon, shield, bow or bottle in it) firmly with the palm on a monster's or an ally's body - a mercenary, a town's people - and the hand takes hold of it there (a pulse). The grab is the VR toolkit's own, in the weight library: while you keep the grip squeezed your hand holds that spot - a humanoid's limb is pulled by your hand's strength against its weight (with 'Monsters' bodies give way by their weight' ticked - a light one follows, a heavy one holds your hand back, its muscles pull it back; 'The monster as drawn gives way too' shows it), anything else does not give and your hand is held on it and goes where the monster goes. Let the grip go to let go; pull your hand farther than the break distance below from the spot held and it tears loose (not in the first 2 s). Only what you see moves: the monster stays where the game has it, nothing is attacked, hurt or moved in the game. With a bow or crossbow the hand that draws the string grabs (not on the string). Needs the weight library 1.4 (d2r_vr_weight.dll in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs) - without it nothing grabs. Unticked: the grip of an empty hand only closes the fist, as before.
weight.grab_reach_cm.label = Grab: how near the body the palm must be, cm
weight.grab_reach_cm.tip = Live. The palm this close to a body's surface (or in it) takes it when the grip closes. Higher: easier to grab; lower: only with the palm right on it.
weight.grab_break_cm.label = Grab: the hand tears loose this far off, cm
weight.grab_break_cm.tip = Live. While a body holds your hand back, your real hand may go on this far from the spot it holds before the grip tears loose (after the first 2 s). A body that does not give lets go at 80 cm anyway, as in the VR toolkit.
weight.grab_arm_reach.label = Grab: let go past the arm's reach
weight.grab_arm_reach.tip = Live. Ticked: when what your hand holds is farther from your shoulder than your arm reaches (the hero's arm, fitted to your span), the hand lets go at once - your arm is never lengthened to hold on (a player walking off with your hand on him stretched it). Not while your real hand is out of reach itself: it is drawn there as without a grab. The hand takes nothing new until you open the grip. Unticked: only the break distance above lets go, as before.
weight.grab_wrap.label = Grab: the hand closes round what it holds
weight.grab_wrap.tip = Live. Ticked: a hand that holds a body is laid on it - turned so the palm faces it, the palm against its surface - and the fingers close round it until each touches (the VR toolkit's own hand pose, from the grip library d2r_vr_grip.dll; without it the palm is laid on and the hand closes as a fist). The body's shape is the capsules of its limbs read from the model. Unticked: the hand is held at the spot and closes as a fist, as before.
weight.grab_muscle_pct.label = Grab: how hard a held monster's muscles hold its limbs, %
weight.grab_muscle_pct.tip = Live. A humanoid held by a limb bends at its joints - the hand at the wrist, the forearm at the elbow, the arm at the shoulder - each against its muscle, which pulls it back to the game's pose; only a strong, far pull carries its body. Higher: stiffer muscles, the limb bends less and the body is carried sooner; lower: limp. 100: as its size gives (the strength goes as the square of this, as in the ragdoll tools). Needs 'Monsters' bodies give way by their weight'.
weight.grab_items.label = Pick up items from the ground with your hand's grip (a test)
weight.grab_items.tip = Live. Ticked: bend down and squeeze the grip of an EMPTY hand firmly with the palm at an item lying on the ground - the game picks it up, as pressing Interact on it would: the game's own pick-up, its own reach (it walks you up if it is not in reach) and its own rules (a full inventory keeps it on the ground). While you keep the grip squeezed after the game took it, the hand shows the item. Nothing else is changed: the item goes where the game puts it. Unticked: items are picked up only with Interact, as before.
weight.grab_items_reach_cm.label = Pick up: how near the item the palm must be, cm
weight.grab_items_reach_cm.tip = Live. The palm this close to the middle of the item's place on the ground picks it up when the grip closes. Higher: easier (you need not bend so far); lower: only with the hand right on it.

# --- Knock the level's props about (F4) ---
group.knock_the_level_s_props_about_f4 = Knock the level's props about (F4)
group.knock_the_level_s_props_about_f4.help = Lets your weapon or fist knock the level's small props (cups, vases, books, stools, barrels...) so they fall and roll. Only the drawing changes. Needs Hit by touch and the weight library; the sliders set the hands' strength and the pulse.
weight.knock_props.label = Cups, plates, vases, books and stools are knocked about by your weapon
weight.knock_props.tip = Ticked: the level's own small props near you - cups, plates, bowls, jugs, vases, bottles, books, skulls, baskets, pails, stools, chairs, barrels, sacks - stand where the game placed them until your weapon or your fist reaches them; then they fall, bounce and roll and come to rest where they land, and the game draws its own model there. Your weapon has its weight in it: a maul throws a cup further than a dagger and shoves a barrel that holds a light sword back. Only the drawing: nothing of the game's changes (no item, no collision, no sound of the game's), and everything is back in its place when the area loads again. The physics runs on a thread of its own at a fixed 120 Hz, not on the game's. Needs hit by touch (Strikes) on - its blades are what strikes - and the weight library (d2r_vr_weight.dll 1.3 or newer in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs); the props' catalogue is made here from your game's own files once (the status line says so). Unticked: the props stand where the game placed them.
weight.knock_strength_pct.label = Knock: the hands' strength on the weapon, %
weight.knock_strength_pct.tip = How hard the hands drive the weapon through what it meets (the weight library's 300 N and 75 N m a hand, times this). Lower: a heavy prop holds the weapon back more; higher: the weapon goes through more. Takes effect a moment later (the props' world is made anew).
weight.knock_haptic_pct.label = Knock: the pulse in the hand, %
weight.knock_haptic_pct.tip = Live. The short pulse in the hand whose weapon set a prop going (harder for a harder knock). 0: none.
weight.grab_props.label = Take the props in your hand (a test)
weight.grab_props.tip = Live. Ticked: squeeze the grip of an EMPTY hand (no weapon, shield, bow or bottle in it) firmly with the palm on or near a cup, a jar, a book, a skull, a stool... and the hand takes it at the spot under the palm (a pulse): it comes into your hand and stays there while you keep the grip squeezed - carried by your hand's strength against its weight (a stool is heavier than a cup), knocking what it meets. Let go and it flies on as your hand threw it, then rests where it lands as a knocked prop does. Pull your hand far from it (the grab's break distance, Grab bodies above) and it tears loose (not in the first 2 s). The hand closes round it with 'Grab: the hand closes round what it holds'. The grab is the VR toolkit's own, in the weight library's props world (d2r_vr_weight.dll with the hands - the log says when it has none). Only the drawing: no item, nothing of the game's changes, back in place when the area loads again. Unticked: an empty hand's grip only closes the fist, as before.

# --- The hero's strength (F4) ---
group.the_hero_s_strength_f4 = The hero's strength (F4)
group.the_hero_s_strength_f4.help = Makes a weapon feel heavier or lighter by the hero's Strength against the weapon's requirement, so a strong Barbarian swings a heavy weapon easily. The class multipliers and sliders tune how much it matters and how hard a weapon sticks.
weight.hero_strength.label = The hero's strength decides how heavy a weapon feels
weight.hero_strength.tip = Ticked: the hero's Strength (the game's stat: points, gear and all) against the weapon's own Strength requirement (the game's Weapons table) scales how heavy it feels - the steel's mass (the lag behind a swing, the sag held out, the swing's inertia) and the hands' strength (a two-hander in one hand sags and lags less in a strong hand, so the second hand is needed less). A Barbarian with plenty of Strength swings a Great Sword or a Maul easily; a Sorceress with little feels the same weapon heavy. It works with the mod's own physics and with the weight-physics library alike. Unticked: the weight is the same for every hero, as ever. The class multipliers and "Strength matters" below tune it; the log says what it did for each weapon.
weight.strength_effect.label = Strength matters, %
weight.strength_effect.tip = How much the hero's strength moves the weight. 100: twice the margin over the requirement halves the lag; 0: not at all (the same as unticked); 200: twice as much.
weight.strength_honest.label = The strength as it is (no +50 each side)
weight.strength_honest.tip = Ticked: the margin is the hero's strength (times his class' multiplier) divided by the weapon's requirement, as it is - a Barbarian with three times the requirement gets three times the margin. A weapon that asks no Strength counts as asking 10, and the steel never gets lighter than its floor, so a light weapon still weighs something. Unticked: both sides get +50 first (as before), which pulls every hero towards the middle - three times the requirement made only a little difference.
weight.two_hands_double.label = Both hands on the weapon: twice the hands' strength
weight.two_hands_double.tip = Ticked: with both hands on a weapon each hand holds it twice as strongly - a two-hander held in both hands lags and sags far less than in one. It works with the mod's own physics and with the weight-physics library alike. Unticked: the two hands share the weight as before.
weight.str_amazon.label = Amazon: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_amazon.tip = The hero's Strength stat times this is what counts: a class that is stronger than its stat says gets more, a weaker one less. Barbarian highest by default.
weight.str_assassin.label = Assassin: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_barbarian.label = Barbarian: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_druid.label = Druid: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_necromancer.label = Necromancer: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_paladin.label = Paladin: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_sorceress.label = Sorceress: strength multiplier, %
weight.str_warlock.label = Warlock: strength multiplier, %
weight.stick_by_strength.label = The class' strength decides how hard a weapon sticks
weight.stick_by_strength.tip = Live. Ticked: how hard a weapon sticks - in a wound (Stab: weapons stick into monsters) and caught between two monsters or more - goes by the class multiplier above (not the Strength stat), as much as "Strength matters" says. 100 %: as the Stab sliders set it; a Barbarian at 200 %: a tenth of that - his weapon practically never sticks and slides out of a crowd; a Paladin at 110 %: three quarters; a Sorceress at 80 %: about twice - it holds on and takes a firmer pull. It scales the stab's resistance, the pull that frees it, the tear's distance and the hold of a crowd on the weapon. A single monster's body stops and holds the weapon the same for every class (the hit and the weight are felt); whether a thrust goes in stays the same. Unticked: the same for every class.
weight.stick_pct.label = How hard a weapon sticks, %
weight.stick_pct.tip = Live. On top of the class above: 100 as the Stab sliders set it; 50 half as hard (frees with half the pull, tears free at half the distance, slides out of a crowd easier); 0 nothing sticks or holds; 200 twice as hard. The log says the factor for the hero ("sticking: x...").

# --- Taking and passing (the grip) ---
group.taking_and_passing_the_grip = Taking and passing (the grip)
group.taking_and_passing_the_grip.help = How the hands take, hold and let go of the weapon with the grips: how near the shaft a grip takes it, whether the second hand slides along a long shaft (per kind of weapon), and where the fist sits from the controller.
weight.grab_cm.label = A grip takes the weapon within, cm
weight.grab_cm.tip = A hand holds the weapon while its grip is squeezed. Squeeze it with your fist this near the shaft (between its butt and its tip) and that hand takes the weapon there. Let a grip go and that hand lets go at once - the other hand, if it holds, keeps it. Both let go, it falls to the floor; take it up there, or squeeze the grip of the hand the game holds it in, away from it, and it flies back into that fist. A new weapon sits in the game's hand until you first let that grip go. A hand with a belt potion takes nothing.
weight.let_go_cm.label = The game's hand lets go pulled away, cm
weight.let_go_cm.tip = A new weapon in the game's hand, its grip never squeezed yet, with the other hand on it too: pull the game's hand this far away from its place on the weapon and it lets go.
weight.slide_second_hand.label = The second hand slides along a long shaft
weight.slide_second_hand.tip = Two hands on a long shaft (a staff, a spear, a polearm, a two-handed sword, axe or mace): the first hand holds where it took it, and the second hand - while its grip stays squeezed - slides along the shaft with its controller, as the left hand did on a staff before. The weapon turns along the line between the hands, as ever. Off the end of the shaft, or pulled away from it, that hand lets go. Off: the second hand holds where its grip closed, on every weapon. On: it slides on the kinds of weapon ticked in the list below - a staff's, a spear's and a polearm's second hand runs along the pole, a sword's, an axe's or a maul's stays on the hilt.
weight.slide_second_hand_sword.label = Swords (two-handed)
weight.slide_second_hand_sword.tip = Ticked: with both hands on this kind of weapon the second hand slides along the shaft with its controller while its grip stays squeezed (with the grip library also loose by the trigger); off an end, or pulled away, it lets go. Unticked: the second hand holds where it closed - tight, the point and the turn fixed - and the weapon turns with the line between the hands. A staff's, a spear's and a polearm's second hand runs along the pole; a sword's, an axe's or a maul's stays on the hilt. Works with the mod's own way of holding and with the grip library alike.
weight.slide_second_hand_axe.label = Axes (two-handed)
weight.slide_second_hand_mace.label = Maces, hammers (two-handed)
weight.slide_second_hand_staff.label = Staffs
weight.slide_second_hand_polearm.label = Polearms
weight.slide_second_hand_spear.label = Spears
weight.slide_second_hand_javelin.label = Javelins
weight.slide_second_hand_other.label = Other weapons
weight.attach_apart.label = Keep the weapon's two attach bones apart (the staff is not flat)
weight.attach_apart.tip = The game lays a two-handed weapon (a staff, a spear, a polearm, a two-handed sword, axe or mace) along the line between its two attach bones - one on each wrist, both hands on the haft. A weapon with weight is drawn where the model has it, and with both bones put in ONE point that line has no length: the weapon is drawn squashed flat along its length - the staff shows as a dark disc though the grip and the red line are right. Ticked: the second attach bone is kept [hands] carry_cm (40 cm, in the ini) along the weapon's own axis from the first, as it always was for a weapon in hand, so the weapon keeps its length and lies where the model has it. Unticked: both in one point. The log says once for each weapon what the game's own two bones look like.
weight.fist_x.label = Fist's middle from the controller: X, cm
weight.fist_x.tip = Where the closed fist sits round the shaft, from the controller, along its own axes (mirrored for the left hand). Move it until a hand that takes the weapon closes round the shaft, not beside it.
weight.fist_y.label = Fist's middle from the controller: Y, cm
weight.fist_z.label = Fist's middle from the controller: Z, cm

# --- Grip fit (the hand on the shaft) ---
group.grip_fit_the_hand_on_the_shaft = Grip fit (the hand on the shaft)
group.grip_fit_the_hand_on_the_shaft.help = How a hand that takes the weapon sits on the shaft: palm on the shaft, fingers in the game's weapon-grip pose. The six sliders for each hand move and turn it from there, without moving the weapon.
weight.grip_fit.label = Lay a hand that takes the weapon on the shaft
weight.grip_fit.tip = A hand that TAKES the weapon (it closes its fist on the shaft: the second hand, a hand that takes it over from the other, the game's hand taking it up again) sits on the shaft like the base grip: the middle of its palm goes onto the shaft's axis (the red line) at the place it took it, the line through its knuckles is laid along the shaft (the roll about the shaft stays your controller's), and its fingers close round it as you squeeze the grip - also with "Free hands make a fist" off. The fist sliders above decide WHERE along the shaft the hand takes it; the sliders below move and turn each hand from there. The hand the game holds the weapon in keeps the game's own pose: only its sliders act on it. Unticked: the hands are drawn at the controllers as before. [debug] phantom_ray shows it: a yellow dot where the hand takes the shaft, a green ring where its palm really is, a white line between them.
weight.grip_fit_like_base.label = The taking hand sits on the shaft like the game's own grip
weight.grip_fit_like_base.tip = The game's own pose of the hand that holds the weapon (the base grip) is the reference: how far its palm stands from the shaft's axis (across the hand and out of the palm) and how its knuckle line leans to the shaft is measured live, and a hand that takes the weapon is given the same - so both hands sit on the staff the same way (the fingers: see the next tick). Unticked: the taking hand's palm is exactly on the axis.
weight.grip_fit_fingers.label = The taking hand's fingers take the game's weapon-grip pose
weight.grip_fit_fingers.tip = The fingers and the thumb of a hand that TAKES the weapon get the game's own weapon-grip pose - the one the hand the game holds it in has (wrapped round the shaft, the thumb on it), read off the game's animation and put on the taking hand mirrored as that hand needs. It is held as it is while the hand holds the weapon (the squeeze does not drive the fingers any more) and the fingers open as the hand lets go or hands the weapon over. Independent of "Free hands make a fist". A staff, a spear, a sword in two hands: whatever the game's hand does on that weapon. Unticked: the fingers just close with your squeeze.
weight.right_grip_x.label = Right hand X: along the shaft (+ toward the tip), cm
weight.right_grip_x.tip = Live. The RIGHT hand on the weapon, moved from where it holds the shaft in the SHAFT'S OWN FRAME, turned as the hand holds it - so a fix found for one grip is right at any roll: X along the shaft (toward the tip), Y across (toward the fingertips), Z up (out of the palm). The rotations are about the same axes: X the roll about the shaft, Y the tilt about the across axis (the fingers up / down), Z the tilt about the up axis (the fingers sideways). It acts whichever state the right hand is in: the game's hand as placed (these move it from the game's pose), or a hand that took the weapon (on top of the fit and the base grip's relation); one hand or two; carrying it or not. The weapon never moves with these - only the hand. The left hand's turns are mirrored from the right's. They work with the grip library too ("Hold the weapon the grip library's way"): the same numbers, the same frame - the moves put the hand exactly where they put ours, the turns orbit it about the shaft.
weight.right_grip_y.label = Right hand Y: across (+ toward the fingertips), cm
weight.right_grip_z.label = Right hand Z: up (+ out of the palm), cm
weight.right_grip_rx.label = Right hand rotation X: roll about the shaft, deg
weight.right_grip_ry.label = Right hand rotation Y: tilt about across, deg
weight.right_grip_rz.label = Right hand rotation Z: tilt about up, deg
weight.left_grip_x.label = Left hand X: along the shaft (+ toward the tip), cm
weight.left_grip_x.tip = Live. The same six for the LEFT hand on the weapon, in the same frame (X along the shaft toward the tip, Y across toward the fingertips, Z up out of the palm; the rotations the roll about the shaft and the two tilts). The same numbers on the two hands make mirror images. All zero: no change at all.
weight.left_grip_y.label = Left hand Y: across (+ toward the fingertips), cm
weight.left_grip_z.label = Left hand Z: up (+ out of the palm), cm
weight.left_grip_rx.label = Left hand rotation X: roll about the shaft, deg
weight.left_grip_ry.label = Left hand rotation Y: tilt about across, deg
weight.left_grip_rz.label = Left hand rotation Z: tilt about up, deg

# --- A thrown weapon ---
group.a_thrown_weapon = A thrown weapon
group.a_thrown_weapon.help = What a thrown weapon's model does after you let go with the grip throw: vanish when the game throws or fly on until it lands, and whether a potion flies all the way. Also sets how far and how far at most a throw goes.
weight.thrown_model.label = A thrown weapon's model
weight.thrown_model.tip = With the throw by the grip (Weapon Adjust > Throws): letting the grip go as a throw lets the weapon's model leave the hand and fall with the motion it had, like any weapon you drop - but it does not lie on the floor or go to the back. The game then throws a missile of its own, and a model flying on beside it is a second weapon. Vanishes: the model is gone the moment the game takes the throw (the hero goes into its throw), and a fresh one stands in the hand, drawn by the game. Flies on: the model keeps falling until it lands, the game's throw animation is over, or the time below. If the game does not take the throw (refused: no Throw skill on a pad slot, nothing to aim at), the model flies and ends as in the second choice, either way.
weight.thrown_model.choice0 = Vanishes when the game throws
weight.thrown_model.choice1 = Flies on until it lands
weight.potion_model_flies.label = Your potion flies all the way to its landing
weight.potion_model_flies.tip = A thrown POTION's model (not a javelin's, a knife's, an axe's - those follow the choice above) is not handed over to the game's own missile when the game takes the throw: it flies the whole trajectory you threw it on and breaks where it lands (it is gone, the next potion is in your hand). It is the potion you see: to hide the game's own one, which would fly beside it, tick the tick that does it ("The game's own flying potion is not drawn" on the Weapon Adjust tab). Without it the potion's model is gone the moment the game takes the throw, as a javelin's is. Live.
weight.thrown_handoff_ms.label = The model flies out of the hand this long, then hands over, ms
weight.thrown_handoff_ms.tip = With the throw by the grip: when you let the grip go as a throw the weapon's model FLIES OUT of your hand along the throw (the weight model's own flight, with the speed your hand gave it); then it hands over to the game's own missile - it vanishes, and the game's animation and missile are what continues the throw; the hand stays empty until that animation is over (the next slider). It hands over when the game's missile is up (its animation's action frame, where that is known) or this long after the release, whichever comes first. 0 (the default): at the moment the game takes the throw, with no flight to see - only the game's own missile flies, so there are never two weapons in the air (one on the weight model's trajectory, one drawn by the animation).
weight.thrown_hand_empty_ms.label = The hand stays empty while the game throws, at most, ms
weight.thrown_hand_empty_ms.tip = When the game takes a throw the model is gone at once, and the hand must stay EMPTY while the game's own throw animation plays - else the spear you threw is seen in your hand while the game's own flies. The weapon is not drawn from the moment the game takes the throw until the hero's animation is over (a moment after it), then the game's next one is in the hand. This is the longest it may stay empty: it never stays hidden if the signal is lost. 0: not hidden (the next one is drawn at once). If it was the last one, the game takes it out of the hand anyway.
weight.thrown_fly_ms.label = A thrown weapon's model flies at most, ms
weight.thrown_fly_ms.tip = How long the model of a thrown weapon may fly after the release at the most: it ends sooner when it lands (or, with Vanishes, when the game takes the throw). The game's own missile flies and hits as ever.
weight.throw_reach_pct.label = Throws: how far, % of the real throw
weight.throw_reach_pct.tip = The weight model works the throw out itself: the weapon's peak velocity of the last 0.15 s before the release - as the hand really moved it, a heavy weapon leaves slower than a light one - flown over the real ground. A real arm throws a few metres; a game screen wants tens. This scales the HORIZONTAL part of that velocity (the fall stays real), and the throws of Weapon Adjust > Throws land where it says. Light and fast goes far, heavy goes short. Lower it if a gentle swing goes too far.
weight.throw_max_cells.label = Throws: the farthest, cells
weight.throw_max_cells.tip = A throw never lands farther than this from the hero. The game's own command check refuses an aim point more than 50 cells off the hero on an axis (never bypassed), so 48 is the most; a cell is two world units, about 0.5 m at this hero's size (the log says how many metres).

# --- A dropped weapon ---
group.a_dropped_weapon = A dropped weapon
group.a_dropped_weapon.help = What happens to a weapon you let go: it lies on the floor, goes to your back or vanishes, and how you draw it back from behind a shoulder. Also the shield's and the bow's put-away, the delays, the take zone and where the weapon hangs on the back.
weight.after_drop.tip = What becomes of a weapon you let go, once it has landed. Lies on the floor: it stays where it fell, as before. Goes to the back: after the delay below it disappears from the floor and hangs on the hero's back (a staff, a spear, a polearm, a javelin or any two-handed weapon across it diagonally with the tip over the shoulder, a one-handed one low across it); it follows his body. Vanishes: after the delay it is not drawn at all. The game's weapon stays his equipped one either way; only its drawing moves. To take it back, in both: reach a hand behind either shoulder and squeeze the grip - it flies into that hand (the grip behind the shoulder is the weapon swap only while nothing is away); or squeeze the grip of a free hand anywhere else, and it flies into that hand. A weapon that is away strikes nothing.
weight.after_drop.choice0 = Lies on the floor
weight.after_drop.choice1 = Goes to the back
weight.after_drop.choice2 = Vanishes
hands.shoulder_draw.label = The shoulders hold your weapons: draw from behind a shoulder
hands.shoulder_draw.tip = A weapon you let go (or throw) lies where it fell IN THE WORLD - it does not walk with you - and the grip of EITHER hand, squeezed anywhere, calls it back into that hand while it is in the air or lies there. After the delay below it goes to the back (the choice above is not used), and from then on you reach a hand behind EITHER shoulder and squeeze the grip to DRAW it: it flies into the hand that reached - either hand does (the left hand at the right shoulder takes it into the left hand: a cross draw, for a tired arm). A short pulse in a hand that enters a shoulder where something is to draw. Behind the shoulder the grip no longer swaps weapon sets: the game's own swap stays on its key. Off: as before (the swap behind the shoulder, the choice above).
hands.shoulder_draw_stow_ms.label = Delay on the floor before it goes to the back, ms
hands.shoulder_draw_stow_ms.tip = How long a weapon you let go lies on the floor - where the grip of either hand calls it back from afar - before it goes to the back and has to be drawn from behind a shoulder. 0: at once. Live.
hands.shoulder_draw_shield.label = ... and the shield follows the sword to the other arm
hands.shoulder_draw_shield.tip = With a shield in the left hand: it stays strapped to the forearm, no grip holds it, and sword and shield are always on OPPOSITE arms: whenever the sword ends up in the hand that wears the shield - drawn into it, taken up by it, passed into it - the shield jumps to the other forearm (mirrored on the right, where it blocks and bashes (Smite) as well). A sword let go leaves it where it is. Nothing changes in the game's slots. Off: the shield stays on the left arm, and the hand that wears it cannot take the weapon. Live.
hands.shoulder_draw_shield_stow.label = ... and the shield can be put away and drawn from behind the left shoulder
hands.shoulder_draw_shield_stow.tip = A grip squeezed behind the LEFT shoulder by a hand that holds nothing PUTS THE SHIELD AWAY (it is not drawn and bashes nothing; it is still your equipped shield) - or, as with a weapon, carry it there: the hand that wears the shield holds its grip (squeezed anywhere, or held already) and LETS GO behind the left shoulder. The same grip while it is away DRAWS it onto the arm of the hand that reached - the right hand puts it on the right forearm, mirrored. Independent of the tick above: with both, a shield drawn while the sword is in the other hand sits opposite it. With this on the left shoulder is the shield's and the weapon is drawn from the right one only. A short pulse in a hand that enters the left shoulder while the shield is away. Live.
hands.shield_stow_no_block.label = ... and a shield put away does not block
hands.shield_stow_no_block.tip = While the shield is away behind the left shoulder the game rolls no block for you: it treats the hero as one with no shield and goes on to its own dodge check. Drawn onto an arm, the shield blocks as ever - the game's own chance, roll, animation and Faster Block Rate; nothing is decided by where you hold it. The shield's Defense stays (it is still equipped), and the character screen still shows its block chance. Off: a shield put away still blocks, as the game has it. Live.
hands.shoulder_draw_ranged.label = A bow or crossbow can be put away and drawn from behind a shoulder
hands.shoulder_draw_ranged.tip = A grip squeezed behind EITHER shoulder by a hand that is not holding the string (or a potion) PUTS THE BOW OR CROSSBOW AWAY (it is not drawn, no string, no aim; it is still your equipped weapon); the same grip while it is away draws it back, into its own hand. Independent of the shield ticks. A short pulse in a hand that enters a shoulder while it is away. Live.
hands.shoulder_zone_body.label = The shoulder zones fit your body (and reach to the spine)
hands.shoulder_zone_body.tip = The reach behind a shoulder - for the weapon-set swap, the weapon's draw, the shield's and the bow's put-away - scaled by your eye height (the T-pose measurement when it is used, else your height setting) and begun at the spine instead of 10 cm out: a hand reaching back over the neck lands in it. Off: the fixed reach, as before. Live.
hands.shoulder_draw_ranged_swap.label = ... and a bow is drawn into the hand that reached
hands.shoulder_draw_ranged_swap.tip = A BOW put away with one hand and drawn with the other goes into the hand that reached: a cross draw, for a tired arm. It is then held, drawn on, aimed and fed from that hand - the mirror image of the left-hand bow; the string, the quiver and the orbs go to the other hand. A crossbow always comes back into its own hand (its stock and grip are wired to the hands the game gives them). Off: a bow always comes back into the hand the settings hold it in. Live.
weight.to_back_delay_ms.label = Delay on the floor before it goes away, ms
weight.to_back_delay_ms.tip = How long a weapon that has landed lies on the floor before it goes to the back or vanishes. 0: at once.
weight.recall_any_hand.label = The grip of any free hand calls it back
weight.recall_any_hand.tip = On: squeezing the grip of an empty hand anywhere (not only behind a shoulder) calls the weapon that is away into that hand. Off: only the hand the game holds it in does, and a hand behind a shoulder takes it. A hand with a belt potion takes nothing. Note: a grip squeezed for a button chord (left grip + menu, left grip + stick click) calls it too, while it is away.
weight.back_take_cm.label = Take zone at the weapon on the back, cm
weight.back_take_cm.tip = A hand whose fist is this near the weapon where it hangs on the back - anywhere along it, not only behind a shoulder - takes it with the grip. 0: only the shoulder zone (a hand reached behind either shoulder). The weapon also hangs low across the back, below the shoulder zone: reach to where it is. The log says how far the hand was when a squeeze took nothing.
weight.take_haptic.label = A pulse in the hand at the take zone
weight.take_haptic.tip = A short pulse in a controller when its hand reaches behind a shoulder while a weapon is away, so the hand feels where to grab. Needs controller haptics on (OpenXR: Haptics).
weight.take_haptic_pct.label = Pulse strength, %
weight.back_long_x.label = Back, long weapon: right (+) / left (-), cm
weight.back_long_x.tip = Live: move it while it hangs there. Long weapons (staff, spear, polearm, javelin, two-handed) lie diagonally across the back, tip over the right shoulder. Axes of the hero's back: right, up, away from the back.
weight.back_long_y.label = Back, long weapon: up (+) / down (-), cm
weight.back_long_z.label = Back, long weapon: away from the back (+), cm
weight.back_long_pitch.label = Back, long weapon: pitch, deg
weight.back_long_pitch.tip = Turned about the hero's right axis (the tip toward the back or the front).
weight.back_long_yaw.label = Back, long weapon: yaw, deg
weight.back_long_yaw.tip = Turned about the vertical (the tip toward the left or right, back or front).
weight.back_long_roll.label = Back, long weapon: roll, deg
weight.back_long_roll.tip = Turned about the shaft itself (which side of a blade faces the back).
weight.back_short_x.label = Back, short weapon: right (+) / left (-), cm
weight.back_short_x.tip = Live: move it while it hangs there. Short weapons (sword, axe, mace, dagger, wand, scepter) lie across the lower back, tip to the hero's left.
weight.back_short_y.label = Back, short weapon: up (+) / down (-), cm
weight.back_short_z.label = Back, short weapon: away from the back (+), cm
weight.back_short_pitch.label = Back, short weapon: pitch, deg
weight.back_short_yaw.label = Back, short weapon: yaw, deg
weight.back_short_roll.label = Back, short weapon: roll, deg
