debug.phantom_ray.label = Draw the weapon's shaft (red line)
debug.phantom_ray.tip = With weight on: the red line runs along the whole shaft as the weight model holds it - where a grip can take it. The same switch as Debug's "Draw the line the left hand takes".

# --- Flail: the head on its chain (F4) ---
group.flail_the_head_on_its_chain_f4 = Flail: the head on its chain (F4)
group.flail_the_head_on_its_chain_f4.help = Lets a flail's spiked head swing free on its chain as you move the hand, and makes the ball the part that hits by touch. The sliders set the damping, the swing, the ball's weight and the bounce off a hit.
flail.chain.label = A flail's head swings free on its chain
flail.chain.tip = Flail, Knout, Scourge, Khalim's Flail and Khalim's Will: the spiked head hangs on its chain and swings as you move the hand - gravity pulls it down, a swing throws it out and it lags behind, it settles when you stop - and when the weapon hits a monster by touch the head bounces back off it. It is the game's own flail model: its chain's bones are moved, nothing is drawn over it. With hit by touch (Strikes) it is the BALL that strikes - a sphere as big as the model's head, where the chain has it, judged by the ball's own speed and way (a swung ball hits, a limp one does not); the handle strikes nothing. The attack it presses is the game's own: its reach, damage and rolls are as before. First person (F4) only. Unticked: the chain keeps the game's animation (stiff in the hand) and the touch the handle's blade, as before. Live.
flail.damping_pct.label = Flail: damping, %
flail.damping_pct.tip = Live. How fast a swing of the head dies down against the hand (the links rubbing): 100 = a free swing halves in about 2 seconds; less, it swings on longer; more, it settles quickly. 0: it never settles by itself.
flail.swing_pct.label = Flail: how much the hand swings it, %
flail.swing_pct.tip = Live. How much of the hand's motion the head feels: 100 = real, it lags and swings out as a weight on a chain does; less, it is carried along more stiffly (0: it only hangs under gravity); more, it swings out further than it would.
flail.ball_weight_pct.label = Flail: the ball's weight, %
flail.ball_weight_pct.tip = Live. How heavy the ball is against the model's own (100 = as before). Heavier: a swing carries on longer and dies down slower (the links' rubbing slows a heavy ball less), a hit by touch turns it back less - it pushes through instead of bouncing - and, with "Weapons have weight" on, the whole flail weighs more by the ball's part of it (about nine tenths of a flail is its iron ball): it lags behind the hand and sags more. Lighter: the other way. Only the look and the weight model's feel; the game's attack and damage are as before.
flail.hit_pct.label = Flail: bounce off a hit, %
flail.hit_pct.tip = Live. When the weapon hits a monster by touch (Strikes: hit by touch), the head bounces back off it: 100 = it comes back at about a third of its speed; 0 = no bounce (it swings through); 200 = it is thrown back harder. Only the look - the hit itself is the game's.

# --- Spells ---
group.spells = Spells
group.spells.help = In F4, turns off the game's auto-target for flying spells so they go where your hand or staff points. You can aim by the drawn hand or staff, and let an upright staff aim along the arm; the blocks below keep auto-target for single spells.
hands.spell_aim.label = Disable auto-target for spells
hands.spell_aim.tip = On: a spell that flies - Fire Bolt, Charged Bolt, Teeth, Frozen Orb, Bone Spear... (as the game's own skill table says) - aims along the hand as every attack does here, and the game's auto-target and aim assist are off for that cast: it no longer turns to a monster. F4 only: in F1, F2, F3 and the flat modes the game's auto-target works as always. Spells placed on the ground (Blizzard, Fissure, Meteor), summons, curses and auras keep the game's targeting. Off: casting as before, with the game's auto-target. Below, a tick keeps the game's auto-target for that one spell - one that seeks its target itself, as Chain Lightning.
hands.spell_aim_model.label = Aim spells by the drawn hand or staff
hands.spell_aim_model.tip = VR first person (F4) only. On: the line a spell goes along comes from the hero as he is drawn, with no correction: a staff, wand or orb in hand aims along itself, toward its head (with the weapon's weight on: along the shaft as your grip holds it); with none, along the hand's fingers - or out of the palm when the fingers point up or down. A staff held upright aims with its hand. The attack along the hand ([bow] mode 4) goes the same way. A bow, crossbow, javelin or throwing weapon keeps its own line. The game's own cast - skill, mana, missile - is not changed, only where it is aimed. Off, or no fresh pose: the controller's line and the aim correction sliders (Weapon Adjust), as before. After d2r-pcvr (bearstonem, MIT). Debug > Aim rays: "Spell's ray" shows it.
hands.staff_upright_arm.label = A staff held upright aims along the arm
hands.staff_upright_arm.tip = VR first person (F4), with "Aim spells by the drawn hand or staff" above. A spell lands on a point on the ground, so only the line's heading counts - and a staff held upright has almost none: its heading is a few degrees of tilt and the hand's wobble. On: near upright the ARM aims, from your drawn shoulder through your hand; as you tilt the staff away from upright its own axis takes over, smoothly. So a staff tipped toward a side sends the spell that way, and an upright one goes where your arm points. A wand or orb aims as before. It only chooses where the game's own spell is aimed, as a click would. Off: the staff's own line, as before. Debug > Aim rays: "Spell's ray" draws the arm in light blue, and the ray turns from green to blue by how much the arm leads. After d2r-pcvr (bearstonem, MIT). Live.
hands.staff_upright_full_deg.label = Arm aims alone within, ° off upright
hands.staff_upright_full_deg.tip = Held within this many degrees of upright, the staff's spell goes along the arm alone. Live.
hands.staff_upright_none_deg.label = Staff aims alone from, ° off upright
hands.staff_upright_none_deg.tip = Tilted this many degrees or more from upright, the staff aims along itself alone; between the two, a smooth blend. Smaller = the staff's tilt takes over sooner. Live.

# ===== Tab: Multiplayer =====

# --- The other players (a TCP/IP game - they need this build too) ---
group.the_other_players_a_tcp_ip_game_they_need_this_build_too = The other players (a TCP/IP game - they need this build too)
multiplayer.pose_share.label = Share my head, hands and weapon with the other players (read at the game's start)
multiplayer.pose_share.tip = While you play VR first person (F4) your head, both controllers and your weapon go to the host and from it to the other players - about 100 bytes 30 times a second, through D2RLoader's own plugin network (the players connect to the host as for the game; nothing goes through any other server) - and theirs come to you, VR or flat. The boxes below say what is done with them. Visual only: nothing in the game or its packets changes. Read at the game's start: restart the game after changing it.
multiplayer.pose_share_bodies.label = The other players are solid for my weapon (and can be grabbed)
multiplayer.pose_share_bodies.tip = The other players are bodies for your weapon, as monsters are - their own skeletons' limbs: your weapon stops on them and on the weapon they hold, steel on steel plays the game's block sound with a pulse in the hand, and with "grab bodies" your hand takes hold of them. Only your drawn weapon is moved: nobody is hit, nothing in the game changes. Live. F4 only.
multiplayer.pose_share_hero.label = Their heroes move as they do (head, arms, weapon)
multiplayer.pose_share_hero.tip = The other VR players' hero models are posed from what their headsets and controllers send: the head as they hold it, the arms on their controllers, the weapon in hand as they draw it (it falls from the hand when they let go), their body turned to where they look - instead of the game's own animation. In any view, F4 or flat. Only the drawn bones of their models change. Live.
multiplayer.pose_share_legs.label = Their legs step the way they move
multiplayer.pose_share_legs.tip = With the box above: their legs step along their travel - forward, backward, sideways - while their pelvis faces where they look, the game's own walk within "the game's own walk within +- this" (Body) of it. The feet stay planted while they bear the body; the knees bend only forward. Needs the gait library d2r_vr_gait.dll in d2rloader\d2r_vr_libs (else the game's own walk). Any view. Live.
multiplayer.pose_share_held.label = See what their hands hold (potions, items, props) and what they throw
multiplayer.pose_share_held.tip = What your hands have goes to the others with your pose, and theirs is drawn for you: a belt potion in the hand, let fall or emptied, an item taken off the ground, a prop of the level - a jar, a book, a cup - in the hand, flying as it was thrown, and where it came to rest. Their potions and items are copies of the game's own models; their props are the level's own, moved where they have them (with "knock props", near you, in F4). Visual only: the potion's use, the items and the props stay each game's own. Live.

# ===== Tab: Debug =====
tab.debug = Debug

# --- Debug ---
group.debug.help = Switches for testers and for finding problems: extra log lines, GPU replay modes, the multiplayer heads-and-hands probe, frame and stutter traces, and reports on why the graphics device was lost. Leave them off for normal play unless asked to send a log.
debug.belt_bottle_trace.label = Belt bottles: a log line for every step of an emptied or dropped bottle
debug.belt_bottle_trace.tip = With "the drunk bottle stays in the hand" or "thrown on the ground, the game drops it" on: the log gets a line when a drink leaves an empty bottle (or not), when it leaves the hand (how fast), comes to rest and goes, and which of the model's meshes were hidden. The drops themselves are always logged. The log only. Live.
debug.knock_props_trace.label = Knocked props: a log line for every knock and every scan
debug.knock_props_trace.tip = With Weapon Weight's "Cups, plates, vases... are knocked about by your weapon" on: the log gets a line for every prop your weapon or fist sets going (its kind, which hand, how fast the blade was, how hard the prop was struck) and for every scan of the props near you (how many, how many of the catalogue's near, how many stand on the floor, on another prop, on furniture, on a guessed ledge, and the scan's cost). The log only - nothing of the knocking changes. Live.
debug.knock_props_glow.label = Knocked props: light the props that are found
debug.knock_props_glow.tip = With Weapon Weight's "Cups, plates, vases... are knocked about by your weapon" on: every prop near you (within 3 m) that the catalogue knows - the ones your weapon or your fist can knock about - is drawn brighter, with the game's own highlight (as an item under the pointer is). To see which of a place's props are found and which are not. Only the drawing. Live.
debug.replay_marks.label = Replay: how the right eye's lists go to the GPU
debug.replay_marks.tip = Stereo from one pass: how the game's replayed command lists are sent to the GPU for the right eye. 1 (the default): each list on its own with a signal after it, so a hang's log names the list the GPU stopped at; every pair ~35 separate submissions (~0.4 ms of the game's thread). 0: each queue's run of lists in one submission - on 2026-10-18 the graphics queue then ran a list that never ended, 30 s to 3 min in. 2: each list on its own without the signals. 3: the same lists in the same calls as the game made them, no marks - the game's own number of submissions (the first time, restart the game). 4: that with a signal after each call. Live.
debug.replay_marks.choice0 = 0 - one batch a queue (hung, test-60..62)
debug.replay_marks.choice1 = 1 - each list with a GPU mark (safe, default)
debug.replay_marks.choice2 = 2 - each list, no marks
debug.replay_marks.choice3 = 3 - in the game's own calls
debug.replay_marks.choice4 = 4 - the game's calls, a mark after each
debug.settings_two_grip_chord.label = Old way into the headset settings: both grips + a stick click
debug.settings_two_grip_chord.tip = The settings in the headset open with a long press of the right stick click. Ticked, the old way works too: squeeze both grips for a third of a second, then click a thumbstick - and from the moment both grips are down the stick clicks are the settings', not the game's. A two-hander is held by both grips, so that took the stick clicks in a fight: off by default, two grips held mean nothing. Live. F4 only.
debug.ui_trace.label = Ctrl+F10 frame trace (slows every frame; restart the game)
debug.ui_trace.tip = Ctrl+F10 writes one frame of the game's render targets and draws to d2r_vr_uitrace.txt. For that the plugin watches every draw the game makes - ReShade then calls it thousands of times a frame, and looks up every constant buffer the game binds: mono ran ~5-8% slower. Off (the default): Ctrl+F10 does nothing. Read at the game's start.
debug.pose_share_hz.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: poses a second
debug.pose_share_hz.tip = How often your pose goes to the host, and how often the host sends each player the others'. More is smoother and costs more of D2RLoader's message allowance (its RateLimited answers are counted in the log). Live.
debug.pose_share_delay_ms.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: played back behind, ms
debug.pose_share_delay_ms.tip = The others' poses are played back this much behind the newest one that came, blended between the two either side, so the markers move smoothly over the network's jitter. Less: closer to now, jerkier. Live.
debug.pose_share_echo.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: the host sends you your own (one-PC test)
debug.pose_share_echo.tip = As the host (a single-player game is its own host): your own pose comes back to you through the whole path, so the markers sit on your own head and hands, late by the trip. To test it on one PC. Live.
debug.pose_share_burst.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: measure the message limit once
debug.pose_share_burst.tip = Once a connection is up: up to 400 messages back to back to the host (and the host to each new player), until D2RLoader answers RateLimited; the log says how many went out, how fast, and how many arrived at the other end. Live.
debug.pose_share_echo_ahead_cm.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: your echo stands ahead of you, cm (0 = on you)
debug.pose_share_echo_ahead_cm.tip = With "the host sends you your own" (one PC): your own pose comes back and stands this far ahead of you, turned to face you - a second player to wave at and to cross weapons with (its body and weapon are met with the box above). 0: the echo sits on your own hands, drawn only. Live.
debug.pose_share_draw.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: draw the other players as debug glass
debug.pose_share_draw.tip = The other players drawn as see-through debug shapes in our camera's views: a blue ball on the head, green balls and lines on the controllers, and with "bodies and weapons too" grey bodies and amber weapons. Off (the default): nothing of it is drawn - your weapon still meets their bodies and weapons as before. Live.
debug.pose_share_legs_self.label = Multiplayer heads and hands: your own hero's legs by the same gait (a test)
debug.pose_share_legs_self.tip = Your own hero's legs step by the same gait as the other players' heroes ("their legs step the way they move"), his own facing - to see the legs on one PC: look at him in F2 or F3 (flat or VR) and walk forward, back and sideways. The log says every 5 s what they did ("legs: ..."). Needs the gait library. Live.
debug.walk_back_dump.label = Walking backwards: write the legs to a file
debug.walk_back_dump.tip = While the hero moves, his legs are kept pose by pose - as the game drew them and as drawn with "Walking backwards, the legs step backwards" - and the last 6 seconds of each walk back (and of 3 s standing with the camera turned round him) go to d2rloader\logs\d2r_vr_walkback.txt (at most 30 a session), for the walk_legs tool that draws them as stick figures. The log also says every 5 s which pose the hero's meshes are skinned from (the one we pose, or another). Writes a file and log lines only; nothing in the game changes. Live.
debug.phantom_ray.label#2 = Draw the line the left hand takes
debug.phantom_ray.tip#2 = A red line along which the left hand takes the weapon in hand and slides (staff, spear, polearm, two-handed sword); with a crossbow also where the bolt flies (Crossbow: shot line sliders turn it). "Draw the axes of the weapon in hand" draws it too.
debug.xbow_barrel_line.label = Crossbow: draw the barrel as modelled
debug.xbow_barrel_line.tip = In VR F4 with a crossbow held the gun's way: a cyan line along the crossbow's barrel as the model has it (its bolt helper, 40 cm back and 30 cm ahead of the front of the stock) and a magenta ball where "left palm under the drawn barrel" puts the palm. Cyan = as the renderer draws the crossbow; orange = the renderer's placing is not seen yet (the hand then stays on the shot line). Every 3 s the log gives the points ("crossbow barrel"). And where the shot goes, live: a ray from the muzzle - green along the drawn barrel ("shoot along the drawn barrel"), orange along the shot line (unticked, or the barrel not read) - to the floor (a full ball) or 8 m out (a ring); the game aims by its heading. With "Draw the line the left hand takes" the red shot line is drawn too: if the two lie together, the shot line sliders already match the model. Needs the shader D2R_DepthFog.fx of the same build. Live.
debug.bone_axes.label = Draw the axes of the weapon in hand
debug.bone_axes.tip = The bone the game hangs the weapon in hand on: its own axes from its origin, 0.5 m each - X green, Y blue, Z yellow; and the red line the left hand takes it by. Weapon Adjust's "Turn about X / Y / Z" turn the weapon about these.
debug.bow_vectors.label = Draw the bow draw's vectors
debug.bow_vectors.tip = Native OpenXR, "Bow: draw the string with both hands" on. In the headset: the bow's axis (cyan), the touch sphere round the string (green with the free hand inside, red outside, deeper once the string is taken), the hands (white = bow, yellow = free), the fixed point 16 cm behind the grip (small cyan), the bow's own string (small magenta), the pull line (orange) and the draw's aim (blue); and a line of numbers in the log five times a second. Needs the shader D2R_DepthFog.fx of the same build. Live.
debug.walk_start_log.label = Log each walk start of BodyWalk's: stick, dead zone, the game's walk, the hero
debug.walk_start_log.tip = One line in the log ("walk start (BodyWalk): ...") each time BodyWalk's stick leaves rest after half a second of standing: the time it left rest, then the milliseconds to it passing the game's dead zone on its own, the game's walk being given a vector (earlier with "BodyWalk's walk starts from"), and the hero's position moving. BodyWalk's own half is its Debug tab's "Walk Start Timing" ("STEP START: first step ..."), on the same clock. Read only: nothing is changed in the game. Live.
debug.bow_latency.label = Log where the time goes between a release and its arrow / thrown missile
debug.bow_latency.tip = Native OpenXR, "Bow: draw the string with both hands" or a throw gesture on. One line in the log for every bow shot and every throw: the milliseconds after the release to the gesture's press, the pad's button reaching the game, the hero's attack or throw mode, the body's turn toward the aim, the animation row the action runs on (name, frames, the action frame), the game's own missile being created (read only: the game's missile create is watched, nothing is changed) and the client showing a missile. Nothing is drawn and nothing is changed in the game. Live.
debug.shot_trace.label = Log what the game does with each attack of ours
debug.shot_trace.tip = On: for every attack the plugin presses (a bow's shot, a blow, a throw), from its press until 1.5 s after it, the log tells every map click (with the Stand Still and Run flags it carries), the command the game's click builds from it, and every command through the game's funnel with its way back up the stack. To find out why the game sometimes runs the hero off after a shot. Read only. Needs "attack in place" on. Live.
debug.game_sky_test.label = The game's sky: another model for the dome (a test)
debug.game_sky_test.tip = With "The game draws the sky" on: our dome in one bright magenta instead of the sky's picture, or the game's own Arreat Summit sky model placed the same way - seen, the game draws it; not seen, it does not (the log's "game sky" lines count its draws and say whether its model loaded). Needs the test files in the mod's data folder. Live.
debug.game_sky_test.choice1 = Our dome in one bright magenta
debug.game_sky_test.choice2 = The game's own Arreat Summit sky model
debug.game_sky_test.choice3 = The Summit's unit naming our magenta model
debug.game_sky_test.choice4 = Our magenta model at the Summit's own path
debug.frame_log.label = Log every frame
debug.frame_log.tip = Every pair, view, hero pose and present to d2r_vr_frames.csv beside the ini, and FlatVR its per-frame pose trace.
debug.frame_trace.label = Log the long frames and what the plugin spent in them
debug.frame_trace.tip = For a stutter that comes with a swing or a hit. A pair (both eyes of one game frame) longer than "Frame trace: long over" is told in the log (d2r-vr-vrcam.log), the worst one of each second: where its time went (the game's own frame, the runtime's wait, the left and the right pass, the draw thread's real work against its waiting), what the plugin itself spent in it (the pose of every skeleton, the hit observer, the aim hooks, the server's lookups, the 100 ms probe of Hit by touch, the haptic call, the log lines), the situation it fell in (standing, walking, a swing, a hit landed) and the access violations caught. Every 10 s one line counts how many pairs were long in each situation - send that log in. It only measures and writes lines; it changes nothing in play. Costs a clock read or two in each hook while it is on. Live.
debug.frame_trace_ms.label = Frame trace: long over, ms
debug.frame_trace_ms.tip = A pair longer than this is a long one for "Log the long frames and what the plugin spent in them". 15 ms is a little over one frame at 72 Hz (13.9 ms); at 90 Hz (11.1 ms) 15 catches every missed frame. Raise it if the game runs at 40-50 frames a second anyway (a mean pair of 20 ms), so that only the real stutters are told. Live.
debug.roomscale_log.label = Log the room-scale walk once a second
debug.roomscale_log.tip = With "Room-scale walking" on (Stereo > Native OpenXR): a line a second in the log while it is live - how far your head is off the hero's place, the stick it gives the game, walking yes / no, blocked yes / no (at the limit: the room slides), your head's and the hero's speed, whether the controller's stick is held and which pad the game reads. Changes nothing in play. Live.
debug.log_async.label = Write the plugin's log from a thread of its own
debug.log_async.tip = For a stutter that comes with a swing or a hit. Every press writes a handful of lines to the log (the pad poll alone: seven), and a second of swinging 20 to 50, each written by the game's own thread in the middle of a frame - about a millisecond a line on the machine this was found on, more where the log's file is slow (an antivirus, a disk that waits). On: the line is copied into a ring and a thread of its own writes it, in order, so the game's thread does not wait. Every line is kept; a line that waited more than 50 ms says so at its end (the log stamps the time it is WRITTEN); what waits is written at a crash and at unload. It changes nothing in play. Off: each thread writes its own lines, as always. Live.
debug.log_async_auto.label = Write the log from a thread of its own where it is slow
debug.log_async_auto.tip = With the one above off, every log line's write is timed. Where the log's file is slow on this PC - 8 of the last 16 lines took 5 ms or more (an antivirus, a slow disk; a player's log had 29 ms a line, and every Frozen Orb cast stopped the game ~330 ms for its eleven lines) - the lines go to that thread for the rest of the run, and the log says so once. At about 1 ms a line nothing changes. Off: the log's speed is not looked at, as before. Live.
debug.dred.label = Say why the GPU's device was lost (DRED)
debug.dred.tip = The game ends - after a failed check in its own DX12 code, a moment before the headset's runtime logs "HRESULT failure [887a0005]" - when the graphics device is removed (a GPU hang, a page fault, a driver reset). On: Windows' DRED is asked for before the game makes its device, and the moment the device goes the log (d2r-vr-vrcam.log) and d2rloader\logs\d2r_vr_gpu_fault.txt say why: the reason, what each command list had done when the GPU stopped, the address of a page fault and what was allocated or freed there, and the plugin's own last events that touch the GPU's memory. Send that file in. It costs the runtime a marker between commands. Needs a game restart. Off: the device loss is still told, with its reason only.
debug.d3d12_validation.label = D3D12 debug layer: errors in the log (slow)
debug.d3d12_validation.tip = To find what takes the graphics device down. Needs Windows' optional feature Graphics Tools. On: before the game makes its device the D3D12 debug layer is switched on, and its errors and warnings go to the log (d2r-vr-vrcam.log) in its own words - a barrier that names the wrong state, a copy past the end of a buffer, a resource released while a list that names it has not run. The game runs much slower: for a test, not for play. Needs a game restart. (d2r_vr.ini: 2 also checks every shader access on the GPU, ten times slower again - for a flat repro only.)
debug.stall_guard.label = Free a GPU queue that stands still for good
debug.stall_guard.tip = Two hangs left the game's graphics queue standing for good - no device removal, the game alive and frozen, its drawing thread inside ReShade's flush. On: while the queue has not moved for a quarter of a second the plugin's optional work that would wait on it (the copy to the headset, an eye's ReShade effects, a depth copy) is not started; after eight seconds with the picture stopped, the plugin signals its own cross-queue fences from the CPU, and says each in the log ("stall guard"). A queue that runs a command list which never ends is not freed by this: see the next switch. Needs a game restart. Off: as before. (d2r_vr.ini: stall_skip_ms, stall_unstick_ms; stall_unstick_game also signals the game's own fences.)
debug.stall_remove.label = Hang report: take the device away after 20 s of a hung queue
debug.stall_remove.tip = For the graphics queue that stands for good (see "Free a GPU queue..."; needs that on). Switched on: after 20 s with the picture stopped and the queue still, the plugin takes the graphics device away on purpose, so that Windows' DRED ("Say why the GPU's device was lost" - on) writes into d2rloader\logs\d2r_vr_gpu_fault.txt which command list the queue was in. The game ends, as after a driver reset - for a test of the hang, not for play. Needs a game restart.
debug.matrix_writer.label = Find who writes the hero matrix
debug.matrix_writer.tip = Switched on: for 3 s, while walking, marks where the game writes the hero's model matrix (d2r_vr_matrix_writers.csv beside the ini, a summary in the log). Turn it off and on again for another run.

# --- Logs and one-shot captures (d2r_vr.ini [debug]) ---
group.logs_and_one_shot_captures_d2r_vr_ini_debug = Logs and one-shot captures (d2r_vr.ini [debug])
group.logs_and_one_shot_captures_d2r_vr_ini_debug.help = Log lines and one-time captures for finding problems: controller presses, what the game does after a throw, the flat view's monster picking, compute shaders and a draw-thread profile. They only write to the log.
debug.input_log.label = Log the controller presses
debug.input_log.tip = Each press of a controller button, with where it came from (BodyWalk, the pad, a gesture). About 1 ms per line on the draw thread. Live.
debug.input_log.choice1 = The first 400
debug.input_log.choice2 = All of them
debug.throw_trace.label = Log what the game does after each throw
debug.throw_trace.tip = For 5 s after every released throw (by gesture or by grip): the hero's throw animation, the missile (made? how far, its life, when it is gone) and the explosion's missile. Read only; about 20 lines a throw. Live.
debug.flat_pick.label = Log the flat view's monster picking
debug.flat_pick.tip = For "monsters cannot be targeted after a while" (docs/notes/flat_targeting.md): what the game's pick asks for and why it stops. At most 4 lines a second. Live.
debug.log_compute_shaders.label = Log the game's compute shaders at the start
debug.log_compute_shaders.tip = One line for each compute shader the game makes (size and hash), to check that the light-bounds fix matches this game build. Restart the game.
debug.profile_draw.label = Profile the draw thread for 5 s (turn on for each run)
debug.profile_draw.tip = Each time this turns on: one 5 s profile of the game's draw thread, in the log. Turn it off and on again for another.
debug.find_prev_matrix.label = Look for the previous frame's camera matrix
debug.find_prev_matrix.tip = A developer's search for the motion vectors' matrix, in the log. Live.

# --- GPU and stereo replay (developer) ---

group.gpu_and_stereo_replay_developer.help = Developer switches for the right eye's stereo replay, the stall guard and the fog in the frame's edges: traces, comparisons and timings. Most need a game restart; not for play.
debug.replay_proto.label = Stereo replay hooks (needed by Stereo's right-eye replay)
debug.replay_proto.tip = On by default: the hooks the right eye's replay and the stall guard ride on. Off only to rule them out. Restart the game.
debug.replay_trace.label = Replay: record the queue's signals and waits
debug.replay_trace.tip = Arms the trace below. Restart the game.
debug.replay_trace_go.label = Replay: write one trace now (turn on for each)
debug.replay_trace_go.tip = With the one above armed: one trace into the log each time this turns on.
debug.replay_peek_go.label = Replay: compare one pair's two pictures (turn on for each)
debug.replay_peek_go.tip = One pair of eyes compared, in the log, each time this turns on.
debug.replay_scan_go.label = Replay: find the left camera's copies (turn on for each)
debug.replay_scan_go.tip = A scan of upload memory for the left camera, in the log, each time this turns on.
debug.cb_compare.label = Compare the eyes' constant buffers
debug.cb_compare.tip = Arms the comparison below. Restart the game.
debug.cb_compare_go.label = Compare the eyes' constant buffers now (turn on for each)
debug.cb_compare_go.tip = With the one above armed: one comparison into the log each time this turns on.
debug.fog_in_frame_paint.label = Fog in the frame's edges: paint what it does

debug.stall_unstick_game.label = Stall guard: also signal the game's own fences
debug.stall_unstick_game.tip = With "Free a GPU queue that stands still": the game's own fences a queue waits for are signalled too. For a lost wake-up only. Restart the game.
debug.stall_skip_ms.label = Stall guard: the queue still this long before our work is skipped, ms
debug.stall_skip_ms.tip = Restart the game.
debug.stall_unstick_ms.label = Stall guard: the picture stopped this long before fences are signalled, ms
debug.stall_remove_ms.label = Hang report: take the device away after this long, ms (0 = never)
debug.stall_remove_ms.tip = For a test of a hang, not for play: the game ends, DRED writes where each queue stood. Restart the game.

# --- Weapon, bodies and checks (also on their own tabs) ---
group.weapon_bodies_and_checks_also_on_their_own_tabs = Weapon, bodies and checks (also on their own tabs)
group.weapon_bodies_and_checks_also_on_their_own_tabs.help = Debug ticks for weapons, bodies and checks, some also found on their own tabs: thrust and stab plates, sound names and strike force in the log, checks without the hostile test, and a few drawing checks.
debug.thrust_debug.tip#2 = As on Strikes > Thrusts: the plate over the weapon hand and the blade tinted BLUE (counted) or ORANGE (refused) after each thrust. Live.
debug.thrust_debug_only.tip#2 = As on Strikes > Thrusts: with the thrust debug on, only the thrusts are shown and tinted. Live.
debug.stab_debug.tip#2 = As on Strikes: the last stab's plate and its marks on the bodies. Switches the capsules on too. Live.
debug.sound_trace.label = Name the game's sounds in the log
debug.sound_trace.tip = Live. Each of the game's sounds is told by name the first time the game makes it, and each time it plays (at most once in 2 s a name): to find the game's own shield-hit sound for the monsters' shields. Only reads - every sound plays as ever. Off: nothing told.
debug.strike_force_debug.label = Tell every strike judged by force in the log
debug.strike_force_debug.tip = With 'Hit by the strike's force' on: every strike it judges gets a line - counted (its N s and the threshold) or not (why). Off: the first twelve refusals and forty presses.
debug.strike_measure.label = Measure each strike's force into the log
debug.strike_measure.tip = With the monsters' bodies on (F4): each strike on a body - from the first touch to when the weapon leaves it - gets one line in the log ("strike measure: ..."): the ARRIVAL (the weapon's momentum as it met the body, N s, and its speed), the DRIVE (your hands pressing it on, N s), the stab's push while it is in, the total and the total in the first 0.15 s, the CUT (the body's push times the slide along it, J) and the cm slid, the peak force, how many hands held it. For setting the strength a hit needs: record a light tap, a hard blow with two hands, a slide along the body, a drop - and send the log. Nothing changes in play. Off by default. Live.
debug.melee_touch_unchecked.label = Hit by touch: no hostile / wall check (not for play)
debug.melee_touch_unchecked.tip = Any live monster the blade meets is attacked - to find out whether that check is what stops a touch. An ally or a monster behind a wall is attacked too. Live.
debug.melee_press_trace.label = Log every press of Hit by touch in full
debug.melee_press_trace.tip = Off: only the first 12 presses are told in full. Live.
debug.monster_rig_dump.label = Log the next monster model's limbs once
debug.monster_rig_dump.tip = Every read of its meshes and bones, for checking the game's mesh layout. Live.
debug.doll_trace.label = Log each time the body lets go of the arms
debug.doll_trace.tip = The hero's facing or rig that failed, and when it is taken again. Live.
debug.shield_blink.label#2 = Blink the strapped shield (a check)
debug.shield_blink.tip#2 = As on Weapon Adjust > Shield: the shield's bone hidden half a second in every two. Live.
debug.hide_strip_tint.label#2 = Show the toolbar's cut strip (magenta veil)
debug.hide_strip_tint.tip#2 = As on UI: F4 body: the strip the toolbar's cut empties painted see-through magenta. Live.
debug.bow_rig_grip.label = Bow: the grip draws the string (before the gesture)
debug.bow_rig_grip.tip = The posing of the draw tried with a plain grip squeeze. Live.
debug.hand_vitals_flip.label = Hand vitals: the palm's side the other way
debug.hand_vitals_flip.tip = For a runtime whose grip pose has its X axis the other way round. Live.
debug.wrist_status_flip.label = Wrist status: the back of the hand the other way
debug.mob_bars_style.label = Ordinary monsters' bars: how the plate is taken off
debug.mob_bars_style.tip = With UI: F4 body's ordinary monster bars. Live.
debug.mob_bars_style.choice0 = Answered far off the screen
debug.mob_bars_style.choice1 = Answered not on the screen (d2r-pcvr's)

# --- Aim rays ---
group.aim_rays = Aim rays
group.aim_rays.help = Draws where a spell or an arrow will go as a ray in the headset, and logs what each bow shot meets and how the arrows we draw fly. For checking the aim; nothing in the game changes.
debug.spell_aim_ray.label = Spell's ray
debug.spell_aim_ray.tip = VR first person (F4), no bow, crossbow or thrown weapon in hand: where a spell goes, live - a ray from where its aim starts (the staff, wand or orb, or the palm), along the direction the aim uses, to the floor (a full ball) or 8 m out (a ring). Green: from the model (Auto-target: "Aim spells by the drawn hand or staff") - it should lie along the staff, wand or orb, or along the hand's fingers. Orange: the old line (the controller and the aim correction sliders) - unticked, or no fresh pose. The game aims by its heading on the ground. Needs the shader D2R_DepthFog.fx of the same build. Live.
debug.bow_aim_ray.label = Bow: draw where the arrow goes (a ray from the bow)
debug.bow_aim_ray.tip = Native OpenXR, "Bow: draw the string with both hands" on, a bow in hand (first person, F4). While the string is drawn - and for a moment after the shot - a long ray in the headset: from the arrow's release point (the bow model's own arrow rest point when it is read, else the bow hand's point) along the line the bow code shoots along (the string hand through that point; the game itself takes only its heading on the ground), to where it meets the floor (a full ball) or 8 m out (a ring). Green = the line goes through the bow model's arrow rest point ("The shot goes through the arrow's rest point too" on); orange = the plain hand-set line (no rest point read, or that setting off). With "Bow and crossbow: aim up and down" on the ray ends on what the shot goes to: a monster's body (a red ball) or the ground as known from where things stand. Nothing is changed in the game. Needs the shader D2R_DepthFog.fx of the same build. Live.
debug.bow_pitch_trace.label = Bow: log what each shot's line meets (aim up and down)
debug.bow_pitch_trace.tip = With "Bow and crossbow: aim up and down" on: one line in the log for every shot of the bow draw (twice a second while a crossbow or a bow is aimed by the hand) - what the line met (a monster: a limb of its own skeleton or the game's capsule; the ground; nothing), how far along it and how far up or down against your ground, the heading the shot was given against the line's own, and what the scene was made of (the monsters near, the hostile ones, their models matched by the ground's shear and how well). Read only. Live.
debug.arrow_flight_trace.label = Bow: log the arrows drawn by us (the arrow's flight)
debug.arrow_flight_trace.tip = With "Bow: draw the shot arrow ourselves" on: log lines for every shot arrow we draw - the shot (what its line met), each of the arrow's entities (with an effect or not), its first frame (where the game's arrow began, its matrix's scale and axes), and its end (frames, how it flew). Read only. Live.
debug.arrow_flight_fx_off.label = Bow: the arrows drawn by us without their effects (a test)
debug.arrow_flight_fx_off.tip = With "Bow: draw the shot arrow ourselves" on: an elemental arrow's own effect (fire, frost, sparks) is switched off by the game's own switch while we draw the arrow - in case the game's effect stays on the game's path instead of following ours. The hits' explosions are not touched. Live.

status.frame_cap_why.3 = one picture a frame (mono, the 3D from the depth): a game frame a headset frame
status.frame_cap_why.4 = FlatVR's own frames start each game frame ([flatvr] frame_sync): the cap only stops a game running away

remap.tip = What this does, from the list; it is written to d2r_vr.ini, section [direct], as "{key} = ...". The standard choice is not written at all (the line goes), so a new default still reaches you; "Nothing" is written as none. "Custom" is a line you wrote by hand that this list has no name for (two outputs, a key command not in the list): it is left as it is until you pick something here. A pad button (Gamepad B, X, Y, RB...) is the game's own skill button; "Pause menu (Esc)" taps the keyboard's Esc for the game. Live. Works in F4 and, for the controllers in F1 - F3 without BodyWalk, there too (the pause menu and the skill panel are F4's).
status.xr_layers.off = OpenXR layer {layers} turned off for D2R VR: it is known to distort this game's picture (in the game's process only - other apps keep it). "Each eye exactly as the headset gives it" draws as other games do and keeps it; or untick "Turn off OpenXR layers known to break the picture".
status.xr_layers.listed_in_runtime_fov = OpenXR layer {layers} loads with the game, left in: the eyes are drawn exactly as the headset gives them, as other games draw, so it should do no harm.
status.xr_layers.listed_in = OpenXR layer {layers} loads with the game: it is known to distort its picture (cross-eyed, stretched) when the eyes are drawn the mod's own way - tick "Each eye exactly as the headset gives it".
status.xr_layers.in = Other OpenXR layers in the game (left as they are): {layers}.

strikes.row_tip = {kind}: {what}
strikes.tip.row = one row of numbers for this kind alone. 0 in a number box = follow the general one.
strikes.tip.amp_x = the least swing amplitude, x the piercing weapons'. 0 (or under 0.25) = follow the family this kind belongs to: {family}. Live.
strikes.tip.cm = the least swing amplitude in cm: the piercing weapons' cm times this row's factor (or its family's).
strikes.tip.min_speed = the least blade speed, m/s, for a contact to count. 0 (or under 0.3) = the general one. Only decides whether a contact counts; the game's damage is the game's. Live.
strikes.tip.stroke_start = how far the blade moves to start a stroke, cm. A longer one refuses short fake swings for this kind. 0 (or under 2) = the general one. Live.
strikes.tip.toward = a contact must be toward the monster (the rule above) to count. Unticked: it counts whichever way the blade moves. Live.
strikes.tip.head_only = only the head of the weapon strikes (the outer part of the blade); a touch with the shaft or the handle is refused. Live.
thrusts.tip.row = this kind's thrusts alone. 0 in a number box = follow the general one.
thrusts.tip.on = ticked: this kind thrusts (a poke along the blade counts). Live.
thrusts.tip.min_speed = the least speed of a thrust, m/s. 0 (or under 0.3) = the general one. Live.
thrusts.tip.cm = how far the point goes forward along the blade, cm. 0 (or under 1) = the general one. Live.
thrusts.tip.min_accel = the least peak acceleration of a thrust, m/s² (a jab, not a push). 0 = the general one. Live.
